mr president, we are all concerned at the moment with strengthening our industrial fabric, both to keep businesses in business and to develop new stable jobs in europe. it is therefore important to have european-level tools to minimise the negative impacts of restructuring on the industrial fabric and thus on employment, but also to prepare for the future of our industry. that is why we must support initiatives such as those of our rapporteur and, in particular, give the social dialogue its rightful place in anticipation of restructuring. it is through this concertation that enterprises and sectors will be able to anticipate and adapt to changes in industrial structure in the future. but beyond this recommendation for legislation, which i hope the commission will accept, in the same spirit of fighting restructuring, the union must also support effective and well-equipped european budgetary instruments to support restructuring, such as the esf or the globalisation adjustment fund, which could be given an anticipatory aspect to support restructuring. it would also be necessary to ensure that a competition policy is in place which prevents a company from preferring the destruction of local know-how to the sale of a site to a potential competitor. finally, in the current context of rising unemployment, but also of citizens' scepticism towards the union, this legislative initiative by our colleague mr cercas is, i am sure, likely to give confidence to a project of a europe of solidarity.
in writing. the crisis that we have been experiencing since 2008 has accelerated the change in the practices of our companies. while restructuring and relocation have existed before, it is undeniable that the negative economic environment of recent years has contributed to the proliferation of such practices on our continent. it is therefore urgent that we act now to save our industry and the millions of jobs it creates! it is already too late to worry about the situation of our companies when layoffs are being considered. we must anticipate and establish a permanent social dialogue between workers, management and public authorities. the example of arcelormittal, whose restructuring is affecting hundreds of european families, seems to me to be an encouraging one. the closure of the hot-rolling mill in the liège steelworks, my home town, is particularly moving. i therefore call on the commission to take up the recommendations contained in this report as soon as possible and to translate them into concrete proposals, applicable at eu level, for the well-being of our workers and our economies. thank you.
in writing. the closure of the ford plant in genk will result in the loss of 10,000 jobs by the beginning of next year. this implies that the opportunities for vulnerable young people in the industrial labour market in my region are also being reduced. we need to take initiatives to give young people a new perspective. the youth guarantee is a powerful instrument. of course, we make young people more resilient in the labour market if they can get an education, an internship or a job. but this model also offers a lot of opportunities for the companies themselves to give new talent a chance. new talent that companies can fully draw on once the economy recovers. it is perfectly in line with the proposals in the cercas report. already today, forward-looking enterprises are involving the workers and their representatives in the management of their enterprises. continuing training is an essential part of this. ford has shown us in genk how not to do it. if restructuring is necessary, start the operation much earlier, in close consultation with the employees, so that in cooperation with the government additional training opportunities are created for the affected employees. it's the only way to find another job quickly, inside or outside the company.
in writing. with youth unemployment in the eu at 21% and with peaks in spain and greece of 55%, it is high time for a hard-hitting approach. the problem with the commission's proposal is that the drawing up of a youth guarantee scheme is a matter for the member states and is also non-binding because it is only a recommendation. this is a problem, because advice alone will not solve youth unemployment! what we need is a genuine european approach. and that also means that the youth guarantee must be financed mainly from european funds. i would therefore like to hear from the committee how it intends to use the european social fund for this purpose. and of the member states how they will ensure that the european social fund will also have sufficient resources for the next seven years. in 2011, 7.5 million young people in the eu aged 15-24 were not in employment, training or further education. this costs the economy €150 billion each year, while the total cost of a youth guarantee in the eurozone would be €21 billion. i'm pretty sure i'm just a quick calculator, you know?

in writing. in voting this resolution, parliament expressed its ambitions for urban redevelopment as they should be developed in the next cohesion policy programming for 2014-2020 (a minimum of 5% of european regional development fund funding will now be devoted to sustainable urban development). i welcome this because attention to urban development is essential when we know that cities are home to two thirds of the european population and that the problems of unemployment, poverty, discrimination and ageing are rife in them! the resolution aims to present a european plan for cities through the intelligent use of the new resources of cohesion policy and the structural funds. the development of such a plan would provide a legal basis defining common long-term objectives and optimise the use of these funds. it emphasises, among other things, better energy efficiency in buildings and the renovation of suburbs. the resolution also calls for action to rebuild the fabric of existing urban areas, including marginalised areas, and to promote the functional reconversion of derelict sites and conversion areas.
in writing. currently, 80% of european citizens live in urban areas and this trend is growing. cities are the main focus of the effects of the economic crisis, the challenges of combating climate change, job creation, well-being and quality of life. while cities are the engines of the economy, production and employment, they are the context in which the problems of suburbanisation and, more generally, social exclusion and segregation, as well as environmental pollution, are manifested. i am therefore convinced that this important issue must be dealt with at european level, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i believe that urban areas should develop medium- or long-term action plans in the fields of economic, social and territorial cohesion. 80% of european citizens live in urban areas. this number is growing, given the acceleration of migration from rural to urban areas. cities are the main focus of the effects of the economic crisis and the challenges of combating climate change, creating jobs, well-being and quality of life. to ensure the social and economic recovery of cities, it is therefore necessary to rethink the methodologies of the urban and spatial planning sector, by comparing planning methods and intervention instruments. this can enrich environmental, spatial planning, trade, transport and traffic policies through a mixed use of land that integrates physical infrastructure and intangible networks.
in writing. - have we not learned our lesson yet? the cozzolino report is a pile of good intentions that lead straight to hell or something like it, for example the generous european studies for street scenes depicting flying gorillas. not a joke, but a sad reality, by the way. of course, "europe" does not have a monopoly on ill-considered or foolish subsidies or on taxpayer money that is wasted. but cities and municipalities, local authorities and even national governments have a more or less efficient control mechanism and are also held accountable for their policies. europe, on the other hand, is a far-from-my-bed show and the commission is dismissing all questions with a shrug or an arrogant answer of 'it is within the rules so it is allowed'. that's not a democracy anymore. more subsidiarity, please, also in action now.
in writing. territorial development plays a key role in cohesion policy in encouraging the creation of new sustainable jobs by smes and in the development of vocational training programmes. in addition, better territorial cooperation and the development of better adapted macro-regional strategies could prove to be effective tools for addressing regional disparities, such as unequal access to education and employment. however, despite many efforts by the european union, these disparities persist and widen the gap between regions. therefore, it is important to maintain the budget for cohesion policy at its current level after 2013 in order to ensure continued support for regions in need of social and economic recovery throughout the union. to achieve this, a fully integrated approach to project implementation instruments, such as local development strategies led by local actors, integrated territorial investments and joint action plans, would be appropriate.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my colleague, mr derek vaughan. the report focuses on finding effective mechanisms to create synergies between the union's funding programmes under the commission's common strategic framework. it seems to me clear that the complementarity between funding programmes will improve the efficiency of union funding at local and regional level. this document therefore provides examples of mechanisms currently in place, or planned to be implemented, in the regions of the union.
in writing. the eusf is the main instrument of the union's solidarity and financial support to member states or regions affected by major disasters. however, changes are needed to make it as efficient as possible and to make union assistance on the ground more visible and effective. to achieve this, it is imperative that the fund-raising and administrative procedures are significantly speeded up. in other words, the time between the time when the disaster occurs and the time when the member state (or region) receives the aid must be reduced. i think that prepayments are a good solution. however, due to the financial crisis, the proposed amendment should not entail any additional financial burden for the union budget and the member states' budgets. the commission must also be more flexible in accepting aid applications: it rejected 66% of them, as the majority of them were presented as regional disasters. it is also essential to clarify the scope and coverage of the fund, removing any legal uncertainty.
in writing. i agree with the rapporteur that the fund must be able to intervene in exceptional circumstances, even if the disaster does not reach the eligibility threshold. but i am also well aware that, in view of the instruments currently available, it is very difficult to respond adequately to major crises of non-natural origin. following the devastating floods in central europe in 2002, the union, lacking the means to respond to the affected population and to assist the member state affected by a disaster, created a new instrument: the european union solidarity fund. since then, the regulation, which was designed at the time, has not been modified in any way to adapt it to new needs and to correct certain shortcomings in its functioning which have been observed in the ten years of its existence. in recent years, the commission has received an increasing number of applications, which is due to the increase in the number of disasters and the current regulations, the lack of which makes it impossible to eliminate uncertainties as to the possible coverage and admissibility of applications related to disasters and submitted under the exceptional standards for so-called 'extraordinary regional disasters'.
in writing. - i had some doubts before i adopted this report. i am not opposed to a european solidarity fund in principle, and the report contains some proposals to make a significant improvement in the way the fund operates, all the better. we must nevertheless continue to ask ourselves how effective the excessive use of euro-bureaucratization is. i 'll stick to it . the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in the midst of the crisis, we are also deciding to keep the fund's resources at the same level for the coming years. that's not wise. i fear that the reality of the economic crisis will soon overtake us.
in writing. the european union is now increasingly developing its powers, which are bringing its citizens into contact with its administration. however, they still do not have procedural rights to defend themselves against the union. as one of the cornerstones of my policy, european justice should be able to be legitimately used by the citizens of the member states and their regions. i therefore supported the vote for a codification of the principle of service and the granting of european administrative procedural law. in doing so, the union and its citizens will both benefit: the union will benefit from a more efficient administration; and they'll be able to trust the latter.
in writing. why did i vote in favour of this text? with the development of the union's powers, citizens are increasingly confronted directly with the european administration, without always having the corresponding procedural rights which they could exercise against it in cases where this would prove necessary. in my view, citizens are entitled to the same level of transparency, efficiency, speed of implementation and responsiveness from the union administration, whether they are lodging a formal complaint or exercising their right to petition under the treaty; and the commission should ensure that information is provided to complainants or petitioners about the possibility of taking further action in the case concerning them. the existing union rules and principles on good administration are dispersed in a variety of sources: primary law, case law of the court of justice of the european union, secondary law, non-binding legislation and unilateral commitments of the union institutions. the union does not have a coherent and complete set of codified rules of administrative law and must remedy this!
in writing. − it is time to work on a european framework for a contemporary approach to business restructuring. we are not advocating a pathetic initiative to impose all kinds of extra rules on entrepreneurs. - no, it's the opposite. employers and employees should anticipate restructuring much more closely. this includes in particular: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be given greater attention to the training of employees to improve their opportunities inside or outside the company in the event of restructuring. the brutal closure of the ford plant in genk is certainly not of this era. the car assembly industry has been warning for years about overcapacity. we need to sit down much earlier in such cases, the employers, the employees and the government, to determine how, through additional training, the impact of such a dramatic closure can be mitigated. that is in the interests of all concerned. these proposals are already clearly set out in the 2010 social agenda. it's time to turn them into action now. it is also a prerequisite for giving the 'new industrial revolution' that the european commission wants to launch a chance of success.
restructuring is a phenomenon which is tending to spread due to the economic crisis. it is usually considered too late. anticipation is the key to stability and competitiveness. companies must be encouraged to anticipate the restructuring required by modernisation, excess capacity and structural adjustment. this is the only way for restructuring to be successful not only economically but above all socially, since human resources must remain at the heart of the strategic development of enterprises.
in writing. corporate restructuring is one of the most significant phenomena of globalisation, responsible for the loss of almost six and a half million jobs in the struggling construction and manufacturing sectors between 2008 and 2011. it is with seriousness, but also with a sense of responsibility, that the european parliament adopted the cercas report this afternoon. in general, it agrees with the diagnosis made by the commission in its october 2010 communication on industrial policy: 'improving the anticipation and management of restructuring would help workers and businesses to adapt to transitions ...'. but, as is often the case, the remedies are lacking, as is the inability in many member states to bring about the sacred union between intermediary bodies when social circumstances so require. the european union would do well to adopt the german model of 'co-management', which gives employees' representatives a recognised and important place on company management boards. the industrial health of germany largely validates the value of its model of social relations which should become one of the tools of the "highly competitive social market economy", piously cited in the lisbon treaty.
in writing. − a strong social dialogue based on mutual trust and shared responsibility is the best instrument for anticipating, preventing and managing enterprise restructuring processes. i agree with mr cercas on this. the european commission must now present a legislative proposal on the provision of information and consultation to employees, and the prevention and management of restructuring. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. extensive training rights for workers and a quality reintegration policy must become the standard in europe. at the same time, the eu must also give workers the rights and opportunities to face changes in the business world with confidence. employers and employees may agree on this in collective agreements. but even if that does not happen, a european directive should guarantee minimum rights for workers. the reintegration of workers should not start at the moment of their dismissal. they should be given the opportunity to train throughout their careers so that they can move more easily from job to job. the european commission must now respond to the european parliament's request and then make a proposal together with the social partners.
in writing. i am a strong supporter of a strong social dialogue, based on mutual trust and shared responsibility, as the best way to find consensual solutions and common approaches to anticipate, prevent and manage restructuring. these practices are becoming more and more common, owing to economic difficulties, and have become more widespread in recent years, taking various forms, intensifying in certain sectors and gaining new ones, and are having unforeseeable consequences for the economic and social fabric of the member states. they often have dramatic consequences for individuals and are too often downplayed by the industrial and financial sectors, whereas without man there is no production. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
i would like to congratulate mr tannock on his thorough and interesting report on eu policy on the horn of africa. it is a good report and it is interesting, for example, that the danger of the advance of islamism and islamic terrorism in africa is mentioned in this report. it is equally good, and this is a strange thing, that it is explicitly stated that developing countries should not be given blank cheques, millions of euros in unconditional development aid, because in the end it is the european taxpayer who has to pay for it and that this must also be accounted for, for example in the form of an adequate food strategy for those countries. but i always say: not words, but deeds! i remember that ethiopia, for example, received no less than 400 million dollars in development aid from the european union in the period 2004-08, and that all the parliamentary questions i asked about the misuse and inadequate use of these funds were ignored by the commission. i am afraid that some scepticism about the practical consequences of this report is justified.

in writing. the horn of africa is one of the most food insecure regions in the world. millions of people in the region suffer from malnutrition and are threatened by famine. this geographical region includes some of the countries with the lowest sanitation standards and is also one of the regions of the world where poverty and lack of governance are most pronounced. the insecurity of the population and food insecurity in particular are leading to serious humanitarian crises. it is clear that the international community has failed to take preventive measures to deal with the problems of the security of the population, drought and famine on the ground. the text does not seek to promote european neo-colonialism, but to provide adequate support while respecting the values of this continent.
in writing. the european parliament believes that the eu should help developing countries to benefit from their genetic resources and traditional knowledge and, in its resolution adopted today, set out the measures it recommends to combat biopiracy (i.e. the lucrative use by multinational companies of medicinal substances and traditional remedies from developing countries without the permission of the latter and without the benefit of the populations who discovered these active ingredients). the challenge is significant because, despite the existence of international agreements to protect the rights of indigenous peoples to their genetic resources and traditional knowledge, there is no mechanism to enforce them. however, 90% of the world's biological heritage is in developing countries, while the vast majority of patents are held by developed countries and 70% of the world's poor depend directly on biological diversity for their survival and well-being.
in writing. biopiracy is a subject that is close to my heart. the protection and conservation of genetic diversity are key elements in the achievement of the millennium development goals. genetic resources are particularly crucial for sustainable agriculture and food security. moreover, genetic diversity is one of the most important aspects for the survival of species and the resilience of the ecosystem. as a result, the depletion of genetic diversity, which is an integral part of the process of erosion of biological diversity, is a fundamental issue for humanity. despite its crucial importance for the survival of humanity, genetic diversity is being depleted at a very worrying rate. such erosion of diversity poses new challenges to both holders and users of genetic resources, the former being most often in developing countries rich in biological diversity, and the latter in developed countries. the eradication of extreme poverty and hunger and the promotion of biodiversity and healthy ecosystems for agriculture, forestry and fisheries in a sustainable development perspective are therefore very important issues.

in writing. a revision of the dangerous preparations directive (1999/45/ec) was necessary to ensure the protection of health and the environment. the amendment fills the legal gaps and the lack of regulation on dangerous preparations. the gap in the conditions for protecting the confidentiality of technical information, which is governed by intellectual property law, is now filled by this revision.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the recast of the dangerous preparations directive makes it possible to update the proposal for a directive, in accordance with the lisbon treaty, to replace the old obsolete provisions with new ones, including updating the legal basis.
in writing. the mediterranean is the most overfished sea in the world. the seriousness of the situation - more than 54% of mediterranean fish stocks studied by scientists are considered to be overfished - has justified the establishment of a binding legal framework at european level, adopted in 2006. since 1 june 2010, the regulation has applied to the member states concerned. as is often the case, some countries are not playing the game and today's vote in the european parliament on the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the mediterranean is timely. it was important that meps, by amending the legislation on fisheries in the mediterranean, support an ambitious approach to greater sustainability of fisheries and better protection of natural resources. this makes all the more sense as the reform of the common fisheries policy will be voted on at the next plenary session. the fisheries committee set the tone by advocating a major reform: a war on overfishing, an end to discards and the trading of annual quotas. all that's left is to turn the trial in three weeks.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. i hope that with the reform of the common fisheries policy, a new regionalised framework will make it possible to find quickly an appropriate regulatory solution for the mediterranean, which will be accepted by the member states and the parties concerned, while taking into account the specificities of this sea basin, but also ensuring in an effective way the sustainability of fisheries and the protection of resources and the environment. since the conservation aspect is essential, it should be included in the title of the regulation.
in writing. biodiversity has long been a major concern of the european union. as early as the 1990s and 2000s, the convention on biological diversity (cbd) and the cartagena protocol on the prevention of biological hazards were drafted to ensure the safe transfer, handling and use of living modified organisms (lmos) that have the potential to cause adverse effects on the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity or that present a priori a risk to human health. the adoption of the nagoya kuala lumpur additional protocol in 2010 was seen as a victory for the protection of all the planet's threatened ecosystems and for the fight against the extinction of certain animal and plant species. in 2010, a major agreement was also adopted on "access and benefit-sharing" (abs), regulating the sharing of profits by the pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries from genetic resources from the "biodiversity reservoir" of the south. i think that these profits from the manufacture of medicines, cosmetics or food resources represent billions which should be used as funds for the developing countries.
in writing. the nagoya kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and reparation will make a significant contribution to the achievement of the objectives of the convention on biological diversity and the cartagena protocol on biosafety. in line with the eu environmental liability directive adopted in 2004, the additional protocol specifically addresses liability and redress for damage to biodiversity caused by lmos. i agree with the text of my colleague matthias groote and with the council decision approving, on behalf of the european union, the nagoya - kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and reparation, as regards matters falling within the union's competence. it is a good thing that most member states have signed the additional protocol. i would urge them to ratify the text as soon as possible.
in writing. despite recent economic and budgetary reforms, the european union is still suffering from the financial crisis. it will be saved by a wide-ranging action to provide a symmetrical response to excessive macro-financial imbalances and to strengthen the general level of socio-economic convergence and solidarity within economic and monetary union (emu). this action is based mainly on long-term fiscal consolidation. for example, the latter will encourage the reduction of unproductive expenditure and greater flexibility in the labour market; this will help to stimulate growth in the medium term. moreover, they will make it possible, above all, to regulate the excessive debt and deficit in which most member states are mired. but it is essential that an emphasis on sustainable growth, economic development and social protection should go hand in hand with these improvements. the key message is therefore to mitigate the short-term recessionary effects while aiming to stimulate medium-term growth factors such as the optimisation of training programmes and the reduction of youth unemployment.
in writing. - the vote is clear. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is a welcome step towards the creation of a single currency. this vote marks a major turning point, because the conservative-liberal majority in the european commission and the council of ministers has been blind to the negative effects of austerity on the economy in recent years. the right-wing parties in the european parliament were equally uncritical of the austerity policy pursued. slowly but surely, they are beginning to realize that their strategy is not working. for the first time in the european parliament there is a majority in favour of a more critical tone. at the end of 2012, budget commissioner olli rehn called several times for a more flexible application of european budgetary standards to stimulate public investment. the tone of the european debate is changing. now for the policy. we need to get our budgets in order, but at a slower pace so we don't prolong the recession unnecessarily. we must give the euro countries more time to reduce their budget deficits and more room for sustainable and social investment.
in writing. the economic, financial and banking crisis has not diminished in intensity. problems affecting public finances undermine socioeconomic development and political stability. the euro area government debt to gdp ratio increased from 86.2% in the first quarter of 2011 to 88.2% in the first quarter of 2012. it appears that the recent reforms of the eu's economic and budgetary governance framework cannot, on their own, solve the crisis. large-scale action is needed to provide a symmetrical response to excessive macro-financial imbalances and to strengthen the overall level of socio-economic convergence and solidarity of the economic and monetary union. i remain very concerned that, despite reform and consolidation efforts by member states, tensions persist in the euro area sovereign bond markets, as evidenced by the large yield spreads and high volatility of interest rates. i see the immediate trigger and the root cause of this as concerns on the financial markets about the soundness of public and private sector finances in some euro area countries.
in writing. today's vote follows strong criticism of the rating agencies, which were accused of not seeing the 2008 financial crisis coming in the first place, and then of having fuelled the sovereign debt crisis by downgrading the ratings of several member states without clear justification, threatening the euro area with implosion for a time. i therefore welcome the adoption of this new regulation (already the third since the introduction of a european framework for credit rating agencies!) which introduces a stricter framework for credit rating agencies. these new rules will, i hope, help to prevent the interference of rating agencies in the european agenda. in particular, they will be required to adhere to three unsolicited sovereign ratings per year. they will also have to explain their methodology in the future. evaluations will have to be made on fixed dates and agencies will no longer be able to match their ratings to policy recommendations for governments. they will therefore have to be more transparent and will be held liable in civil cases of intentional error or negligence. i regret, however, that the text does not go far enough to combat the domination of the 'big three' (standard and poor's, moody's, fitch) over almost the entire market.
in writing. in these times of financial crisis, rating agencies have more power than ever: they can, on the basis of an increasingly standardised analysis, devalue a country's creditworthiness, with the consequences we are experiencing today. these powers make european economies dependent on their ratings. it is therefore imperative that we free ourselves from this and that we have a more transparent and regular assessment of our debts, especially sovereign debts: they will be obliged to provide a detailed report on the reasons for their assessment and to return it within a given period. in addition, the european securities and markets authority (esma) could act as a watchdog for those agencies by monitoring their activities and ensuring the diversity of their valuation methods by promoting competition between agencies and, where appropriate, administering sanctions. in order to reduce our dependency, the participation of credit rating agencies in rated entities will be limited in order to eliminate conflicts of interest.
in writing. this is a text that is going in the right direction. the three existing rating agencies are acting like gods before whom the member states tremble. with each prediction, governments fill the altar with offerings often involving the destinies of many of their citizens. we can no longer be held hostage by these agencies, by such opaque private companies. they have only the power that is given to them, a power based on the fear they cause. i am a strong advocate of healthier, fairer, more transparent and above all more independent ratings, which would become indicators rather than threats. i therefore voted in favour of this report, while stressing that 'the direct incorporation of credit ratings only into the ucits and aif monitoring system encourages market participants to pay excessive attention to the opinions of credit rating agencies rather than to carry out their own credit analysis'.
in writing. one of the consequences of the crisis is that it has indirectly led investors, including ucits and aifs, to rely excessively on credit ratings for their investments in debt instruments, without necessarily carrying out their own assessments of the credit quality of the issuers of these securities. in order to protect investments and credit, persons managing ucits and aifs should be required to avoid relying exclusively and automatically on, or making excessive use of, external credit ratings when assessing the risks inherent in the investments of those ucits and aifs. given the objective of this directive, which is to contribute to reducing the over-reliance of ucits and aifs on external credit ratings when investing, it is very important that credit quality and creditworthiness can be freely verified.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which extends the scope of the rating rules to rating outlooks, changes to the use of credit ratings, the independence of rating agencies, rating disclosure and sovereign debt rating. for many years, the activity of credit rating agencies has been very extensive, with a significant impact on the behaviour of economic and financial actors and on the life of public institutions.
in writing. the baltic sea fish stocks are a real food treasure for europeans, and must be protected. this is the role of the multiannual plan for cod stocks. the plan will set the maximum fishing mortality rate, the periods and types of vessels allowed to fish. for example, fishermen will not be able to catch more than 0.25% of fish aged 3 to 6 years in the case of cod stock in area a. it should be noted that this amendment allows small-scale fishing of cod catches during the closing season, particularly in the summer months, without affecting the concentrations before and during spawning which, in the baltic, take place in the deep sea, far from coastal areas. that's why this plan deserves my full attention.
in writing. according to the reports of the international council for the exploration of the sea, the cod stocks in the baltic sea were overfished in the early 2000s. the fishing mortality rate had reduced the stock to a level that it was in danger of collapsing. the western baltic cod stock was in a slightly better situation, but the stock yields were far below what they could be in the long term. for this reason, a multiannual plan has been established for the cod stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the main objective of the plan was to ensure that the baltic cod stocks could be exploited under economically, environmentally and socially sustainable conditions. to achieve this objective, the plan set out rules for establishing the annual fishing opportunities for this stock in terms of total allowable catches and fishing effort. those rules include a parameter related to fishing mortality, based on scientific recommendations issued annually and used to determine the conservation status of a stock.
in writing. transitional technical measures have been in place since 1 january 2010 and will expire on 31 december 2012. at the very least, this leaves little time for the european parliament and the council to reach political agreement on one of the most complex and important aspects of the cfp. this will require a lot of goodwill on the part of all the actors, which is what parliament hopes to get from the other actors in the debate. this proposal on technical measures should not prejudge decisions on landing obligations to be taken under the cfp basic regulation, and the temporary nature of the legal act should be clearly linked to the envisaged regionalised framework for technical conservation measures, once the new cfp has been adopted. technical measures must be carefully designed for specific cases and areas and cannot be considered as rules applicable to all member states in the same way; a regionalised approach is therefore essential.
in writing. the rules of procedure provide that the president, vice-presidents and quaestors shall be elected by secret ballot. however, where the number of candidates does not exceed the number of seats to be filled, the candidates may be elected by acclamation. the question was whether this standard should apply in the same way when there is only one candidate and only one post to be filled. we believe that if only one vice-president is to be replaced and there is only one candidate, he can be elected by acclamation. the president has discretion to decide whether the election shall be by acclamation or by secret ballot. the elected candidate shall take the place of the vice-president whom he replaces in the order of precedence.

in writing. it is important that the member states' ministers for employment and social affairs agree to implement youth guarantee mechanisms in all member states. the youth guarantee is not a job guarantee but an instrument through which all young eu citizens and legal residents aged 25 or under, and recent graduates aged under 30, are offered a job, continuing training or a good quality apprenticeship within four months of losing their job or leaving mainstream education. it should also be stressed that the youth guarantee must effectively improve the situation of young people who are not in employment, education or training. its guarantee mechanisms should be eligible for specific forms of european funding, in particular in the member states with the highest rates of youth unemployment.

- i'm the reporter. - mr president, i am very pleased to be able to present the report here today. i have worked very closely with my colleagues in writing not only the report but also the compromise amendments, and without their support this report would of course never have looked like it does today and would never have been such a good report. on the subject of improving access to finance for smes, i have held extensive consultations with many of the sector's stakeholders, not only entrepreneurs or business organisations themselves, but also many credit institutions and federations of credit institutions. it was and still is very important to me that we as the european parliament write a report which has a broad support among the stakeholders themselves. we all know that europe has some 23 million smes, which generate the lion's share of economic value added and create jobs in europe. the recent months of the financial crisis have made it clear that many smes are finding themselves in difficulty when seeking funding. and they are even more troubled when they go to the banks and look for the necessary loans. because 85% of our smes are still financed by bank loans. but the funding requirements are getting stricter. getting a traditional loan is harder than ever because of the effects of the financial crisis. difficult access to finance is hampering the growth of smes, but also the overall economic growth. smes therefore need concrete solutions and would not benefit from another broad and comprehensive report. that is why i have put forward concrete proposals in this report. we propose that more attention be paid to alternative forms of financing. crowdfunding, venture capital, we must encourage this, for example through fund to fund investments with the help of the european investment fund. we must also look at greater flexibility and transparency in bank lending, including by addressing red tape and limiting the personal guarantee as a condition. the report also focuses not only on training but also on the guidance of entrepreneurs in drawing up a business plan. we also want to improve general financial knowledge by means of an entrepreneurship course in secondary and higher education. after all, the creativity and entrepreneurial spirit of young people is crucial to getting us out of the crisis. this report is an own-initiative report drawn up in response to the european commission's action plan. the european commission has also recently put forward a second action plan: the entrepreneurship 2020. i am very pleased that many of the elements contained in our report have already been taken up by the commission. the commission's proposals include strengthening existing financial instruments and simplifying tax structures to give smes access to finance through direct private investment. but it also focuses on the professionalisation and coaching of entrepreneurs and wants to give entrepreneurs a second chance after bankruptcy. the european parliament is largely on the same page. the european regulations must leave sufficient room for the specific nature of all smes. there are, after all, great differences between smes, not only within countries, but also between countries. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied in a fair and transparent manner. europe, with this report and the commission's proposal, is showing the way forward, but the member states also have a great deal of responsibility. i therefore call very clearly on the member states in my report to eliminate administrative burdens and to provide fiscal incentives for entrepreneurship and also to activate the savings capital that is currently sitting idle and to convert it into real investment in our real economy and in our smes. that savings must be activated to enable economic growth and jobs to be restored. the report was unanimously approved by the econ committee of parliament. as i said earlier, this report sets out some very important and very concrete solutions and i hope, together with my colleagues, that we can count on massive support for this report here in the plenary tomorrow.

in writing. the smaller aegean islands face several challenges, such as the extra cost of transporting certain agricultural products, the ageing of the population, and the need to promote local production. the specific nature of these islands calls for specific action to enable local farmers to cope with their difficulties. it is therefore essential to adopt measures to guarantee the supply of agricultural products and to preserve and develop local agricultural production. support for greater regional integration would also promote economic development and growth in these regions.
in writing. agricultural activity, in its most modern sense, is inextricably linked to sustainable economic, social and ecological development. the agricultural production of the aegean islands must be designed to prevent any unilateral dependence of local economic activity on the main source of income, namely the provision of tourist services, with a primary focus on safeguarding the valuable local natural and cultural heritage. it should be stressed, however, that the commission's proposal to adopt specific measures for agriculture in the smaller aegean islands seeks to reformulate, not revise, the existing regulation. all the european parliament's proposals will have to take account of the regulatory scope of the scheme, whose financing is part of the first pillar of the cap. addressing the permanent and structural handicaps of the agricultural sector in the aegean islands requires a systematic approach, a thorough needs analysis and a clear strategic direction. the aid scheme for the smaller aegean islands alone cannot and should not be able to address the challenges mentioned above.
in writing. today, in the field of agriculture, it is easy to see that the big industrial producers are in the forefront. however, it is important to continue to focus on local producers and on the specific features of the territory, especially in the outermost regions of the european union. to this end, it is essential to take certain specific measures which will contribute to the development of these productions. these measures will ensure sustainable plant and animal diversification and will contribute to better self-sufficiency of the local population, which will then reduce imports. they will encourage innovation and research leading to sustainable agricultural production. it is also imperative to increase the competitiveness of the different producers in the outermost regions of the union. it is by going in this direction and implementing these specific measures that local producers will be able to survive.
in writing. i fully agree with the rapporteur that the union should step up border controls on imports from third countries, whose production should meet the same veterinary and phytosanitary requirements as those imposed on farmers and herders in the outermost regions in order to avoid unfair competition with local products. bananas, which account for a very large proportion of the final agricultural production of the outermost regions, in particular the canary islands (25% of the region's total production), will have to face the tariff concessions granted by the union to banana exports from latin american countries. the importance of this sector, which, like tomato and sugar, is one of the few export-oriented sectors on the islands, could easily justify, in my view, a revision of the posei financial allocations to compensate for the losses which the concessions could cause to the producers on the islands. however, other productions besides bananas, such as tomatoes, sugar and rum, are also subject to strong external pressures, the consequences of which should be properly assessed by the commission.

in writing. there are 23 million smes in the eu. this means that 99% of european enterprises are smes and that smes provide 2/3 of jobs in the private sector. it goes without saying that they are one of the essential pillars of the european economy. in these times of crisis, smes are finding it increasingly difficult to obtain financing from banks. this is not without damaging consequences for employment, social integration, innovation, growth and the european economy as a whole. the commission, in launching its action plan, wants to take concrete measures to mobilise savings for growth and jobs, in particular by helping smes to have easier access to finance, by helping them to become better acquainted with financial mechanisms, taking into account their diversity and specificity. the commission's action plan is in line with the europe 2020 strategy and is a key tool to help us emerge from the economic and financial crisis.
in writing. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are very important to the european union. they are the backbone of the european economy and an important driver of growth in the union. smes are a powerful contributor to job creation in the 27 member states, but they are vulnerable. this vulnerability became clear in the aftermath of the crisis. as a result, some lenders have become more cautious in lending to smes. excessive caution and a lack of investment could lead to a tightening of credit. in addition, the new stricter rules applicable in particular to financial institutions and capital requirements put in place by the european union and national authorities have made it more difficult for smes to access finance. these companies are often at the end of a long distribution chain and as such are most affected by late payments and current payment deadlines. this report is a small step but it is a step in the right direction.

vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, just last night i reiterated how important it is for the commission, and for me as the person responsible for industrial policy, to take action to re-industrialize our european union in a modern and competitive way. it is a clear choice we have made, but the industrial policy which i think must lead to have a different industrial network than the industrial network of the 1980s and 1990s. a modern, competitive, high-quality industry that is a key player in the green economy and therefore also in our action to combat climate change. i am sure that a balanced policy, where industrial policy, environmental policy and health policy can work together and all have the same objective, which is to make life better for our fellow citizens. so my proposal - and i want to reassure mr grossetête and mr tatarella - is certainly not a proposal against industry, especially the car industry, which is one of the key sectors in the document on the policy for reindustrialisation in the european union. but we are thinking of a green car, a car that is less polluting, not only in terms of co2 emissions but also in terms of noise pollution. the commission proposal for a regulation seems to me to be a proposal which seeks to balance the different interests: the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment. it is not an exaggerated proposal, it is not an extremist proposal, but it is a proposal which seeks to reconcile the interests of a modern and competitive industrial policy and the protection of the environment and therefore of the health of citizens. i believe that we can continue to work in this direction and i am not unwilling to examine the amendments for improvement of the commission's text, both in terms of timing and in terms of electric vehicles. in the debate which will follow parliament's vote, and also in the council, we are prepared to work together to make the text of the new regulation better. i have to say that many of the things we are asking for for certain vehicles are already in place, in the sense that they are in line with the regulations we are proposing. it is true that for some - and i keep repeating this - is to make social policy, that is to help our fellow citizens to live better lives both in terms of protecting their health and in terms of their economic conditions. i thank the members who have said that the european commission's proposal is too ambitious, and since i also heard the commission being praised for its ambitious proposals on other matters last night, it seems to me that the feeling between this house and the european commission is still very strong and i thank you for that.
in writing. i think we can all agree that we must reduce traffic noise as much as possible. noise pollution is undoubtedly causing serious health problems. however, to achieve results, a comprehensive approach to traffic noise is needed. we cannot put the entire burden on the car industry, but we must combat traffic noise on several fronts. the quality of the road surface must be improved and the use of sound-efficient car tyres increased. we are all in favour of quieter cars, but we must also take account of the precarious situation in which the car industry finds itself today. the sector is in recession. i am therefore convinced that we must take an ambitious but balanced approach.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, mr barroso has said that an agreement is possible. let us be honest, mr barroso. an agreement is possible, and i think there will be an agreement, but not on the terms you put in your introduction. you talked about a real mid-term review, flexibility between headings and between years, real own resources and no cuts in spending for the future, and you also agree not to create a big debt or deficit in europe because of that difference between commitments and payments. let us be honest. there will be no real mid-term review in the proposal. there will not be any flexibility between headings. the member states do not accept flexibility between headings because they say that this is impossible for them. i am afraid that even the commission’s good proposal will fall on own resources, on the ftt. i hear rumours that germany does not want it and that, in the final conclusion they do not want this ftt in this budget, as envisaged by the commission. the same goes for the additional cuts. where will we see additional cuts? in heading 1a again? the new 25? we have to ask the irish presidency about that. we need to know. what will the final proposal be in order to make a deal in the council? more additional cuts in heading 1a so that in the end we can go back to the 2013 budget? we would be better off continuing with the 2013 budget than discussing what to do with this budget – this mff – for the next year. so i am afraid that, while we totally agree with the commission on the next mff, the reality is that there will be another deal, as there was seven years ago with 42 exceptions, rebates and derogations in the budget. what will happen is that this decision by the european council will not be a formal decision. it will only be a political decision. a discussion will then start in the general affairs council and we will only be consulted here in this parliament to say ‘yes’ or ‘no’, not next week but in three months time. and in three months time the presidency and the member states will try to buy a number of delegations here in the parliament in order to find a majority for that budget. exactly the same thing happened seven years ago. so we have to be very clear. if we say today that our conditions are a mid-term review, flexibility, real own resources, no cuts in spending for the future and no real deficit, as we are creating now with this mff, we have to continue to stand by that in one month, in two months and in three months’ time when we will have to give a formal ‘yes’ or ‘no’ on this mff for the coming years. that is the political power play. for me it is not about figures; it is a power play between the council and parliament. who is in fact the budgetary authority in a democratic system? is it the heads of state or government or is it the european parliament? that is what it is about. in every democracy it is the parliament which is the budgetary authority and not the council, not the head of government or the head of state. it is about debts, so it is not only about figures. it is not just about what we will spend in the next seven years, but it is also about the balance of power inside a democratic european union. is it parliament that has the last say, or is it the council? my proposal, mr barroso, is that in the discussion – and i am also saying this to the irish presidency – we talk not only about the mid-term review. my proposal is to have a sunset clause after two or three years. why not? we are now talking about a budget for seven years. anything could happen. we could have an enormous crisis in europe so that this mff might no longer be applicable, so why not have a sunset clause that, after three years – mr daul said after two years and i agree with that, but i think three years is more realistic – obliges us to give a new consent to go further with this budget for the next three or four years. finally i think that we need to return to annual budgets. what country sets a budget for seven years and sticks to that? that does not exist anywhere. in fact it lowers the power of parliament. the only other example that i know of was the soviet union. there it was for five years. we do it for seven years. we think that we can we make a plan for longer than that. that is the reason why mr farage also agrees with me that we should go back to annual budgets. thank you, mr farage. that is the first sensible and positive reaction that i have had from you in nearly three years. things are getting better and better with you. you are becoming a normal member of the european parliament, which is a good development.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are in a rather special session. yesterday we applauded mr hollande for proposing that we invest in more sustainable development and in young people. the budget, the latest version of mr van rompuy's budget, proposes 15% cuts in the areas of research and youth. we are going to hear from the tunisian president, mr marzouki, shortly, about what is happening in tunisia and we are going to give him our full support for the democratic transition. the budget proposes a reduction of 13% for foreign policy and 11% for the development fund. we discussed yesterday the european semester and the importance of having a social and employment dimension, particularly in our regions. but here we are being offered a 20% reduction for the regions in transition. so i ask you, or at any rate the most sceptical among us, to consider whether it is possible, yes or no, for this parliament to be part of a more promising budgetary strategy and a strategy which enables the council to honour these commitments. these commitments must be paid, we cannot afford the current delay and we cannot afford, as was very well said yesterday, the announced deficit. so, frankly, the more skeptical ones have to join those who today want a real budget.
mr president, i would like to return to the commercial policy aspects. we talked about openness, globalization, growth and so on. all right, but let's be careful. the tragic case of mittal, whose workers are today marching near parliament, calls for at least three reflections. firstly, is europe, which is so timid in defending its borders against immigration, not too naive when it comes to, for example, investors, predators, who only follow a financial logic? we are totally powerless today to deal with these acts. secondly, in our trade policies, should we not be more careful about what our partners do in terms of, for example, state aid and other benefits? we are preparing an agreement with the united states and we are abandoning the close monitoring of these agreements, of these possibilities of distortion of competition. the same is true for russia and china. this makes us particularly vulnerable. thirdly, it is not right that our trade agreements do not take social and environmental constraints into account any more. this breach allows predators to empty europe of its industrial products and then reimport products made under more unregulated conditions, sometimes by their own subsidiaries. this is what mittal is doing, closing sites in europe and then using its foreign subsidiaries to come and resupply them. 'there is something rotten in the kingdom of denmark', as shakespeare would have said, but without falling into protectionism, we must insist on the fair reciprocity of trade agreements by including social and environmental criteria. without this, there will be no industrial policy in europe.
in writing. if the proposals for the next multiannual budget fall too far short of the commission's proposal, the european parliament must take its responsibility and reject them. we have that power and our group will do everything possible to oppose irrational cuts. i am glad to see that the other groups have also matured their minds. the european union will no longer be able to fulfil its tasks effectively if the european budget is cut even more drastically. the european budget is being cut back at the expense of measures needed to overcome the crisis. we need to invest in sustainable and growth-oriented investments and in people (for example, the erasmus programme or the youth guarantee scheme). we have the impression that only national interests dominate the european debate in the council, whereas we have a common interest in fighting the crisis. by investing in research and development, infrastructure, training programmes and other crucial areas such as the fight against youth unemployment, europe can help member states to tackle the crisis. the union is not a toy for national interests, it is an instrument for common european interests.
in writing. in 2007, romania and bulgaria joined the european union. following this enlargement of the eu customs union, trade rights of some members of the world trade organisation have been somewhat reduced, particularly those of the united states. under the wto rules (which date back to gatt), any member of the wto is entitled to negotiate compensation if it deems it necessary. in this case, the united states has done so to obtain the restoration of its trade rights. this is entirely justified and understandable. that is why i voted in favour of this compensation agreement between the european union and the united states. it is important to remember, however, that, on the whole, this enlargement of the union has been favourable to wto members.
in writing. with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the european union has enlarged its customs union. consequently, it was obliged, under the rules of the world trade organisation (article xxiv (6) of gatt), to open negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights in the lists of acceding countries in order to agree on mutually satisfactory compensation to offset the increase in consolidated duties and the resulting significant losses. such compensation is necessary if the adoption of the external tariff regime of the union leads to an increase in duties beyond the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto, while 'duly taking into account the reductions in customs duties on the same tariff line made by other constituent entities of the customs union at the time of the establishment of that union', in accordance with the provisions of article xxiv (6).
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation by my colleague, mrs pervenche berès, on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that member states are to regard their economic policies and the promotion of employment as matters of common interest and to coordinate them within the council. in two separate articles, it provides that the council is to adopt the broad guidelines for economic policies (article 121) and the guidelines for employment (article 148) and that the latter must be compatible with the former. the employment guidelines were adopted on 21 october 2010 and, as provided for in the adoption decision, they should remain stable until 2014 in order to focus on their implementation.
in writing. i welcome the vote on this report which should allow european patients to have faster access to generic medicines. we also propose a 60-day time limit for deciding on the price and reimbursement of generic medicines, in order to speed up the availability of these products and save money for patients and social security systems. the competent authorities in the member states would also be required to publish, at least once a year, a list of medicines covered by their public health insurance system together with their price, which i believe is essential information for patients.
in writing. while respecting the exclusive competence of member states to set prices and reimbursement for medicinal products, minimum procedural requirements should also ensure legal certainty and transparency for competent national authorities, foster the production of medicinal products and the entry of generic medicinal products onto the market, and encourage research and development of new medicinal products, with the ultimate aim of facilitating access to affordable treatment for all patients in europe. i would like to stress, as a matter of priority, the need to strengthen the provisions on the transparency of the decision-making process and the decisions taken, which is the subject of growing demand from society, particularly as regards the setting of prices and reimbursement of pharmaceutical products. we have therefore suggested a series of additional measures, including the obligation for the competent authorities to disclose the names and declarations of interests of the experts who are members of their decision-making bodies. those provisions, as well as greater access to documents and information for the general public, should aim to enhance the transparency, integrity and independence of decisions taken and should, in the long term, strengthen trust in the competent public authorities at national level.
in writing. the european parliament voted in favour of an ambitious reform aimed at making fishing in the european union more sustainable by ending overfishing practices that are causing the decline of fisheries resources. we voted for the restoration of fish stocks in eu waters, which are now overfished, by 2015 and for a gradual ban on discards from 2014 (the practice of dumping unmarketable fish because they are too small, damaged or simply out of quota, etc., which represents almost a quarter of the total eu catch). the reform, which is due to come into force in 2014, still needs to be discussed between parliament and the council, but the irish presidency has already announced that it hopes to reach an agreement before the end of its term in june. i am glad of this because the vote on this report is a great victory!
in writing. the common fisheries policy has not yet produced the expected results. however, eu waters are equipped with all the conditions necessary for economic, social and environmental benefits to be derived from fishing. it is therefore essential to make changes to this policy in order to develop this sector in a sustainable way that is beneficial for fishermen, citizens and the marine environment. some elements are essential to ensure sound fisheries management, such as the restoration of fish stocks, without which fishing becomes impossible. to do this, fishermen must respect their quotas, adopt a no-refuse policy and thus reduce waste. at the moment we are all concerned with environmental problems, so it seems to me also vital to pay particular attention to small fishing enterprises, which, through their non-industrial techniques, contribute to the respect and balance of nature. adopting this reform means making the fisheries sector sustainable, profitable and environmentally friendly.
in writing. i supported this morning a historic vote by the european parliament in favour of an ambitious reform of the common fisheries policy, with one slogan: stop overfishing! the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the measures proposed include: stock restoration, the setting of annual fishing quotas, an end to the intolerable practice of dumping thousands of tonnes of fish for human consumption into european waters, and the use of long-term programmes based on more reliable scientific data. this means more fish, better catches and, consequently, more jobs in the sector. the new policy is expected to come into force in 2014 and by 2020 will increase fish catch by 15 million tonnes and fishermen's income by 25% if properly implemented. in the meantime, the ball is in the court of the member states, which will have to put aside certain national interests and resolutely decide on a modern european fisheries system on a human scale.
in writing. - we have just adopted a historic proposal to prevent overfishing and the unintended discarding of by-catches. almost a quarter of all catches are discarded half-alive or half-dead in order to stay below quotas or because they are not the fish we want. fortunately, this proposal will put an end to that. three decades of mismanagement by european fisheries ministers have left european fisheries largely dependent on subsidies, while 75 to 90% of european fish stocks are overfished and ecosystems are ruined. the annual negotiations between ministers, which set fishing quotas far too high, will be a thing of the past, because fishing must be based on scientific advice. between 1987 and 2011, european fisheries ministers ignored scientific advice in some 70% of their decisions. in order to stop overfishing and restore fish stocks to healthy levels, catch limits should be maintained until 2015. that would allow fish stocks to recover by 2020. however, it is feared that european fisheries ministers will try to water down these reforms. that's the political stake now: the european parliament has been asked to give its opinion on the draft agreement.
in writing. not only is overfishing a scourge that is destroying the marine environment, it also risks destroying almost 100 000 european jobs and putting entire communities that depend directly on the sea at risk. the over-exploitation of fish stocks is reducing their size and the volume of catches. the 4 million tonnes of fish caught cannot meet the ever-growing demand of europeans, who consume 23.1 kilos of fish per person per year. 90% of mediterranean stocks are overfished. it is not too late to act, but it is time, otherwise seasickness will be permanent!
in writing. − if we want to protect human health and at the same time strengthen the european manufacturing base, we need a sound compromise that makes noise reduction technically possible. a reduction of 3 to 4 db can be achieved within the next six years. these values are a major improvement and ensure that our companies are able to compete effectively and sustainably in global competition.
in writing. the european internal market is an area without internal frontiers in which the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital must be ensured. since road vehicles are the main means of transport and the main source of noise in the transport sector, it is important to take measures to regulate them without delay. the european union already applies type-approval criteria in co2 emissions legislation, in particular regulation (ec) no 715/2007 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 june 2007 on the type-approval of motor vehicles with respect to emissions from passenger cars and light commercial vehicles. the problem with these vehicles is not just the particulate matter. noise from traffic also causes health damage in many ways. given that the type and quality of the road surface also influence road traffic noise emissions, it is therefore necessary to adopt a comprehensive european approach which takes into account the acoustic performance of the road surface.
in writing. the european parliament voted today on a draft report on new noise standards for cars, lorries and buses. the objective of reducing ambient noise by lowering noise limit values and introducing a new and refined test method for measuring noise emissions is important for the protection of the environment and public health. i have, however, opposed amendment no 51 which imposes radical reduction measures (a reduction of 5 decibels), which are unrealistic and not necessary for public health. such a decline could in particular jeopardise belgium's status as a manufacturing centre. i am in favour of a balanced decision which moves towards protecting the environment and public health and incorporates economic factors, without neglecting the job losses which this could cause in some countries if manufacturers were to go bankrupt or move elsewhere.
in writing. - i am disappointed that we did not find a majority today to tighten up the noise standards for motor vehicles. traffic noise is harmful to health, yet since the 1990s noise standards have not been tightened. today a majority of the european parliament once again turned a deaf ear to the car lobby. this is bad news for europeans who are exposed to traffic noise. public health should always take precedence over the interests of the car industry. unfortunately, a majority of conservatives think otherwise. according to the european environment agency, half of the eu population in urban areas is exposed to intolerable traffic noise. noise pollution from traffic kills 50,000 europeans every year. meanwhile, traffic and noise continue to increase. the reduction of car noise has been opposed by the car lobby for years, including during these negotiations. the commission has already proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to noise. it is clear who is defending the general interest in this house and who is defending the short-term interests of a particular sector of industry.
in writing. the main objective of the commission proposal for a regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles is to protect public health and the environment by means of measures to reduce the noise emitted by these vehicles. the aim is to introduce a new test method for measuring noise emissions and new noise limit values for different categories of light, medium and heavy vehicles. i agree with the general approach of this proposal, which is a step forward in counteracting the effects of noise emissions from motor vehicles on public health and the environment. i am very sorry, however, that the commission's present proposal does not give sufficient emphasis to the information given to consumers on the noise level of motor vehicles. i would, for example, be in favour of introducing a system of labelling of vehicle noise emissions, in order to promote low-noise vehicles and to enable consumers to make an informed choice before buying a vehicle.
in writing. the economic and financial crisis has had a serious impact on the public finances of many member states. while most of them have had to take drastic measures to reduce their debt levels and budget deficits in order to put public finances on a sustainable path, some countries have been hit so badly that they have had to resort to the union's financial support mechanisms. due to their serious economic situation, those member states have encountered problems in meeting the co-financing requirements required to receive union funds. this is particularly the case with regard to funds allocated under the general programme 'solidarity and management of migration flows'. the commission is proposing to increase the co-financing rates for member states benefiting from a financial support mechanism. the proposal aims to increase the rate of union co-financing by 20 percentage points and to reduce the co-financing needs of the member states concerned by the same amount. the co-financing rate would thus be increased to 70%.
in writing. i am generally in favour of proposals to increase the co-financing rate for member states receiving financial assistance. the purpose of the fund is to create a solidarity mechanism between member states for the management of migration flows. this task is not shared equally between member states; it is therefore justified to re-evaluate the co-financing requirements in the light of the current economic challenges. good management of migration flows is of great importance for the european union as a whole. the failure of a single member state to manage these flows effectively has an impact not only on that member state but also on many other member states.
in writing. to make fishing sustainable, it is imperative to take account of its resources and thus avoid depleting fish stocks. to achieve this, alongside the reformed common fisheries policy, certain technical measures must be taken. to ensure the sustainable development of this sector, all fishermen must comply with the standards for the equipment used. it must also fish according to the zones and closure periods. last but not least, special attention must be paid to the protection of marine fauna; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fish stocks are not depleted. the best possible result will be achieved by respecting the marine environment and the rules governing fishing. the key to this is to take account of the rules and to implement them.

in writing. violence against women and girls worldwide, especially in armed conflicts, requires the creation of a genuine 'humanity project'. in the age of globalization, we can no longer afford to leave so many human beings on the margins of our consciousness. globalization is in dire need of universalism. history will judge us by our actions and our silence. no one can say they didn't know. democracy is never bought. we must preserve it. no one is immune to the north or south. it's not about development or economic wealth. it's about values, public liberties and respect for others. we must fight against all forms of impunity, corruption, trivialization and criminality.
