in writing. the european union is facing an unprecedented demographic challenge. it is not without reason that 2012 has been designated as the european year of active ageing. in view of the ageing of the population, appropriate measures must be taken to enable older people to develop in an appropriate environment. a 'society for all ages' must be created, both socially, economically and culturally. to be able to remain active, independent and healthy, one needs, of course, adequate infrastructure and easy access to services, but also an ecological environment, a social and cultural life, etc. a person who lives in an environment where he has everything he needs is a person who remains dynamic, independent and healthy. it is because it takes these different aspects into account that i voted in favour of the european innovation partnership for active and healthy ageing.
in writing. in my view, the demographic transition europe is going through should not be underestimated. its population is ageing rapidly and the number of people aged 65 or over will almost double from 85 million in 2008 to 151 million in 2060. in addition, while 20% of the population was at least 60 years old in 2010, this percentage will rise to at least 35% by 2050. recent projections, however, predict that immigration could slow down the process of population ageing. they are based on the assumption that several eu member states will ease their immigration restrictions in order to avoid major imbalances in the economic dependency ratio of older people. without migration, the population of the european union will fall from 495 million to 416 million by 2060, while the economic dependency ratio of older people will fall from 25 to 62%. with migration, the population could increase by up to 506 million people, while the economic dependency ratio of the elderly would reach "only" 53%.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution which affirms the position to be taken by the eu at the 16th conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). we call for an end to the systematic use of secret ballot which undermines efforts to stop the poaching of african elephants and rhinos. this is the only way to guarantee transparency and accountability in the decision-making process. in this resolution we call on the parties to cites to step up the fight against poaching of elephants for their ivory and of rhinoceroses for their horns. i also want to see several shark species included in the list of animals whose trade must be controlled, and that the cites agenda gives greater prominence to the fate of polar bears, which are increasingly endangered because of the melting of the arctic ice.
in writing. cites aims to ensure that international trade in wildlife does not threaten the survival of species in the wild. at present, large areas of land, particularly in africa, which are designated for environmental protection, are beyond the control of the state, its sovereignty and its security. these lands, and their natural resources, are the scene of subversive or criminal activities. if nothing is done to prevent this, the situation will worsen and will have disastrous consequences for the environment and stability of many countries. much of this land is located on international borders, making it easy for criminals to do their work. the third element of this interconnection is security. we are facing a global challenge that we cannot meet alone. there is an urgent need to take action and make the protection of animals and natural resources a priority. we need a deliberate, firm and proactive european policy, followed by decisive action. we must act now, before it's too late.

in writing. many member states are currently experiencing economic and budgetary difficulties. in the interests of solidarity, the european institutions should limit their administrative budget. nevertheless, it is vital that these cuts do not in any way hamper the proper functioning of the institutions, because the european budget is the only tool capable of strengthening european competitiveness and reviving growth. if savings can be made in the areas of translation, interpretation, computer technology, travel, respect for established budgets is imperative. let us not forget that this budget is money for europeans (e.g. erasmus, the cohesion funds, etc.). as the members have said, the way in which the european institutions operate must be optimized. i also believe that new own resources are needed, particularly through the introduction of the international financial transaction tax.
in writing. the guidelines report will send a key political message about the european parliament's expectations for the 2014 administrative budgets, with particular attention to the ep's own budget. parliament's priorities for 2014 in this area are budgetary responsibility and self-discipline, the continuation of the limitation or freezing of administrative budgets in compliance with legal obligations, the need to develop investment and strengthen interinstitutional cooperation. the key priorities for the 2014 budget are increasing efficiency through further structural and organisational reforms, and launching innovative thinking to find new areas of potential economies.
in writing. − this report goes hand in hand with the report on promoting the interests of society and a path to sustainable and inclusive recovery. both strengthen corporate social responsibility (csr). this provides for the promotion, enforcement and monitoring of social and environmental standards by enterprises. it not only contributes to the europe 2020 strategy by promoting sustainable growth, safeguarding jobs and revitalising the economy, but also helps to mitigate the social consequences of the financial and economic crisis. in particular, i welcome the call for businesses to retain as much freedom of action as possible despite the mandatory and voluntary approaches and for measures to avoid imposing administrative or financial burdens on smes. i also welcome the promotion of innovative solutions that enable businesses to tackle social and environmental challenges, such as intelligent transport systems and environmentally friendly products. corporate social responsibility has a multifaceted positive impact, because it benefits not only the company by increasing trust and social acceptance, but also its employees and society as a whole by promoting social cohesion.
in writing. corporate social responsibility (csr) is not a new or outdated concept. after a slight modernization, it can greatly help businesses to regain confidence in the economy battered by the crisis. if they incorporate this principle into their sustainability strategy, everyone will benefit. in addition, in order to encourage companies to take on this responsibility, it is imperative that they avoid unnecessary administrative, bureaucratic and financial burdens. in the same vein, it is essential to improve the transparency and effectiveness of csr policies. it is also necessary to make companies as aware as possible of csr and the consequences of non-compliance. however, csr should not be overused as a marketing tool, but should be integrated into the strategies of companies, which must be subject to codes of good conduct in order to enjoy better market identification. voting for this resolution is another step towards economic recovery in europe.
in writing. the growing recognition of corporate 'social responsibility' can be interpreted and read in several ways. on the one hand, the process of globalisation and the emergence of 'global' markets are fostering the emergence of social and environmental standards within companies; on the other hand, an increasingly attentive and informed civil society is 'calling' for more responsible behaviour on the part of companies. the dual impulse driving the advancement of csr in an international governance system, which some have described as post-national, reflects the complementarity of interests between business and society in general. it is therefore appropriate to adopt a broader and farsighted approach in this respect, in order to exploit the full potential of csr. i am not inclined to accept an approach to csr which assumes that business takes over the primary functions of government in promoting, implementing and monitoring social and environmental standards. csr should be guided primarily by the enterprises themselves, according to their own possibilities and requirements, and supported, as appropriate, by the public authorities, in order to balance the interests of enterprises and society.
in writing. although there have been marked improvements, many european companies have not yet fully integrated social and environmental concerns into their activities and strategy, which undermine labour rights and human rights in general. only 15 out of 27 countries promote csr, which is a very interesting fact. however, before inviting all member states to follow the csr path, it would be wise for them to apply, as a first step, the fundamental principles of the international labour organisation, such as the elimination of all forms of forced or compulsory labour and the effective abolition of child labour. secondly, the european union must set an example if it is to get its member states to act accordingly: it must stop dealing with countries that blatantly violate labour and human rights, and include clauses in its trade agreements to ensure that these rights are respected and then csr. in this way, in addition to restoring confidence between businesses and the economy, which has been damaged by the crisis, the fundamental rights of workers will be respected.
in writing. while it is wise to guard against the accusation of 'eco-whitening', csr should be seen as an opportunity to be seized and not as a threat to the competitiveness of enterprises. it is also part of europe's own 'social licence' to pursue trade-driven growth. the short-term thinking in brussels, which focuses exclusively on transparency, accountability and accountability of financial markets alone would also reproduce the same mistakes of which those responsible for the collapse of the banking system are accused. the report calls on responsible companies to demonstrate their active commitment to mitigating the social consequences of the crisis and by launching a number of csr actions: job creation for young people, health at work, sustainability of pensions, promotion of the 'minimum living wage', combating labour exploitation practices in business supply chains and promoting new markets for socially and environmentally useful products and services.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the report by david casa (epp, malta) on the proposal for a directive presented by the commission in july 2012 to amend the vat directive with a view to establishing a rapid reaction mechanism (rrm) against vat fraud. the directive is intended to allow a member state faced with a sudden and massive case of vat fraud to take emergency measures, which it is not allowed to do at present under vat legislation, unless it obtains a derogation after a lengthy process. an accelerated procedure would allow them to be granted a temporary derogation of up to one year within one month. this effective and pragmatic measure will help to combat vat fraud and will strengthen efforts to combat tax evasion and avoidance. we are, however, asking that the proposal be accompanied by a long-term strategy to combat fraud which implies more structural changes in vat regimes and that, as far as possible, the constraints on businesses should not be increased.
in writing. tax evasion is currently a recurring problem within the european union. vat fraud is harmful to companies that comply with their obligations and costs the union and national budgets several billion euros each year. in this time of budgetary constraints and austerity, action is needed. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution to standardize vat legislation and, above all, to establish a rapid reaction mechanism against this fraud. the current approaches to tackling this are time-consuming and cumbersome, which makes it difficult to take the necessary measures in a timely manner. this resolution will enable member states to react more quickly and effectively to vat fraud and also brings real added value to the union.
in writing. vat fraud costs the european union and national budgets several billion euros a year. in some serious cases, huge sums of money are lost in a very short time, because of the speed with which fraud mechanisms are evolving today. between june 2008 and december 2009, for example, an estimated €5 billion was lost as a result of vat fraud in the context of greenhouse gas emission allowance trading. currently, if a member state wishes to combat vat fraud by measures not provided for in eu vat legislation, it must formally request a derogation to do so. the commission then draws up a proposal and submits it to the council, which must adopt it unanimously before the measure can be implemented. this procedure can be time-consuming and cumbersome. it prevents the member state concerned from taking the necessary measures in time to put an end to the fraud. the rapid response mechanism would mean that member states would no longer have to wait for this formal procedure to be completed before applying anti-fraud measures.
in writing. in the context of the vote on this report, i took the opportunity to strongly condemn the position adopted at the last european council in february on the 2013 budget, which is to artificially reduce the level of payment appropriations available in the union budget. i am very sorry about that, because the union budget is first and foremost an investment budget, and 94% of the resources that go into it are reinjected into the member states.
in writing. the euro area is currently experiencing a double-dip recession caused by excessive debt and the financial crisis. in the european union, more than 8 million people have already lost their jobs since 2008, more than 25 million europeans are currently unemployed, of whom almost 11 million have been unemployed for more than a year, around 10 million young people are now unemployed and in the past year alone 2 million people lost their jobs. in addition, labour market regulations in some member states do not leave the necessary flexibility to absorb shocks such as the current crisis. i believe that growth-friendly fiscal consolidation is necessary to get out of the crisis. i therefore welcome the draft provisions of the second set of measures to strengthen the economic dialogue and the overall control of the european semester process by the national parliaments and the european parliament. i also believe that member states should pursue differentiated strategies according to their budgetary situation and that they should keep the growth of public expenditure below the rate of gdp growth in the medium term;
in writing. the socialist group strongly criticised the austerity policies imposed by the european commission on certain member states at risk of or suffering from serious financial instability. we strongly support the conclusions of the annual independent growth review (eaic) that these policies are counterproductive and cannot bring growth back to europe. the eaic proposes instead to slow down the pace of adjustment, within the limits of the revised stability and growth pact (the 'economic governance' package), as this strategy is likely to free up up to €80 billion per year for growth and job creation policies. the commission must change its position on the annual growth review. europe is currently experiencing zero growth and the 0.1% forecast by the commission does not represent real growth. how long will the commission and the eu member states simply wait and watch the devastating effects of these austerity policies? the international monetary fund (imf) recently revised down its growth forecasts, a clear sign that europe is heading for a wall.
in writing. i welcome the vote on this report. i would like to point out, however, that in anticipation of the vote i asked the commission to put in place the necessary monitoring mechanisms to ensure that the member states implement the social recommendations made in the context of the european semester and the national reform programme.
in writing. − the two reports on social and economic policy aspects in the annual growth survey are very welcome, as they analyse the impact of the european semester. the latter is an important step in overcoming the consequences of the financial and economic crisis. the consequences are devastating: since 2008, more than 8 million eu citizens have lost their jobs, and 25 million are currently unemployed. the unemployment rate is 10 million, and young people are the main victims. urgent measures are examined in the context of the annual growth report. this balance sheet is important in order to draw conclusions for future action. i particularly welcome the call for growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, because it is an efficient way out of the crisis. in particular in times of crisis, not only should there be budgetary discipline with high-quality monitoring and evaluation of public finances, but also, and above all, investments in sustainable growth. i support, among other things, the call to make national labour markets more adaptable, competitive and dynamic. this should be achieved by measures to create jobs, such as the creation of employment incentives and the promotion of self-employment and entrepreneurship. if we look closely at how we can deal with the still-ongoing consequences of the economic and financial crisis and draw conclusions for the future, then we can actually use this crisis as an opportunity.
in writing. the social and employment situation has deteriorated sharply over the past 12 months, and the outlook for 2013 is not very encouraging. the unemployment rate has never been higher. the union now has more than 25 000 000 unemployed. this wave of unemployment is particularly affecting young people. it is imperative that member states address this situation and make youth unemployment and the resulting poverty their top priorities. to do this, various measures must be taken. in these times of austerity, fiscal consolidation is inevitable, but given its negative impact on growth and employment, it is necessary to adjust it according to the country concerned.
in writing. the european parliament calls on the european finance ministers to finally make use of the flexibility in the budgetary rules. the eu needs to make room as soon as possible to invest in jobs and to tackle the growing poverty in the eu. that's a good thing. unemployment reached a record high due to the continuing recession. it is time to review the austerity policy. when heads of government decide on their economic policies for 2013 in march, the focus should shift from short-term austerity to room for investment in jobs and reforms to green the economy. unfortunately, the green proposal to no longer base european economic policy on the infamous 3% standard but to take account of income equality and labour force participation was almost rejected by the right-wing groups. this is a missed opportunity to make european economic policy more socially oriented. it could have reversed the trend of declining support for european economic policy. the liberals and christian democrats are demonstrating that they do not have a coherent vision of how to tackle the crisis.
in writing. the social and employment situation has worsened since the last eac in 2012, and the outlook for 2013 is pessimistic. in the last 12 months, the number of unemployed has risen by 2 million to over 25 million in the european union (10.5% of the working age population). fragmentation of the labour market has continued to increase, long-term unemployment has reached worrying levels, average household incomes are declining in many member states and indicators point to higher levels and more acute forms of poverty and social exclusion, with an increase in workers' poverty and social polarisation in many member states. progress towards the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy has been disappointing.
in writing. − this report identifies remaining obstacles to the single market and proposes concrete solutions. i particularly welcome the following three demands: firstly, the call for better legislation, including increased voting in the preparation of legislative proposals affecting the internal market; secondly, better implementation, enforcement and enforcement, including through the introduction of correlation tables reflecting national transposition of eu rules; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied in a fair and transparent manner. the specific recommendations are very sensible. they build on each other, thereby promoting the provision and use of crossborder services and the mobility of labour, and dissolving existing boundary effects, whether of a purely technical or administrative nature. one example among many is the increased use of online tools or internal market information systems in cross-border cooperation between administrations within the third recommendation. finally, i would like to stress the importance of regular monitoring of the implementation and application of the internal market rules in the context of the european semester, which should also include the establishment of a single european transport area.
in writing. in the current economic crisis, the single market needs to be completed as quickly as possible in order to stimulate growth, competitiveness and job creation. without growth, europe loses all credibility, without solidarity, it loses all legitimacy. the european contract for growth is simple: it is a question of activating all possible levers to allow a vigorous and sustainable recovery of growth, a necessary condition to support our social systems. the single market has a key role to play in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. as a result of the efforts made by the commission and the member states, the average transposition deficit now stands at 0.9%, thanks to the progress made in recent months; whereas further efforts will have to be made as the deficits lead to mistrust of the union in general and of the single market in particular; it is important to encourage the rapid development of the single market if the commission's estimates that eu gdp could grow by 4% over the next ten years are to be realised.
in writing. we know the impact of european market harmonisation on our economy and on our citizens. the single market is the lever for growth and development in the european union. however, i welcome the schwab report which aims to create a coherent framework for european market governance. the role of the single market and consumer protection needs to be strengthened more than ever. and it is precisely to consumers that we must turn, to design this role first with the input of citizens and workers. as a socialist and rapporteur for the modernisation of public procurement, i will continue to call for the respect of social rights within the single market to play a full role in economic and social recovery, which will prevent social dumping and ensure working conditions for all europeans on the basis of the principle of equal treatment of workers. the increased democratic accountability of the european semester through the role of the european parliament and national parliaments, as well as increased dialogue with the social partners, go in the right direction to achieve the market model we want.

in writing. i supported this resolution to underline the importance of the debates of the 22nd session of the un human rights council. i would like to stress in particular the negative impact of the economic and financial crisis and corruption on the exercise of human rights. the importance of the european union's even more active participation in the united nations human rights mechanisms cannot be overemphasized.

in writing. the european investment bank currently plays a key role in shaping the future of the european union and in achieving its objectives of growth and jobs. the competitiveness of our trading partners is constantly growing, and the union must be able to cope with this. to this end, measures must be taken at different levels. from a financial point of view, it is imperative that the eib maintains its triple a status and to do so it must seek to increase its capital. the eib also has to make the right choices in terms of internal and external priorities. cultural activities, for example, deserve more attention. the latter have been severely penalized following the financial crisis. finally, it is essential that the european investment bank should always be more transparent. by voting for this resolution, which includes these various measures, we are putting all the chances in our hands to achieve these objectives.
in writing. − in its annual report on the european investment bank (eib), the european parliament calls for financing of green investments. the eib's lending to projects that are harmful to the environment, climate or developing countries must be stopped quickly. the eib's mission is to contribute to the eu's climate and development objectives. but the practice is quite different. it's time we looked at that a lot more critically. in 2011, the eib froze loans to the trading company glencore, whose subsidiary was involved in corruption, tax evasion and serious pollution around a copper mine in zambia. we must learn from this scandal. never again should eib money be used for such abuses. the eib's transparency and accountability must be improved. the greens unfortunately did not receive support from other groups for a proposal to phase out polluting investments as quickly as possible. between 2007 and 2011, as much as 30% of eib energy budget lending went to fossil energy. unfortunately, too many politicians still believe that we can delay the choice of sustainability forever. this will come back to them like a boomerang.

in writing. in an age when the internet is at the forefront of many areas, this proposal seems quite legitimate to me. it aims to establish an online platform to help consumers and traders settle contractual disputes arising from the online sale of goods or services from one member state to another. by consulting this free website, both parties to the dispute will be informed of the remedies available to them. it would have been interesting to extend the scope of this platform to national disputes, but it is a good start. this website will save money, save time and strengthen the appeals process. voting for this proposal for online consumer dispute resolution is a first step towards a very promising tool.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to set up an interactive website offering consumers and traders a one-stop shop for the out-of-court settlement of contractual disputes arising from the cross-border online sale of goods or the provision of services by a trader established in one member state to a consumer resident in another member state. the appeals available to consumers should be strengthened by allowing their complaints to be submitted to an adr body (arbitration authority, conciliator, mediator or appeal board) for an out-of-court settlement. i particularly support the provision of voluntary adr systems in every sector of the economy to facilitate consumer access to and implementation of redress. i also welcome the fact that the proposal for a regulation applies to complaints from consumers, but also from traders.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report so that consumers who buy cross-border can be sure that they can get redress for problems they encounter with the products or services they have bought. the european commission has also published a report on the implementation of the european union's new rules on the protection of the environment. an out-of-court dispute settlement system must therefore give citizens the confidence to take full advantage of the benefits of electronic commerce. the aim is therefore to develop a solid framework for the development of consumer oer bodies. first, the lack of awareness of oer procedures among many consumers and professionals needs to be addressed. the harmonisation of quality criteria will subsequently enable consumers to have recourse to a quality, impartial, independent, fair and transparent odr procedure.
in writing. i voted in favour of my colleague's text. the partnership agreement between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) states and the eu and its member states (the cotonou agreement) provides a legal basis for eu cooperation with these states. the commission should clarify its strategy on promoting the private sector and the use of new provisions such as financing through a combination of grants and loans. the text calls on the european union to define a set of environmental and social standards to be respected in the proposals for public contracts financed by the european development fund (edf) in the acp countries. i also expect the commission to do everything in its power to ensure that the edf is budgeted smoothly from 1 january 2021. the commission must also keep the ep regularly informed of the progress of preparations. this budgetary integration should improve aid predictability but should not be used as a pretext for reducing development aid expenditure. the provisions on democratic control must guarantee the involvement of national parliaments in the monitoring of the expenditure of budget appropriations.

in writing. the presence and control of radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption is a public health issue serious enough for the european parliament to consider! i therefore welcome the adoption of this report which calls for the protection of human health and the environment from the harmful effects of radiation by the development of minimum standards and monitoring of radioactive contamination to ensure that more ambitious limits are applied throughout the eu for the concentrations of radioactive substances in drinking water. i also called for better information to be given to the public, who are often unaware of the risks of nuclear activities in their neighbourhood, for the polluter-pays principle to be applied in all member states, and for stricter contamination standards to take account of natural and man-made radioactivity and the affected populations in order to take better account of the critical populations, namely children, which will allow for a better assessment of the doses received by the population, contrary to the standards laid down by the european commission.
in writing. access to safe drinking water for all eu citizens is one of the main objectives of our policies on human health and environmental protection. at present, the quality of water intended for human consumption in europe is governed by the drinking water directive. unfortunately, some of its requirements are still being ignored. voting in favour of this new directive will help to overcome some of the difficulties we are facing today. it will make it possible to take account of all the adverse effects of the various pollutants. in addition, natural and man-made sources of radioactivity will be treated quite separately and the polluter pays principle will apply. the combination of new technologies and new measures will mean safe drinking water for all european citizens and increased protection of human health.
in writing. even if the proposal refers to the non-application of the drinking water directive, i agree with the author of the parliament's text that the approach taken by the commission is not satisfactory and needs to be changed in two key respects. access to safe drinking water for european citizens is a central concern of policies in the fields of human health and environmental protection. the quality of water intended for human consumption is currently covered by council directive 98/83/ec, including the regulation on pollutants such as toxic chemicals and radionuclides. however, the requirements for tritium control and total indicative dose have not yet been applied, while member states were required to comply with the drinking water directive by the end of 2003. with this proposal the commission intends to incorporate the corresponding requirements not in the said directive but in new specific legislation on the basis of the euratom treaty.

in writing. the commission proposal for a regulation lays down additional requirements for the surveillance of national budgetary policies, proposes a common budgetary timetable and calls for closer surveillance of budgetary decisions of member states subject to an excessive deficit procedure. i agree with the proposal. i believe, however, that the implementation of budgetary surveillance should always be conditional on the fundamental objectives of the union, and in particular on the provisions of article 9 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union aimed at promoting a high level of employment and ensuring adequate social protection.
in writing. - i am satisfied that the two-pack has been approved and is coming into effect soon. i also took note of the commission's statement. the epp has been campaigning for greater eu budgetary integration and monitoring to support member states in drawing up sustainable budgets, the basis for growth and jobs. the two-pack has profound implications for the national budgetary procedure in the euro area. the commission is now monitoring the budget not only ex post, but from the drafting stage onwards and can make preventive adjustments. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. the epp has incorporated the essentials of the budgetary treaty into the two-pack. independent bodies that monitor compliance with the numerical mto budget rules, correction mechanism, economic partnership programme and coordination of sovereign debt issuance plans. a group of experts shall report by march 2014 on the possibilities of partial replacement of national debt issuance by joint issuance in the form of a debt servicing fund or eurobonds. the epp has always been open to debate on this subject if it is taken seriously. the group of experts is taking care of it. it is politically wise that other groups, too, should now adopt a more gradual and realistic approach, with a loss of time.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation establishes a legal framework governing the possibility for various investment funds to obtain the designation 'european venture capital funds' and the corresponding passport. the aim is to create a european venture capital investment sector for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the proposal for a regulation lays down the criteria, in terms of available assets, which a given fund must meet in order to obtain the abovementioned designation and passport. it also introduces requirements for managers of such funds and restrictions on the investments that can be made with the assets of a fund. it should be noted that there are already two directives on investment funds: directive 2011/61/eu of the european parliament and of the council and directive 2009/65/ec of the european parliament and of the council. they contain rules on investment funds, their management and the status of investors in such funds. the purpose of this opinion is to ensure consistency between the proposal for a regulation and those legal instruments currently in force.
in writing. the social economy sector covers a very wide field and is constantly expanding. because of their roots and cultural heritage, its companies are at the heart of important social issues, such as social protection and equal opportunities. the training of the low-skilled, the integration of young people into working life, the transition from a precarious situation to the status of worker or entrepreneur appear to be common aspirations encountered by this sector. the specificities of social enterprises, whose main objective is to have a positive social impact, must therefore be taken into account. in addition, these are often smes, largely financed by grants from foundations, private individuals or the public sector. i share the objective of creating a legislative framework adapted to the needs of social enterprises, investors wishing to finance them and specialised investment funds acting as intermediaries between the two. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer.
in writing. more and more investors are looking for social objectives rather than just financial returns. a social investment market is therefore emerging in the union, which is composed in particular of funds targeting socially oriented enterprises. it is necessary to establish a common framework for the use of the designation 'european social entrepreneurship funds' (esefs), in particular as regards the composition of the portfolio of funds operating under that designation, their investment targets, the investment tools they may implement and the categories of investors that may invest in such funds, by laying down uniform rules at union level. in the absence of such a common framework, there is a risk that member states would take divergent measures at national level, which would have a direct negative impact on the internal market and would hamper its smooth functioning, as funds wishing to carry out cross-border activity would be subject to different rules in different member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by elisabeth morin-chartier on the impact of the crisis on gender equality and women's rights, which was adopted by 495 votes to 96, with 69 abstentions. parliament condemned the budget cuts and austerity measures which had further weakened the position of women. a real silent crisis for women! the resolution therefore insists that the crisis should not jeopardise the results achieved by policies to promote equality between men and women and should not serve as a pretext for reducing efforts in this area. we have asked the commission to integrate the gender dimension into all policies and in particular those concerning the impact of austerity measures. we have stressed that women have played a key role in the resistance to the crisis and that they must therefore be fully involved in the management of recovery plans. we also called for a directive to close the pay gap and for more investment in continuing training, teleworking, women's entrepreneurship and childcare.

member of the commission. − mr president, match fixing and corruption pose the greatest threats to european sport today, and the european commission is determined to do all it can to help the sports authorities tackle them. i am certainly aware of the involvement of organised criminal networks in the latest match-fixing scandal affecting professional football in europe. my services have been in contact with europol to discuss the case, and i welcome the action taken by europol so far. the commission adopted a recommendation for a council decision on the negotiation of a council of europe convention against the manipulation of sports competitions in november 2012. that recommendation calls on the member states to allow the commission to join them in the negotiations. we expect the council to adopt its negotiating directives in the near future. i believe that the convention, once adopted, will send a strong signal on europe’s determination to safeguard the integrity of sport. the convention should also be open for signature by non-european countries, thus addressing the global dimension of the problem. in order to ensure a comprehensive approach, all competent commission services are now working closely together to ensure consistency with the eu acquis on criminal law, data protection and the internal market. as the recent announcement made by europol shows, the involvement of law enforcement agencies, and notably their cooperation at eu level, is essential to combat the threat of match fixing. these latest cases of match-fixing are likely to require close coordination among judicial authorities involved in criminal investigation and prosecution. the competent authorities will be able to rely on eurojust for the practical coordination of cross-border prosecution, but also on a whole range of instruments adopted in the field of judicial cooperation, including the european arrest warrant. however, policing and prosecution are only one part of the solution. in order to be effective, the fight against match fixing needs to include preventive measures as well. i am glad to inform you that, under the 2012 preparatory actions for sport, the commission selected five projects in the area of match-fixing. these projects will help to educate the relevant actors and raise awareness about the problem within both the sports movement and the general public. work on these five projects started at the beginning of 2013, and results are expected in the first half of 2014. the coordinators of the projects are working together to achieve synergies and common strategies. the outcome of the projects will help us to spread good practices and strengthen networks. i would also like to add that i am working closely with my colleague, commissioner barnier, to address the problem of match-fixing from the angle of sports betting. on 23 november 2012, the commission adopted an action plan on online gambling, which included a chapter on the integrity of sport. one of the actions proposed by the commission is a recommendation to be adopted in 2014. the recommendation will encourage a more efficient exchange of good practices in the prevention and combating of betting-related match fixing. the commission therefore intends to involve all the relevant stakeholders in this process. the results of the 2012 preparatory actions will also provide useful input. other initiatives such as studies, workshops and expert meetings will gather evidence and inform the drafting of the recommendation. finally, on 5 february 2013, the commission adopted a proposal to review the eu’s anti-money laundering directive. in the light of concerns that the gambling sector is vulnerable to money laundering, the commission has proposed to broaden the scope of the directive beyond casinos to cover the whole gambling sector. given the evolution of money laundering risks, it is important that the eu framework is able to respond in a robust but also flexible way.

in writing. given the current economic conditions, all actors in our society need access to independent, reliable, comparable and timely data to be able to monitor and assess the economic reality. this is the main objective of this regulation. based on the latest revision of the un system of national accounts, it aims to establish the rules to be applied for the collection and publication of basic macroeconomic data in the eu. the aim of this regulation is to ensure automated methods of real-time data collection, maximum transparency of public sector activities, limitation of derogations to the strict minimum in order to give a clear and complete picture, etc. this regulation on the european system of national and regional accounts in the eu will make it easier for us all to know precisely where we stand in economic terms.

in writing. − it is important to define the distribution of seats in the european parliament after 2014. i do welcome the fact that the basis for the new distribution of seats is the principle of 'no one wins, no one loses' when more than one seat has been won. nevertheless, this calculation results in some member states, including belgium, losing an important seat in the eu parliament. it is therefore important that at national level the loss of a seat does not restrict the principle that particularly small countries should be represented in accordance with their national structure, i.e. the regions. the loss of a seat should not lead to the minorities of each member state having to give up their seat, so that diversity is preserved not only within europe but also within the member states and their regions.
in writing. due to the accession of croatia to the eu, the number of seats allocated to some member states will have to be revised. according to the eu treaty, the representation of citizens in the ep must be degressively proportional. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. the latter includes a reduction of one, two or three seats for 13 member states. in this new scenario, belgium is again facing a decline in seats, whereas it was already the case a few years ago, and some large eu member states are passing through the net. in politics there are rarely positive solutions in all respects. you always have a choice between a very bad solution and a not-so-bad one. here i chose the least bad. i must say that it was impossible to find a better solution.
in writing. article 14 (2) of the lisbon treaty sets the number of meps at 751, with effect from the next elections to the european parliament. it introduces a maximum of 96 seats and a minimum of 6 seats per member state and requires that the allocation of these seats among member states be based on the principle of degressive proportionality. the european parliament currently has 754 meps (plus the president). there will be 766 with the accession of croatia. as a result, this number must be reduced to 15 before next year's elections. the treaty states that the change is to be decided unanimously by the european council on the basis of a proposal from the european parliament. the gualtieri-trzaskowski report is the european parliament's draft proposal. a strict mathematical application of the principle of degressive proportionality would result in heavy losses for small and mediumsized member states and gains for larger ones. the draft proposal is therefore based on the principle that 'no one loses or gains more than one seat', while respecting as far as possible the principle of degressive proportionality.
in writing. i did not support this afternoon horst schnellhardt's proposal to reject the harmonized definition of absinthe liqueur proposed by the commission. it's impossible for me to understand his arguments. or rather, i understand them too well. the rejection of the compromise which the council reached almost unanimously actually allows those in europe who usurp the name to continue to sell liquors of any kind under the name of absinthe. in the interests of transparency, the commission wanted the consumer to be clearly informed. the absinthe label is used for liqueur from artemisia absinthum, and all other labels for flavoured liqueurs from other plants. logic, would you say? yes, and the approach taken to fruit juices (name matching the content), or in the great "vodka quarrel". the same german rapporteur, curiously enough, had then insisted that vodkas made from something other than cereals or potatoes should bear the indication. two weights, two measures. he has just convinced parliament that absinthe can be sold to the consumer with impunity without... absinthe. it's very strong, isn't it? a whole traditional sector has just been robbed of its rightful claim to value. that's too bad.
in writing. we vetoed the proposal to define absinthe in european legislation on wednesday. according to a majority of them, producers of certain traditional varieties of absinthe could no longer use the term 'absinthe' or would be forced to change their recipes. this iconic and controversial drink, dubbed the "green fairy", is said to have fueled the creativity of artists in the early 20th century, when it was banned in many countries. at present, there is no clear definition of this alcohol in european legislation. however, not all traditional absinthe recipes in the union require a minimum level of anethole. producers say that traditional practices vary according to regional availability of herbs and plants, as well as consumer tastes, for example in sugar. we voted against the definition and put an end to the control procedure which was in force. if we want to introduce a definition of absinthe into european law, the european commission should present a new proposal.

in writing. - agriculture faces major challenges and to meet them it is useful to define the framework for the future common agricultural policy (cap). in addition to the proposal on direct payments, the package for the future of the cap includes three other proposals, which i also welcome, because all three are intended to lead to a more sustainable, more transparent, less administrative and more efficient agriculture. the aim of direct payments must be to achieve a more targeted and more equitable distribution of payments. agricultural financing is a key element of the eu budget and thus of the mff negotiations. the aim is to achieve profitable food production, sustainable management of natural resources and climate protection measures. they are particularly important today, with the numerous food scandals, and they promote local food production and quality improvement. i am particularly pleased that young farmers are to be given more support and that a special scheme is foreseen for small farmers.
in writing. the time for reform has not yet come for the common agricultural policy. the pressure cooker of the experts on the committee on agriculture has worked well, to the detriment of medium and small farms. the ceiling for direct aid is fixed, but it is set at eur 300 000. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the farmers' incomes are not affected by the increase in the number of farmers. applied to the size of belgium, this "reform" is even more questionable: 46 farms, or 0.01% of the total, receive more than €300,000 of european subsidies annually. and of course, there is an exception for agricultural cooperatives. that is why i was one of the 113 members who supported a cap of €100,000 per farm to make the system more equitable. this would have enabled more than 10 500 farms in belgium, for example, to benefit from european aid. the proposal to give a supplementary premium for the first hectares was also not supported. the policy of "small steps" is to be content with, the consideration of returns on scale and the employment of employees in the holding. this is not good news for most farmers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this opening. in line with the europe 2020 strategy to promote resource efficiency for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in eu agricultural and rural areas, the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) sets the following specific objectives: sustainable food production; sustainable management of natural resources with climate action; balanced territorial development to maintain the two pillars of the cap, namely pillar i or the direct payment regulation, covering direct payments and market-related measures providing support for farmers' annual income, with a safety net in the event of market instability, and pillar ii or the rural development regulation, covering rural development in regions where member states draw up multiannual programmes and participate in their financing.

in writing. − this report deals with the european parliament’s position regarding the commission communication on future eu energy policy up to 2050. it backs the commission’s finding that res (renewable energy sources) and ee (energy efficiency) are ‘no regret’ options. it also notes that since massive investments are required even under a ‘business as usual’ scenario, it is preferable to use them to modernise and develop our energy system towards a decarbonised future. our shadow rapporteur calls for a clear statement from the european parliament indicating that we want to see clear support for a high renewable and energy efficiency scenario. moreover, unacceptable sections of the report should be removed, such as the call for the commission to actively promote nuclear energy and discussion of scenarios for increased dependence on nuclear energy and gas.

in writing. − nuclear power plants in the eu should be subject to regular risk and safety assessments. accidents at nuclear power stations are a huge threat not only to the member state concerned but also to neighbouring countries. this is all the more so because of the tendency to build nuclear power stations in border regions. i very much welcome this resolution, which strengthens crossborder cooperation in this area. as early as 2011, i had already drawn attention to the importance of coordinating emergency plans between neighbouring countries, and therefore i am very pleased that it is now called for, among other things, to study external emergency and prevention measures, especially for cross-border areas in the eu, by 2013 and to publish the results by the end of 2014. it also recommends that the competent authorities cooperate more closely across borders and that there should be a cross-border exchange of experts and best practice. crossborder cooperation and coordination in this area are essential. i therefore particularly welcome the fact that people living within 50 km of a nuclear power plant should be taken into account and that, where a majority of the residents in the neighbouring country are concerned, the relevant national authorities of that neighbouring country should be involved in all national and regional decisions relating to the nuclear power plant.

in writing. i welcome the vote on this report, which comes at the same time as the world health organisation (who) is publishing a comprehensive scientific assessment of the endocrine disruptors issue. the report confirms that many endocrine disorders and diseases are on the rise, including breast and prostate cancers, infertility and reproductive problems (lower sperm quality in men, early puberty in girls), diabetes and obesity, and neurological diseases (attention deficit disorder, parkinson's disease). i have been trying to sound the alarm for over 15 years, so i can only congratulate the european parliament and the who for finally looking at this health time bomb of endocrine disruptors. i also had the opportunity to express my total disagreement with the attempts by some to introduce the 'activity' criterion as the threshold for the definition of endocrine disruptors, because this approach would unduly limit the definition of disruptors and would not be in line with the classification of carcinogens, mutagens and reproductive toxicants, which is based on solid evidence! let us keep as vigilant as possible on this vital issue!
in writing. in the last twenty years, we have seen an increase in human diseases and hormonal disorders. since our genes could not change in such a short time, external factors, such as lifestyle, diet, medication, chemicals, and so forth, are the cause. since health protection is a key element of european union policy, it is imperative that the precautionary principle is fully applied. endocrine disruptors play an important role in the worrying trend observed and, due to their ubiquity, it is impossible for the population to protect itself against them. it is more than necessary to do everything possible to increase the protection of public health and especially that of children, young people and women, who are considered to be the most vulnerable groups. this resolution is a step in the right direction by revising all relevant legislation to include, in particular, clauses on chemical substances specifically applicable to textile products, which are often in contact with children.
in writing. endocrine disruptors, chemicals that are particularly common in our daily lives, were the main neglected substances in the reach regulation on chemicals adopted in 2006. this is a regrettable omission, as more and more scientific voices are speaking out against the dangers of these substances, which are associated with genital malformations and the high rate of hormone-dependent cancers, such as prostate and breast cancers, early puberty in girls, and so on. in turn, we are exposed to them through our diet, our breathing, and our skin, since they are found mainly in cosmetics (parabens), plastics (bisphenol a and phthalates), and detergents (alkylphenols). and apart from the ban on bisphenol a in baby bottles and certain phthalates in toys, endocrine disruptors continue to circulate freely. for all these reasons, and also to send a clear message to the commission which is currently working on a definition of the ptbs, this afternoon's vote on the westlund report is important. it stresses in particular the urgency of introducing toxicity tests which take account of particularly vulnerable periods of development such as pregnancy.
in writing. i support this report for several reasons. first, precautionary measures to protect human health should be implemented where there is a reasonable likelihood of adverse effects from endocrine disruptors. the criteria used to define endocrine disruption should be based on comprehensive hazard assessments, supported by the latest scientific developments and taking into account potential combinations and long-term effects. from this point of view, the hazard assessment should form the basis for risk assessment and risk management measures. the commission is then invited to carry out a systematic review of all relevant legislation and, if necessary, to amend existing legislation or to submit new legislative proposals by june 2015 to reduce it to endocrine disrupting chemicals. endocrine disruptors should be considered as 'substances without threshold effect' unless the producers provide scientific evidence of the presence of a threshold below which no harmful effect occurs. the commission is also asked to develop methodologies to minimise animal testing.

in writing. after rising almost fivefold in two years to over $2 a pound in the spring of 2011, world cotton prices have collapsed again to 75 cents a pound as of january 4, 2013. this sharp decline is again putting at risk the cotton sector in west and central africa, where white gold is the main export crop, the lifeblood of their economies and development efforts. between the early 1980s and the late 2000s, the continuous fall in prices caused a sharp decline in production in the acp countries, with farmers gradually turning away from this less and less lucrative crop. then, in early 2010, the trend reversed abruptly and the prices rose sharply. mainly linked to demand from the chinese manufacturing sector and to special weather conditions, this price increase was truly staggering, reaching the highest levels not seen since the civil war. the volatility of the markets is a scourge that must be firmly fought.

member of the commission. − mr president, firstly i would like to thank parliament and its rapporteur for its very good cooperation on this file. i think that the way we have progressed here is very good. emissions from international aircraft represent a rapidly growing contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions. yet, after nearly two decades of negotiations, there has been no internationally-agreed principle on who has the responsibility – and who has the authority – to control emissions from international flights. this is a problem, not only because of the emissions themselves, but also – as mr liese has just stated – for reasons of fairness. how can we explain to our citizens that we are taking measures to reduce emissions from their use of cars, transport or the heating of their house, farms or whatever it is, if at the same time we do nothing about the very significant emissions every passenger causes when taking an intercontinental flight? it simply does not make sense. that is why, years ago, the european union decided to include aviation in our emissions trading system. we did so after the un’s aviation body, icao, had given their endorsement after they could not themselves agree to move on. if you wanted to move on nationally or regionally, it should be through some kind of emissions trading scheme. that was one of the options that they actually pointed to. when they realised that the eu was actually serious about acting – when we started to include emissions in our scheme – many third countries seemed to have second thoughts about this idea. but the fact is that the european union has always made it clear that a global approach to addressing the fast-growing emissions from international aviation is our preferred option. nobody has worked harder actually to achieve that than we have in the european union. that is why, based on the encouraging results of the icao council meeting of 9 november 2012 and the constructive engagement of our international partners in the relevant discussions, the commission proposed that the eu ‘stop the clock’ by temporarily derogating from the eu ets compliance obligations for international flights operated in 2012 to and from europe. this significant gesture by the eu would create a unique window of opportunity for the icao process. many states have called for action to be taken at international level through icao and argued that the ets was an obstacle in this respect. so now we can make it abundantly clear to everybody that this is not the case and show that it is now up to our partners to work with us and to demonstrate a genuine commitment to, and an engagement in, finding solutions. the icao assembly in september 2013 will need to take the international efforts to the next level in order to demonstrate that the icao’s member states are ready to take appropriate measures in the area of international aviation. in 2010 the icao assembly agreed to an aspirational goal of carbon neutral growth by 2020. the industry (iata) has adopted this goal and set itself a target of 50% emission reductions from 2005 levels by 2050. however, all trajectories show that, without market-based measures, these targets will be missed. in fact, a business-as-usual scenario suggests an increase of 400% by 2050. so the 2013 icao assembly will need to agree on an immediately-applicable and meaningful framework that guides the design of national and regional market-based mechanisms, a realistic timetable for a global market-based mechanism, and an ambitious set of technological and operational measures. the commission will report back to parliament and the council on the progress achieved at the icao assembly. if clear and sufficient progress is made there, the commission will propose further legislative action with a view to adapting the eu ets in line with a successful icao outcome. however, if this is not the case, the eu ets will again apply to external flights. the swift adoption of the ‘stopping-the-clock’ decision, discussed by parliament today, would ensure legal certainty for national authorities and aircraft operators with regard to compliance for 2012 emissions. let me emphasise that all operators – whether registered inside or outside the eu – will have to comply for their intra-european flights. these obligations will be in writing. enisa - the european agency for network and information security, the 'agency' - was established in march 2004. in september 2010, the commission put forward two proposals, the first to extend the mandate of the agency for 18 months, while the second was a more technical proposal to modernise and rationalise the agency. with the unanimous support of parliament, it was decided to approve the extension of the mandate of the agency first to ensure its immediate future and to give parliament more time to engage in a thorough debate and study on the longer term future of the agency. this regulation, which provides for the formal replacement of the agency established by the 2004 regulation by another agency, provides a good opportunity to re-examine the question of the seat. moreover, parliament, as a co-legislator, should clearly exercise this responsibility by also having a role in the choice of the seat of the bodies it agrees to set up, instead of leaving the question to the member states alone without public debate. your rapporteur therefore recommends that the seat of the agency be in brussels.

in writing. fisheries relations between the european union and the republic of mauritius began in 1989. they were not disrupted until 2007, but when the protocol expired, the parties could not agree on the terms of its renewal. the ex ante assessment of the current conditions of the fisheries sector in mauritius with a view to a new partnership agreement and protocol, prepared with the support of the commission, indicates that 'the impact assessment does not identify any likely negative economic, social or environmental impacts'. the new fisheries partnership agreement and the new protocol are balanced and serve the interests of both parties, and it is therefore recommended that the european parliament approve the conclusion of the agreement and the protocol. parliament must be informed immediately and fully at all stages of the procedures relating to the fisheries partnership agreement and the protocol, or their renewal, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3 of the draft legislative resolution.

in writing. the main objective of this proposal is to prohibit discharges into the skagerrak. the current situation, which in some cases allows large parts of the total catch to be discarded, is perhaps the most difficult for the population to understand and support in the context of the common fisheries policy. the fact that we are facing serious difficulties in feeding the world's population at a time when good quality fish are being thrown into the sea seems incomprehensible, even immoral. the proposal establishes a landing obligation and the necessary provisions to monitor and ensure that this obligation is respected. the best way for the legislator to enforce the rules on citizens is to ensure that they are seen as fair and equitable. they want to obey the law, but they would only do so reluctantly if they felt it was unjust. the main instrument for converting the ban on discards into a fair solution, respecting fishing opportunities and quotas, does not fall within the competence of the european parliament.

in writing. this eu directive, which entered into force on 21 december 2004, addresses gender equality and gender discrimination outside the world of work for the first time at eu level. the directive has been controversial in relation to the use of sex as a factor in the calculation of premiums and benefits for insurance and related financial services. the test-achats judgment had major consequences in the field of car insurance premiums. the rapporteur notes that the commission's preparation of an implementation report setting out binding guidelines would have been very useful for the application of the rules. therefore, the commission should present clear guidelines on how to apply the directive and ensure that there are no gaps in the legislation.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which opens up new avenues of thought and provides concrete indications on how to promote the development of our southern partner countries through international trade and economic links. it is important for developing countries to diversify their sources of income as much as possible. the report also targets the support that can be given to smes in these countries, which are potential drivers of higher growth. i would also stress the importance of transparency, which is essential in this area. the report also stresses the importance of the central role of the private sector, which i believe is essential to support public investment in these countries.
in writing. trade policy is one of the most important policy areas for the eu's policy coherence for development (dpc). if used properly, the instruments of trade policy can have a considerable impact on the development of poor countries. the eu's trade policy towards developing countries must have as its main objective to serve and reinforce the results achieved by our aid policy. seeking to develop the world, even by means other than aid, is tantamount to upholding the eu's core values and its treaty obligations. in order to better serve development objectives, eu trade policy must focus on generating positive spill-over effects in local, regional and national economies, as well as on promoting the diversification of developing countries' economies; it must also encourage more advanced and more profitable production. the imposition of customs duties on processed products in excess of those on raw materials may contribute to keeping developing countries in the role of mere exporters of raw materials.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report which underlines the importance of trade for development. to improve the impact of these measures, the report proposes that more concrete consideration should be given to the specific features and capacities of the various countries and that efforts should be made to promote greater regional integration for these countries. it also stresses the need for developing countries to improve local governance and social, environmental and labour standards, as well as respect for human rights as a key criterion for improving and strengthening trade relations, which i believe is essential for improving the living conditions of the inhabitants. finally, the report addresses the role of emerging and developed countries. it rightly stresses that these countries must honour their commitments to promote economic development by ensuring that measures are taken in accordance with democratic principles.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. i would also like to stress the importance of decent wage levels and acceptable safety conditions at work for a sustainable system of global trade and new global production chains. synergies between trade and development policies need to be improved. they should take into account the needs and capacities of beneficiary countries, encouraging instruments such as regional integration to ensure better exploitation of these synergies, and prioritise measures aiming, inter alia, at: promoting sustainable and inclusive development; creating jobs and enhancing skills and human capital development while reducing social inequalities; to improve resilience to economic shocks; supporting the development of the private sector, in particular small operators, including micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, in order to promote their participation in trade and investment at local, regional, cross-border, bilateral and multilateral levels; and improve fiscal governance and the fight against corruption, tax fraud and evasion, money laundering and tax havens, including through the establishment of information exchanges and control mechanisms on payments made by companies.
on behalf of the ecr group. – madam president, i want to warn against a monetary kamikaze. we are witnessing a worldwide monetary bonanza: quantitative easing in the us and japan doubling its monetary base. monetary expansion has not helped much so far: the us labour market is weak and japan has been in recession for fifteen years already. the eurozone has its own version of monetary easing, in the form of the ltros – roughly one trillion euros of cheap credit. that monetary easing comes through a watering-down of collateral requirements. the german paper die welt asked the ecb about this, but met with evasion of the issue, i am afraid. those who think we can solve our problems by monetary easing are wrong. we can buy a bit of time, but the underlying realities only get worse. the financial crisis was fuelled by a long-lasting cheap money flow, but now we are making it worse. we are getting more cheap money. the new york stock exchange is booming, but i am afraid it is yet another bubble. we need the underlying realities to change. we need supply-side measures to turn around the situation: productive, innovative activities, reduced tax burdens and user-friendly regulation. but we are doing the opposite – more taxation. look at france: the french government aims to introduce a super tax on the rich. it fights tax evasion, and then the minister for budgets appears to be a tax evader himself and, thereafter, it appears that members of the french government – a socialist government – are among the rich. no wonder public support is melting away. some central bankers think that they are a substitute for god, if not yet replacing him. they create money out of nothing; they spread wealth without work. look at alan greenspan. once he was the god of the dollar. now he is regarded as the master of disaster. let me give you a suggestion, mr draghi. put a picture of mr greenspan high in your office as a reminder of the fallibility of central bankers.

in writing. at the european summit in june 2012, the heads of state or government announced that once the single supervisory mechanism is in place, the esm could be used to recapitalise euro area banks directly. however, this option would not be open to non-euro area member states that adhere to the single surveillance. these member states have access to the balance of payments instrument, but its toolbox is limited compared to that of the esm. there are apparently no legal obstacles. however, the instrument is limited in terms of the amount of funds available to it. it is estimated that the maximum capacities of the oda instrument may not exceed 60 billion. this limitation is due to the fact that the funds are guaranteed by the union budget. if one of the borrowing member states were to default, the union would risk defaulting on its own obligations. if a financial institution were to be recapitalised directly through the bdp instrument, the union budget would then be exposed to that institution. the risk is much lower if the loan is granted to a member state and not directly to a financial institution.

in writing. the aim of the proposal is to clarify and harmonise the union rules on the vat treatment of vouchers. this will have a positive impact on businesses by eliminating double taxation and uncertainty about their tax obligations. it will also help to close the loopholes which facilitate tax evasion by certain companies exploiting disparities between member states. the new rules also fit well into the wider framework of the digital strategy for europe, in particular its objective of creating a digital single market. i am convinced that a coherent legal framework on vouchers is essential to implement by 2015 the rules on the change of place of delivery/service in business-to-consumer transactions. without these rules, any undertaking selling identical vouchers to individuals in different member states could be required to apply totally different vat treatments to those vouchers, even if the vouchers and the goods or services they enable to be purchased are the same.
