the agenda calls for the debate on the statements by the council and the commission on the 2012 comprehensive monitoring report of turkey (2012/2870 ((rsp)).
the debate has shown once again that the solution to the many hot spots which are hampering relations between the eu and turkey lies in turkish hands, including the kurdish question. i have already warned here of the danger of ankara unilaterally setting the terms of the peace process with the kurds. we must therefore be careful that this does not become a good news show for erdoğan and his people. the recent creation of a council of 49 turkish sages, who are to explain the peace process throughout the country, but then seen through the rose-colored glasses of ankara, suggests the opposite. we are not optimistic, either, when we look at the kck trial, the numerous arrests of politically elected representatives and journalists. the report rightly emphasizes the need for a lasting political dialogue between ankara and all the kurdish political forces, because that is the key to the kurdish solution. the eu must therefore also take full advantage of this momentum to fully enforce the self-evident fundamental rights of the kurds. full language and cultural rights, political autonomy and a constitution which finally recognizes freedom of expression, association and assembly for the 15 million kurds in the country.
it was unbelievable that in 2004 the decision was taken to open accession negotiations with turkey, a non-european country like turkey. what is even more incredible is that nine years later these negotiations are still being held, despite the commitment that the negotiations would be suspended if it became clear that turkey was not fulfilling its obligations. let us at least stop talking about a progress report when there is no progress at all in the case of turkey. nowhere in the world are more journalists in prison than in turkey. other opinion makers, such as writers and professors, are also in prison for expressing an opinion. the day before yesterday, the well-known pianist fazil say was sentenced to a suspended prison sentence for expressing an opinion critical of islam. the islamist government of erdoğan is pursuing an increasingly authoritarian, anti-european, anti-western and anti-christian course, and that is why we must now gradually put an end to these negotiations on turkey's accession. let us, for once, european commission, take account of the voters in europe who seem to have more common sense and more historical awareness than the european policy-makers.
member of the commission. − mr president, minister, honourable members, let me make two points: the first one is that kosovo has made substantial progress, both in the dialogue with serbia and also in the technical preparations for a stabilisation and association agreement, and kosovo should not stop there. we want kosovo to be ready across the board so that we can convince our member states to develop our relationship further. kosovo needs to continue with the same dynamism, with further credible efforts on the rule of law and all the issues we highlighted in our 2012 feasibility study. the commission will continue to support kosovo in this, and that brings to me a second remark: the discussion about the five member states. now, the college’s responsibility is clearly defined by the treaties, and you will not find there any basis for commission involvement in this issue. but i do not want to hide behind what this statement, although it reflects the reality of the treaty. this brings me to the three issues which we are pursuing jointly, under the leadership of high representative cathy ashton. we have absolutely no problem in combining common foreign and security policy (cfsp), member state and community instruments to tackle these issues, because what matters for both of us, with the support of the member states and the european parliament, is that we deliver. let me explain what exactly we want to deliver, and how exactly we thereby hope to make it easier for the five countries in question to make, when the time comes, the relevant decision on the relationship with kosovo. first, normalisation. it was this commission which last year, as part of the progress report, was the first to come up with the concept of normalising the relationship between belgrade and pristina. we described for the first time what we meant by normalisation, and we incorporated it into the enlargement process and thus created the only framework which could create the conditions for the relationship between belgrade and pristina to be normalised. this, i believe, will be a very important consideration – not only for those five member states, but particularly for them – when they decide about the relationship. the second issue is the dialogue. we have already had the second stage of the dialogue. you will remember the technical one, where a number of agreements were reached, and where implementation continues. we also have a political dialogue at the highest level. we have discussed that a lot this afternoon and this evening, and i can confirm that the dialogue is still continuing. i am determined that it shall continue until later today. the dialogue is an important part of normalisation. the dialogue should bring a solution, which again will make the relationship with kosovo easier. this brings me to the third point. high representative cathy ashton and i were both very keen to have kosovo involved in the mainstream of the enlargement process. it is one aspect of the stabilisation and association agreement. we presented the feasibility study last october and have put forward some minimum requirements for kosovo to deliver as part of negotiating the right step forward for kosovo to be a part of the enlargement mainstream in the western balkans. the second one is visa dialogue, which sooner or later is going to bring kosovo citizens the same benefits as other countries in the western balkans, namely a visa-free system as far as the schengen countries are concerned. the framework agreement with kosovo allowing it to participate in european union programmes will be another legally binding document, once parliament gives its consent and we are able to sign it. it will be just another concrete contribution to bringing kosovo into the mainstream. as eulex is downsized, the importance of the structured dialogue on the rule of law and the weight and importance of the enlargement instrument will be increased. all of these are important elements which i hope very much will ensure that all member states, not just most of them, make it possible for all the countries of the western balkans to achieve their european aspirations.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i would like to begin by thanking ms lunacek for her very detailed and committed work on behalf of parliament. it is very much appreciated. i do not propose to reiterate the points which have been made very comprehensively and very eloquently by my friend štefan füle. i would just say, i suppose in summary, that regional cooperation and particularly good neighbourly relations are absolutely essential elements of the stabilisation and association process, and parties concerned in the western balkans must ensure that any disputes between them do not have a detrimental effect on their shared goal of progress towards european membership. obviously the case of kosovo and of serbia is a work in progress, not without significant challenges. the process is in place, as i said in the earlier debate, so it is key that the two parties do not lose sight of the ultimate goals, the long-term goals of peace and prosperity. i think the best way of achieving that is a successful outcome from the dialogue which is taking place, as we know, today, so that both serbia and kosovo can continue to build momentum on their path towards european integration. that is something that the irish presidency very strongly supports, and we are very hopeful for a positive outcome. thank you to all of the members who have participated not just in this debate but in the previous debate. it has been a long but a very interesting and useful evening from the point of view of the presidency, and thank you very much for your attention and your patience.
the eu has not fully absorbed enlargement operations since 2004, yet it is busy giving a prospect of accession to countries like kosovo. that's far from a sign of good governance. it is one of the reasons why public opinion in the member states is increasingly turning away from the eu. the voters want to see the european union finally drawn into the picture and rightly wonder what the added value of eu membership for kosovo or turkey might be. it will only create new problems. it is a curious paradox that the more the eu is confronted with internal problems (euro crisis, schengen, democratic deficit, lack of transparency and accountability to citizens), the more it wants to become bigger. we need a reality check as soon as possible.
madam president, as rapporteur in the committee on industry, research and industry i would like to focus on the specific issue of the search for oil and gas in the arctic region, which has already been mentioned here. we have all followed the endeavours of shell in alaska that have clearly shown that operations in the arctic are indeed extremely difficult and dangerous for mankind, and for nature of course. many in this house have since called for a moratorium on oil drilling in the arctic waters. we all know, apart from the special case of greenland of course, that the eu does not have any arctic waters. however, commissioner, in the new draft legislation on offshore oil and gas operations that is scheduled for approval here in this house next month, we have introduced a clear obligation for drilling companies to demonstrate that they can effectively respond to oil spills and that they also have to limit their operations when they cannot respond. that is a real legislative obligation that is future-proof and above all it applies a fortiori to potential off-shore drills in the arctic. we are counting on you, commissioner, to support and wholeheartedly spread this legal instrument within the arctic council, hopefully as a soon-to-be permanent observing member, and especially in your international role as a commissioner.

in writing. - i welcome this commission proposal as it tackles the problem of environmentally harmful and unsafe practices in ship-wrecking. in an international transport mode such as shipping, it is essential to seek international regulations. the hong kong convention on safe and environmentally sound recycling, adopted by the international maritime organisation in 2009, is a good step towards addressing the existing problems. however, this will not come into force until 2020, so i welcome this proposal to speed up its entry into force, which calls for, among other things, the scrapping of ships in safe and environmentally sound scrapyards. the rapporteur's call for a financing mechanism for the environmentally sound recycling of ships goes too far. the port authorities in the member states would be obliged to levy a recycling charge on ships. such a measure contradicts the fact that only an international regulation makes sense in such a sector and adds to the administrative burden of ports. even more problematic is the risk that ships will be more likely to call at ports outside europe to avoid this levy. such levies should therefore be imposed on the owner and should be paid into a fund managed internationally, such as the imo, on any further sale of the ship.

in writing. due to the multiplicity of hazardous materials on board a ship, any ship leaving the european union for dismantling is hazardous waste and therefore can currently only be legally dismantled within the oecd. however, this legislation is circumvented in an almost systematic way. in 2009, more than 90% of eu-flagged vessels were actually dismantled outside the oecd, mainly in south asia (india, pakistan and bangladesh), using the 'sand-by' method and with considerable environmental and health consequences. this report highlights four priorities. (a) a financial mechanism to finance environmentally friendly ship recycling; (b) an inventory of dangerous materials for all ships calling at ports of the union; (c) a ship recycling plan for all eu ships going for recycling or over 20 years old, to be approved by the competent authorities; (d) more explicit criteria for ship recycling facilities, including the exclusion of landing, and the regular verification and inspection of such facilities; (e) criminal sanctions for certain infringements.

- i'm the reporter. - we are all satisfied that we have been able to complete this process, that we now have new, better rules for the safety of oil and gas drilling in european waters and, above all, that we are learning timely lessons from the deepwater horizon oil rig incident in the gulf of mexico. that incident has demonstrated in a very painful way that there was a lack of proper risk assessment in the us, that there was poor safety management and a lack of operational contingency plans. we are rightly drawing lessons from this in the european union. oil and gas, as was also shown in the previous debate on mr reul's report, will remain essential for our energy supply for several decades to come. the extraction of oil and gas in european waters is of great importance from the point of view of our energy independence and will remain so for a long time. but drilling is increasingly taking place in more extreme conditions, increasingly further north and also deeper, sometimes as far as two or three kilometres below sea level. the risks of an accident or incident are thereby increased. that is one of the main reasons why we have made these additional security measures work as quickly as possible through a first reading. the directive is, first and foremost, a directive which sets the highest standards in risk management. the standard we are setting now can serve as an example to the world. but it's not just about risk prevention, it's also about the contingency plans that companies need to have in place. that is of course essential in the event of an incident. this new regulatory framework requires companies to review their emergency plans before the start of the activity to test whether those emergency plans are operational in the event of an incident. a very important aspect is that there are strict provisions on the financial capacity of oil and gas operators, so that those who want to get started, even in extreme circumstances, have the technical and financial capacity to cope with the ecological and economic consequences of a possible incident. another important element: public consultation. it is obvious that if we want to maintain public support for oil and gas drilling in eu waters, we must involve public opinion. this has not been the case in all cases to date and it is good that these new rules ensure that in all cases of oil and gas exploration, and indeed production, the public is closely involved and consulted in all member states. another important element: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. mandatory reporting will enable those companies and us as a public authority to learn from accidents involving eu operators outside the european union. that too is a very important step forward. and finally - but i assume that will be discussed later in the debate - the arctic. we all know that we do not have eu waters in the arctic today, so it is obviously difficult in this context to push for a moratorium on oil and gas drilling in that area. we have agreed with the commission and the member states to make maximum efforts in the arctic council. we have gone for the concrete measures that are tangible and achievable. in any event, and this is crucial, european operators considering drilling in the arctic will have to demonstrate that they are able to carry out their contingency plans in all weather conditions, including in that area. if not, then of course they will have to abandon these drilling. but as i said, i assume that will be brought up in the debate. i look forward to hearing the reactions and to the debate.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has already made a number of proposals. i too could imagine even more far-reaching requirements for technical standards and safety. but the current system gives us a better quality for the safety of our european waters. it is an important step towards a european understanding of the safety of offshore oil and gas production. since the main resources in the north sea, the north atlantic, the black sea and the mediterranean each concern several member states of the european union, european legislation is the right way to go. we shall not stop working if you adopt these proposals. it is important that member states apply and implement this system fully, that any possible circumvention and abuse is avoided and that independent control authorities exercise strict controls. what will we do as a commission? we will certainly take up and export these safety standards in our discussions with the opec countries - libya, algeria - with our immediate neighbours in the context of our neighbourhood strategy - ukraine - with our partners worldwide - the usa and others - and recommend them to others, to our partners, to our neighbours - in other words, to all those who are important to us in terms of indivisible waters or high technical know-how. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used effectively. i think that this is an important step towards europeanising our security philosophy for oil and gas production in europe. commission statement with regard to article 41 of directive 2013/.../eu of the european parliament and of the council on safety of offshore oil and gas operations and amending directive 2004/35/ec the commission regrets that under article 41 (3) and (5) some member states are partially exempted from the obligation to transpose the directive and considers that such derogations should not be regarded as a precedent in order not to affect the integrity of eu law. the commission notes that member states may use the option not to transpose and apply article 20 of the directive because of the current absence of any company registered in their jurisdiction which has offshore activities outside the territory of the union. in order to ensure effective enforcement of this directive, the commission underlines that it is incumbent on these member states to ensure that companies already registered with them do not circumvent the objectives of the directive by extending their business objects to include offshore activities without notifying the competent national authorities of this extension so that they can take the necessary steps to ensure full application of article 20. the commission will take all necessary measures against any circumvention which may be brought to its attention.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i am very grateful to renate weber for her report and to the honourable members tonight for the views they have expressed during this debate. i am looking forward to the vote tomorrow, for if the final result reflects the tenor of this debate then the prospects are positive. the report is a crucial contribution to our in-depth reflection on how to ensure respect for media freedom and pluralism across europe – and, as we saw last week in the united states, for example, it is not only in europe that societies face big challenges in relation to the appropriate protection of journalistic freedom. this is not the first time we have discussed threats to press freedom in this house. the issue has rightly been referred to as one of the basic elements of our democracy, and the point has been made to the commission that if a country is not dealing appropriately with these fundamental matters, there is a need for intervention. i could not agree more; but to intervene you need instruments, a definition of responsibilities and opportunities, and these are the matters we are now really starting to debate. so i am glad that this time we have to hand a clear report, with proposals for concrete action, enabling us to have a principled debate with member states and all the stakeholders. however, in order to decide which actions need to be taken and by whom, we require three things. the first is clarity about eu competences, for you need competences in order to act; the second is reflection on how best to use the competences; and the third is the member states’ political will to play their part. i am pleased that the irish presidency has shown commitment on this issue, and i sincerely hope that the incoming lithuanian presidency will build on that. as you know, some time ago i set up an independent high-level group chaired by professor vaira vīķe-freiberga, the former president of latvia, to reflect on the underlying issues related to media freedom and pluralism, and earlier this year the group delivered a comprehensive report with 30 recommendations, some of which are similar to what you propose, ms weber, in your report. i would like to point out that we are already acting on some of the areas addressed both in the recommendations of the independent high-level group and in the weber report. for instance, we are about to allocate a grant to implement the media pluralism monitoring tool in 2013 on the basis of a budget allocated by you. this tool will give us a much more coherent overview of where pluralism is under threat across europe. at the same time we are working on implementation of a pilot project for a european centre for press and media freedom. we plan to launch a call for proposals very soon. other potential actions in the area of media freedom and pluralism require broad consultation with all the relevant stakeholders. that is why i recently launched two public consultations: the first to gather feedback on all the recommendations of the high-level group report, and the second, more specifically, to collect views on the independence of regulatory bodies responsible for audiovisual media services, including the question of a possible revision of article 30 of the audiovisual media services directive. so the timing of the report by renate weber, just when we need input into the discussion, could not be better, and it is most welcome. after we close the consultation in mid-june we will have an even better overview of what exactly we need to do. i hope, mr in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, media pluralism stands or falls with media ownership. the concentration of media in one hand is always and everywhere a negative for democracy. that is why transparency of media ownership is so important and is an essential part of this report. we are counting on the european commission to come forward with a concrete instrument for measurement and control. but media freedom is also fundamentally linked to journalistic ethics. pluralism does not mean that the media, the journalists, have a free hand to do or not do what they want. recent developments in the united kingdom and other countries have shown that member states need to establish an independent media council, which can deal efficiently with citizens' complaints about the media and, if necessary, also make amends.
mr president, as the rapporteur has said, pensions are primarily a matter for the member states, with their own specificities. but it is important for us to make recommendations on a difficult subject in a complex context of crisis, and i will highlight some points which are important for our group. first, the first pillar, which is fundamental to solidarity, must be the cornerstone of pension systems and ensure more than a minimum pension, namely a decent income. secondly, the second pillar can make a contribution, but cannot be a prerequisite for achieving this objective. the third pillar can only be favoured for the lowest incomes and incomplete careers. the employment rate is obviously the fundamental aspect of pension funding and it must be promoted, not only for the elderly but also for the young, so that they contribute to the system. furthermore, any reform of the legal retirement age can only be carried out after the appropriateness of the reform has been assessed with the social partners and cannot be linked to life expectancy. finally, i would say that, although it is obviously not a socialist report, as it would have been written in our group alone, it is a good compromise and i would like to thank the rapporteur for it.

in writing. i welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on the agreement between the european union and sri lanka on certain aspects of air services. this decision is a sign of closer cooperation with sri lanka and also creates a sound legal basis for bilateral agreements between a few member countries and sri lanka. the commission therefore concludes that the compensation granted to ryanair for the services it provides to ryanair is compatible with the internal market. now any air carrier wishing to operate between sri lanka and a member state will be able to do so, provided of course that a bilateral agreement has already been concluded between that member state and sri lanka and that traffic rights are also available. i am sure that this will have a positive impact on our economies and on tourism.
in writing. the eu-sri lanka agreement on certain aspects of air services will strengthen the eu-sri lanka bilateral relations in the field of aviation. the european designation clause will enable all community air carriers to enjoy non-discriminatory access to air services between the union and sri lanka and bilateral air services agreements will be in accordance with european union law. this agreement could be a factor for economic growth in the air sector and for the development of tourism between the member states and sri lanka.
in writing. international relations in the field of air transport between member states and third countries are traditionally governed by bilateral air services agreements. these bilateral agreements contain a 'designation clause' which allows a third country to reject, withdraw or suspend the licences or authorisations of an air carrier which has been designated by a member state but which is not substantially owned and effectively controlled by that member state or its nationals. in 2002, the court of justice of the european union ruled that this traditional designation clause was contrary to eu law. this was found to be discriminatory against community carriers established in the territory of one member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states and to be in breach of article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in the present case, sri lanka has signed 15 bilateral agreements, the relevant provisions of which need to be replaced or supplemented by the provisions of a single agreement concluded on behalf of the union.
in writing. i welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on enhanced cooperation between the european union and the european organisation for the safety of air navigation. since 2004, the aim of european leaders has been to create a 'single european sky' that would allow for the optimal use of airspace. by strengthening its cooperation with the european organisation for the safety of air navigation (eurocontrol), the european union is taking a further step towards the effective implementation of the euc project. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. the committee also wants to see the eu's role in the fight against terrorism strengthened, and calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism.
in writing. closer cooperation between the european union and the european organisation for the safety of european navigation will advance the implementation of the single european sky, launched in 2004 but still not completed. the fragmentation of european airspace has significant negative impacts on airspace users and the environment. the single management of european airspace is therefore essential to meet future needs in terms of aviation capacity and safety and to ensure the quality of air services provided to european citizens.
in writing. i believe that the agreement will help to ensure the continued implementation of the single european sky and recommend that the european parliament endorse its conclusion. first, the agreement confirms eurocontrol as the technical and operational body of the union in the development and implementation of the eusc; it shall set out the areas of cooperation and define the forms and mechanisms thereof and shall aim to generate synergies with the european aviation safety agency (easa) and to avoid unnecessary duplication of its work on safety-related air traffic management and environmental issues. it is also proposed to set up a joint committee to be responsible for the management and operation of the agreement. this committee would have the power to adopt and amend the annexes to the agreement.
in writing. the new regulation aims to confirm the european university institute (eui) in florence in its role as manager of the eu archives. it thus confirms a factual situation, since the majority of the institutions which have made their archives available to the public already entrusted them to the eui. the filing of paper archives at the eui is now compulsory for all eu institutions and bodies, except the court of justice and the european central bank. the archives are an essential source of information for anyone interested in the history of european union integration. they are a testimony to the influence of the institutions. they have a cultural and educational aspect. they reflect the evolution of our societies. the fact that they are made compulsory for filing with the eui is a gesture of transparency and good interinstitutional cooperation. in this context, i fully support the new regulation which encourages the eu institutions to move towards digitisation. digitisation has undeniable advantages such as preservation of documents, storage, easy consultation, etc. it is an indispensable tool for work in our time and for the future.
in writing. the suggested cost-sharing approach is based on the criterion that the level of contribution will be proportional "to the size of the different headcount tables of the depositing institutions". this criterion seems to be quite advantageous for the european parliament, since, despite its size, it will not make a very large financial contribution, although it is likely to deposit a large amount of historical archives. i am glad that it takes account of the current realities of the digital archiving process, which is not uniform from one institution of the union to another. in addition, as archives in europe are currently facing the challenges of the digital age, the proposal encourages the union institutions to move towards digitisation. as regards the sensitive issue of data protection, i am also pleased that the proposal clarifies the rules applicable to archives. in the event that personal data remain in the archives, the proposal emphasises the role of the eui as a 'sub-processor' of personal data within the meaning of the regulation, acting on the instructions of the depositing institutions of the union.
in writing. i fully share the position expressed in the report by mr carlo casini that the date of the next elections should be moved from thursday 22 june to sunday 25 may 2014 in order to avoid them being held during a school holiday period in many member states. the european parliament is the body that represents all the citizens of the european union. it is therefore of the utmost importance that these elections are not held on a date which could have a negative impact on the turnout in these elections.
in writing. this report responds to a request for consultation by the council on a draft decision to amend the electoral period, which should normally apply at the next european elections, namely in accordance with article 11 (2) of the act concerning the election of the members of the european parliament by direct universal suffrage (the 'electoral act') from thursday 5 to sunday 8 june 2014, by reference to the dates on which the first elections by direct universal suffrage were held (from thursday 9 to sunday 12 june 1979). taking into account that the long weekend of pentecost corresponds in the majority of the member states to the dates normally applicable, the council considered that it would be preferable to move them forward by proposing to set the electoral period as follows: from thursday 22 to sunday 25 may 2014. the important thing, as far as i know, is that the citizen is in the best possible condition to vote.

in writing. i agree with the ideas in the report by mr klaus-heiner lehne on takeover bids. acquisition activities are highly dependent on financial and economic developments. we cannot therefore assess accurately and correctly the application of the directive in the member states, since the date of transposition of the directive coincided with the beginning of the financial crisis. it has grown and spread to the real economy, affecting all countries and all sectors.
in writing. i note that after decades of failed attempts, the directive was finally adopted at second reading by the european parliament at the end of 2003 and published in the official journal in april 2004. member states had until may 2006 to transpose the provisions of the directive into national law. it is a pity that the date of transposition of the directive coincided with the beginning of the crisis. in the light of these observations, i believe that the application of the directive cannot be properly assessed on the basis of the limited data available. i therefore believe that more relevant data are needed not only to establish the need to amend the directive but also to define precisely the next harmonisation measures to be adopted.
in writing. i welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on regional strategies for industrial zones in the european union. today, the industrial sector still accounts for 16% of the union's gdp. however, for the last 50 years, this sector has been suffering from a real decline: relocations, social plans, restructurings, etc. there are many examples in europe. the resolution will enable the european union to provide constructive assistance to the oldest industrialised regions, not only by providing public funds but also by providing tools to enable these areas to facilitate their industrial conversion. for while european enlargement has diverted our attention from the new members and the resulting regional disparities, it is imperative that we do not forget these industrial regions which are at the origin of the formation of today's europe and on which many jobs for our fellow europeans still depend.
in writing. the industrial sector is a major asset of the european union. but at the moment this sector, so promising for the union, is suffering the consequences of the crisis and is experiencing a major decline. it represented 20% of the union's gdp before the economic crisis, but now only 16%. the union must solve the deindustrialization problem, which is undoubtedly the major problem in europe, if it is to continue to have a voice on the international scene. europe needs the industrial conversion of former industrial areas more than ever if it is to achieve the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. local and territorial authorities need the union to help them with the resources available at community level. special financial attention to regions and cities in difficulty will encourage business creation in these areas, and alleviate the burden of the crisis, while contributing to economic recovery.
in writing. although the industrial sector has been in decline in the european union for the last fifty years, european industry still accounts for about 16% of the union's gdp. however, given the decline of many traditional industries (coal, steel, textiles, machinery, etc.) which once contributed to the prosperity of many regions for several decades, a number of regions in the european union are facing similar problems today. many regions of the european union are therefore dependent on european funding to help them reconvert and restructure their former industrial areas. in this context, it is becoming clear that, in the context of the financial and economic crisis, sectoral policies are not sufficient to achieve the great ambitions of the european industrial policy and the europe 2020 strategy. the support provided by cohesion policy measures is becoming increasingly important. this report looks at the main challenges of structural transformation processes in the formerly industrialised regions of the european union and the role that european cohesion policy can play in this context. the report therefore sets out three main objectives.
in writing. i welcome the work done by mr ivo belet on this report. in recent years we have seen large-scale environmental disasters caused by oil exploration and production. adequate standards and best control practices need to be put in place within the european union in order to reduce offshore oil-related incidents and their devastating and irreversible consequences. the measures envisaged in this report, including the exchange of information and cooperation with third countries, will make it possible to provide rapid and effective assistance in the event of an accident linked to this type of activity that may affect european citizens and the environment of the european union. this report illustrates the european union's determination not to stand idly by and to take action to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past.
in writing. on 20 april 2010, the explosion on the deepwater horizon oil rig killed 11 men working on the rig and caused a spill of approximately 4.9 million barrels (780,000 cubic meters) of crude oil. it took 3 months to fill the well and 2 more months to complete the back-up well and be able to declare the well "effectively dead". this is totally unacceptable! the accident also prompted a review of eu policies: the european commission immediately launched an assessment of the safety of offshore oil and gas operations in european waters. it concluded that a clear and up-to-date european framework is needed to apply eu-wide best practices already in place in the regulatory regimes of some eu member states. the proposal for a regulation on the security of offshore oil and gas exploration, production and production activities, presented by the commission to parliament in october 2011, focuses on concrete measures to address the disparities and fragmentation that characterise the overall practices and legislation of member states in the field of offshore oil and gas exploitation.
in writing. − the deployment of renewable energy is vital for europe to become less dependent on oil and gas imports and is a key factor for growth and jobs. so it is good that we have a clear vision for 2030, which creates certainty for industry. but more european coordination is logical and necessary. it is in the interest of all of us to avoid the fact that member states, because of their geographical location, have to subsidize certain renewable energy sources too heavily to make them competitive with conventional fossil energy sources. the development of a fully-fledged european energy market is therefore essential. this is the only way to get renewable energy from one side of europe to the other. the administrative jungle of 170 (!) different subsidy schemes in the various member states must also be simplified.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on renewable energy production in europe. the outlook is that our continent will become increasingly dependent on energy imports to meet domestic demand in the coming years. unlike other countries or continents, we do not have the natural resources to meet our energy needs. it is therefore imperative to define an energy policy which takes into account the following three parameters: security of supply, competitiveness, and economic and environmental sustainability. the completion of the internal energy market by 2014 should promote smes active in renewable energy production. it is europe's duty to provide for measures to compensate for our lack of natural resources. i am therefore pleased with the framework voted in this report which will allow for greater public support for research and development in renewable energy production which i personally would like to see reaching 40 to 45% of our total consumption by 2015.
in writing. − increasing the use of renewable energy is of paramount importance to increase europe's energy independence, to promote sustainability in the eu and to boost the competitiveness of european industry. this is why renewable energy needs to be given special attention in the european energy market. this is the only way for the eu to achieve its target of producing 20% of its energy from renewable sources by 2020. this report is welcome, as it calls for, among other things, the further development of renewable energy infrastructure and draws attention to the uncoordinated cross-border energy flows caused by insufficient network capacity and storage, and insufficient cooperation. it also advocates increasing the social acceptance of renewable energy sources by end-users. the basis for this, in addition to the accessibility of energy from renewable sources, is, in my view, above all, easy-to-understand information for consumers about renewable energies and their uses. this own-initiative report should be limited to reference to already established energy targets and should avoid the introduction of new binding targets for renewable energy by 2030.
in writing. the european union is heavily dependent on energy imports. the promotion of renewable energy is essential to reduce the eu's dependence on third countries, but also to combat climate change and to ensure sustainable economic growth. i voted for the amendment asking the commission to propose a binding eu-wide target for energy from renewable sources by 2030, but i voted against the amendment proposing to set this target between 40 and 45% of energy production because it is not sustainable for belgium.
in writing. addressing the energy challenge is a major challenge for the union. the european union has no choice but to win the battle for energy independence, or else it risks becoming the only net energy importer on the continent, since the united states and canada discovered the oil shale. this is reason enough to support the reul report this afternoon, which stresses the essential role of renewable energies in the energy mix and their contribution to the fight against climate change. this concerns a wide range of energy sources: hydroelectric, geothermal, solar, tidal, wind, biomass, biofuels, which already offer different services in the fields of electricity, heating, cooling and transport, but are unevenly distributed across europe. belgium, for example, is one of the countries with limited room for manoeuvre: no mountains and rivers to invest in hydraulics, little sun to make photovoltaics a dominant energy source. the european union cannot ignore this reality; the principle of unequal access to natural resources should now be a priority criterion to be taken into account by the commission when establishing the share of renewable energy in the union's energy mix for 2030.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. the 2020 renewable energy targets for the european union as a whole, as well as for member states, set by the renewable energy directive, have accelerated the uptake of renewable energy in europe, in particular in rural areas. in order to ensure policy continuity and increase investment security, the union should present new objectives for the period after 2020 as soon as possible.
in writing. i welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on women's rights in the balkan candidate countries. in theory, it is true that these countries have made enormous progress in this area in order to bring their legislation into line with the eu acquis. however, the reality on the ground is quite different: women in the balkans are still too often victims of sexism, stereotypes and even violence. this resolution promises to make great progress in this field, since, on the one hand, it provides for concrete measures in the application of women's rights, without simply listing the problems, and, on the other hand, it deals with each country individually, taking account of the specific socioeconomic, political and cultural characteristics of the country. this decision should, i hope, enable citizens in the balkans to be better informed about gender equality through awareness campaigns, to increase the employment rate of women, which remains very low in the region, and to effectively combat violence - whether verbal or physical - against women.
in writing. gender equality is something we all want. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. the balkan societies remain very patriarchal and therefore much progress remains to be made in this area if the balkan countries want to join the eu. equality between men and women is a fundamental right enshrined in the treaty of lisbon, enshrined in the european charter of fundamental rights, and a priority policy of the union. it's a matter of human justice. how can we contribute to fair, equitable and sustainable development if half the population does not enjoy the same rights and continues to be discriminated against? gender equality and the empowerment of women are key elements of growth, economic development and sustainable development. this is why strengthened mechanisms need to be put in place to improve the situation of women in the balkan candidate countries and to guarantee gender equality.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which highlights the progress made but also some serious obstacles to the promotion of gender equality. for provisions on women's rights and gender equality to be effective, enforcement mechanisms need to be in place. citizens must be aware of their rights and be able to report any discrimination or violation of their rights to an authority, and their complaints must be dealt with in a correct and timely manner in order to be of practical use. the last report of the committee on women's rights and gender equality on women's rights and gender equality in the balkan candidate countries dates from 2008. since then, most of the balkan countries have made progress towards eu membership, but at different rates. promoting gender equality is a key element of these processes. not only because women represent half the population of the candidate countries, but also because gender equality is a core value of the union, enshrined in its treaty.
in writing. i welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on standards for media freedom across the european union. the media are - and must remain - the "watchdogs" of our societies, enabling each individual to be properly informed, while giving them the tools to become responsible citizens. freedom and pluralism of the media are therefore two fundamental rights enshrined in the values of the european union. it is imperative that they be respected to the best of our ability, whether we are a member state or a candidate country. this decision not only impacts the media, it also directly impacts the citizen whose right to freedom of expression it guarantees. in this resolution, parliament thus confirms its determination to support the right of every european to be informed fairly and neutrally, democratically and peacefully, of decisions in the public interest. if we do not respect these objectives of media freedom, it is not only our european model that will be affected. it's for our democracy.
in writing. the fundamental rights of citizens to freedom of expression and information can only be guaranteed through a free and pluralistic media. however, on several occasions, journalists and media have been subject to pressure, threats and harassment within the european union itself. some of the greatest threats to media freedom in some member states are the result of recent legislation. the european union and its member states must set an example to ensure their credibility and consistency in condemning practices outside the union. the member states and the union should respect, guarantee, protect and promote the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information and the freedom and pluralism of the media, and refrain from any threat to that freedom. it is important to ensure the independence and protection of journalists. conflicts of interest must be avoided, excessive concentration of media must be prevented and transparency in media ownership must be ensured. freedom of the media remains an issue in europe and common standards should be adopted to guarantee it. a free and accountable press is an indispensable feature of democracy and the rule of law.
in writing. journalism is a real source of satisfaction in europe; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are not undermined. but i must say that in some countries the media cannot express themselves freely. the lack of transparency of media ownership in some states is worrying. we therefore call on the commission and the member states to take initiatives to ensure transparency of media ownership and management, including by requiring audiovisual, print and other similar media to provide national media authorities, company registers and the public with sufficiently accurate and up-to-date information on ownership, to allow the identification of beneficiaries, ultimate owners and co-owners of media bodies, their cvs and means of financing, to transpose it into a single european media register, to identify excessive concentrations in the media, and to prevent organisations from concealing special interests and therefore manipulating the media by removing journalists from their journalistic neutrality.
in writing. − demographic change will bring with it an ageing population, which will present a major challenge to pension systems. this is all the more so given that the financial and economic crisis and the associated public debt and increased unemployment are having a significant impact on pension benefits and thus on the retirement benefits of eu citizens. in order to take account of these developments, urgent adjustments are needed in the pension systems of the member states. the eu commission is considering measures such as the equalization of the retirement age for men and women or the adjustment of the retirement age to the increase in life expectancy. however, it seems to me particularly important that all the measures proposed by the european commission guarantee a decent standard of living and financial independence for older europeans. while i welcome the call for better access to lifelong learning and the development of employment opportunities for older workers, this should not result in making it difficult for europe's older people to enjoy their well-earned retirement in a dignified way with a decent standard of living. this is why measures to combat youth unemployment seem to me to be a better starting point than to demand longer employment for older eu citizens.
in writing. economic, demographic and social developments are putting increasing pressure on our pension systems. the present system shows its limits and will not be able to meet the needs of the growing retirement age population in a few years' time. society is aging, life expectancy is increasing, birth rates are falling. structural reform of pension funding is needed. the economic and social crisis has affected thousands of people. many people rely on pensions, which are the main source of income for older people in europe. the european union must ensure that all its citizens have a decent pension.
in writing. in all the member states of the european union, pension systems are under pressure. life expectancy is increasing, birth rates are falling, young people are entering the labour market later than expected, and the effects of the crisis on the pension system are being felt. although pensions remain a national competence, the european strategy for adequate, secure and sustainable pensions voted this afternoon in plenary is an excellent instrument for initiating discussion and then implementing further reforms. this non-binding own-initiative report aims to reduce the gap between the different pension systems and ensure both their sustainability, solidarity between generations, the principle of equity between members (employees, civil servants, self-employed) and a guarantee of protection for the most deprived. these systems should also help to strengthen labour market mobility and free movement, while providing solutions for today and tomorrow. belgium, like other european countries, is preparing for a second wave of pension reform for the period 2020-2040, after a first reform aimed mainly at extending careers.
in writing. − as a result of increasing life expectancy, europeans enjoy their pensions longer. at the same time, the pressure on their affordability is proportionately increasing. in europe we have different pension systems, but also different levels of participation. for example, in sweden almost 74% of the 55+ age group are in work, in belgium it is barely 40%. pension schemes are primarily the responsibility of the member states, although some coordination is needed and renewal is necessary. i do not always agree with the suggestions in the report by mrs oomen-ruijten. the three-pillar system is being promoted as an ideal, and the rapporteur admits that there is a lack of solidarity among young people. the third pillar - strengthening the pension system - will not solve this problem. the first pillar, which the government itself is responsible for, must remain the most important pillar. a lot of people depend on that income, and it's a buffer against poverty. my other criticism concerns the portability of accumulated pension rights. over the years, the labour market has changed towards greater mobility and flexibility, also beyond national borders. the report states that accumulated pension rights must not be lost. i want them to be portable and paid for.
in writing. pension systems are under pressure. the euro area authorities either save to meet the requirements of the stability and growth pact by balancing their expenditure and income or are forced to take strong measures to reduce excessive deficits. in all the states, there is also talk of an ageing society. the crisis has also put a lesser strain on the so-called second pillar schemes, namely the collective schemes, which provide retirement savings. the european strategy for adequate, safe and sustainable pensions for young people and older people, presented in the white paper, is an excellent instrument for initiating discussion and then implementing reforms, notably through soft law, but also through legislation where necessary. we must work together, with due respect for the responsibility of the member states and the social partners, to establish systems which are adequate, safe and sustainable. however, these systems must also contribute to strengthening labour market mobility and free movement, and offer solutions for today and tomorrow.
in writing. - the ageing population, which is increasingly a reality in europe, is too often portrayed in a negative light. the fact that people are living longer today is in itself a positive fact, which we should regard as a fine achievement for man and science. but as policy makers, we cannot be blind to the effects of ageing on our societies. the report sets out the guidelines for the policies to be pursued by the member states in the years ahead. a policy to ensure the affordability of pensions, based on three pillars but with a sufficiently strong first pillar. a policy that does not accept that the elderly end up in poverty. a policy that eliminates unjustified differences between men and women. a policy that fully chooses to activate people, including older workers, to strengthen the resilience of our society. finally, a policy which informs its citizens correctly and thoroughly about what they can expect in their old age and how they can contribute to the most favourable pension. such a policy that embraces and creates the best possible conditions for ageing is forward-looking and responsible. i therefore fully support the report by mrs oomen-ruijten.
- i'm the reporter. − only through results can we regain the trust of people and businesses and promote sustainable growth. the creation of a genuine common european banking supervision, as a fundamental building block of the wider banking union, is a step forward in this direction. we have been asking for it for years and we are therefore pleased to see real progress in the last few months. the sense of urgency has not disappeared and therefore solid progress is needed to strengthen confidence, to make the financial sector stronger and more credible, to provide the economy with the necessary capital and, finally, to better protect savers. the ecb's entry into the role of new supervisor also fulfils a necessary first condition for the recapitalisation of banking institutions directly from the esm. this in turn plays an important role in breaking the vicious circle between the banking and public finance crises. the trialogue agreement on the ssm and the eba legislation was reached in a very democratic way because we were on our toes and because the council and the commission kept their commitment to deal with both texts in one package and to deal with them in full co-decision. it is partly thanks to the constructive cooperation with the shadow rapporteurs that we were able to establish our position in less than 10 weeks and to achieve our initial objectives in full. (1) we will have a credible, efficiently organised single supervisory mechanism (ssm) with the ecb as the centre. (2) we will have a supervisory mechanism that is as close as possible to the proper functioning of the internal market. (3) we get a supervisory mechanism that is mandatory for euro member states and that we make very attractive for the accession of countries that have not yet joined the euro, which translates, among other things, into equal voting rights in the banking supervision council and some opt-out possibilities to compensate for the asymmetric situation. (4) we will have a division of tasks between the ecb and the national supervisory authorities, taking into account subsidiarity, proportionality, practicality and credibility of the system. the ecb will monitor directly the more significant banks and those banks seeking or receiving support from the european emergency funds. in principle, national supervisors will continue to monitor less significant banks, provided that the ecb can at any time take over the supervision of a bank if necessary. the fifth. we have worked particularly hard on the ecb's accountability, because any shift of powers from the national to the european level must be accompanied by adequate accountability at the european level, in particular to the european parliament. the sixth. finally, a realistic timetable for entry into force has been agreed, taking into account the european supervisory authority's capacity to perform those new supervisory tasks in an excellent manner. on wednesday we shall vote on the package of amendments, but we shall not put an end to this dossier. as rapporteur, i shall propose that the final vote on the legislative resolution be postponed until a later part-session. we have another blow to the council, which cannot reach a unanimous final agreement on the agreement on the ssm through a procedure in one member state. it also gives us, as the european parliament, the opportunity to conclude another solid interinstitutional agreement with the ecb on accountability and accountability. this is a matter of the utmost importance for democracy. whether it is parliament's access to documents, our rights of inquiry or our role in the appointment and removal of the president and vice-presidents, we want clear agreements on the practical implementation of these before we close this dossier in plenary. for all these reasons, i hope you will support this outcome of the negotiations and that i can count on your support on wednesday. thank you for your cooperation.
for the greens/efa group madam president, i come from a country, belgium, which has been marked perhaps more than rightly by the banking crises we have experienced. this country is crisscrossed by systemic banking institutions which, of course, are transnational in nature and which are sometimes run outside our borders, when it is not the belgian institutions themselves that influence what happens in central europe, for example; i'm thinking of a bank like kbc. so we know the futility of having a banking regulatory system that is national, when we are working in a single market and with banking institutions that are transnational in nature. we have paid a heavy price, and i can only welcome the initiative initially taken by the council and translated into texts by the commission to set up this first pillar of banking union. so, while the banking union is not the alpha and omega of european integration, certainly not, it is probably the most decisive step the union is taking towards integration, towards an ever closer union between our states and our peoples. in this sense, i am glad that this step has been taken - it is not yet fully achieved, but it is an ambitious step. but there can be no question of a federal leap in europe if it is at the cost of a weakening of democracy, and we know how angry our people are rightly today against a weakening of the democratic legitimacy of decisions taken at both national and european level. from this point of view, it is true that - and i want to echo what sylvie has just said - the architectural choice of placing this integrated supervisory mechanism at the european central bank seems to us somewhat regrettable, in the sense that it is not the best way to achieve an inclusive system for the entire internal market. this is certainly not the best way of applying the famous separation of banking from monetary policy and, finally, it is certainly not the best way of ensuring democratic control of banking supervision - in writing. the european parliament urged eu governments to step up the fight against tax fraud and evasion on the eve of a summit partly devoted to the subject. it is estimated that tax fraud causes a loss of €1 trillion in the eu each year. on average, tax losses in europe today exceed the total amount spent by member states on health care and are more than four times the amount spent on education! parliament urged the twenty-seven to implement the recommendations made by the european commission, including adopting a unified approach to tax havens and blacklisting them, with the main objective of halving the tax gap by 2020. the uk, which will host the g8 summit next month, has made the fight against tax evasion a priority. so perhaps it is time for europe to put its own house in order and convince austria and switzerland, even if the solution has to be global.
in writing. these frauds shift the tax burden onto workers and low and middle income households. in addition, they force the public authorities to make cuts in public services. the consequences are even more pronounced in countries where the socioeconomic situation is dire. in greece, for example, large companies have transferred €60 billion out of the country since 1 january 2012 in order to benefit from tax breaks. the total cost of tax fraud is higher than the combined health budgets of the union. stopping tax evasion would wipe out all the deficits in just nine years. we must act! national measures alone cannot remedy this scourge; a coherent, concrete and common european strategy on taxation is essential the massive tax evasion and avoidance by large companies has a serious impact on small businesses and individuals, who are subject to an additional tax burden as a result of these offences. the proposed rules must now be enforced so that honest citizens and honest businesses do not pay for the big companies that cheat!
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it is also a political signal to tomorrow's euro summit. if we ask the european citizens to bear the burden of heavy savings, we must be able to assure the citizens that everyone is making a correct and fair contribution. i would like to take this opportunity to remind you of the ambitious agenda we adopted by a large majority on 19 april 2012 on the introduction of the ccctb, the common consolidated corporate tax base. the eu's corporate tax system would become more transparent. the eu-wide consolidation of profit and loss will make it more difficult to abuse interpricing, avoid taxation and set up tax structures. it is therefore important that the council work on the implementation of the ccctb as soon as possible. the need for the correct application of tax rules requires the legislator to introduce the best possible tax rules and to pursue the most optimal functioning of the internal market. if we make it easier and cheaper to expand a business across borders, we can then demand with greater authority that everyone pays the taxes they owe. good governance and fiscal justice go hand in hand.
in writing. tax policy is, let us not forget, the responsibility of the member states and not the eu. however, a more intensive exchange of information, the application of minimum standards of good governance at the tax level, and a more coordinated approach between member states are required at international level to combat aggressive tax planning and tax havens. i have been advocating for many years that the tax on labour should be reduced. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the situation of the elderly. it discourages employment and investment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it suggests, as a possible solution to the problems mentioned, the establishment of an intelligent and coordinated 'tax snake' system which, rather than trying to harmonise the various national tax systems, would aim to coordinate them taking into account the tax reductions and increases introduced in each country. as a reminder, the recent debt crisis has raised several new problems in the european union, and their resolution requires an adequate adjustment of fiscal policies in the short, medium and long term. some countries have already made these adjustments, while others are still in the process of doing so. it is imperative to stress that tax policy remains a competence of national sovereignty and that it is therefore necessary to respect the various tax systems in force in the member states. in addition, obstacles to the internal market and uncertainties and misunderstandings arising from legal gaps should be removed as soon as possible.
in writing. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union was drawn up by a convention held from 17 december 1999 to 2 october 2000 and brought together representatives of the european parliament, the member states, national parliaments and the commission; it was proclaimed on 7 december 2000 and the text was adopted in strasbourg on 12 december 2007. a second convention was organised between 22 february 2002 and 18 july 2003 to draw up the draft treaty establishing a constitution for europe, the substance of which was, in its entirety, taken up by the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009. these two conventions were convened to deal with major issues relating to the constitutional order of the european union, including the adoption of a binding text setting out the fundamental principles and rights recognised by the union. it was therefore not necessary to convene a convention to examine the proposal to extend to the czech republic protocol no 30 on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to poland and the united kingdom, as this proposal would have little or no effect.
in writing. protocol no 30 does not exempt the united kingdom and poland from the binding provisions of the charter. this is not a "non-participation clause". it does not change the charter. however, as things stand, the protocol does not appear to alter the legal situation which would prevail in its absence. however, the very existence of this protocol is a source of legal uncertainty and political confusion. in this respect, it affects all member states adversely, not just the united kingdom, poland or even the czech republic. it is also perfectly clear that if protocol no 30 were ever to be interpreted as having the effect of limiting the scope or force of the provisions of the charter, the result would be a weakening of the protection of fundamental rights granted to polish and british citizens, which would run counter to the efforts of the union to maintain a uniformly high level of protection.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on the regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters, which is part of a package of legislative measures to strengthen the rights of victims in the european union. it thus responds to the need to adopt a european legal framework allowing for the recognition of all victims of crime, as well as the highest possible level of protection within the eu. the proposal for a regulation complements, at civil level, the directive which allows for the mutual recognition of protection measures in criminal matters. the combined application of the two instruments, criminal and civil, will allow persons covered by a protection measure to move freely and safely within the european union and will ultimately lead to the strengthening and development of the area of freedom, security and justice in the union. a process is provided for, for example, to ensure not only a quick and simple recognition of protection measures in another member state, but also to facilitate their enforcement. the mechanism will also reduce the administrative burden for victims and ensure that they are protected when travelling to or settling in another member state.
in writing. i support the general idea of the regulation on mutual recognition of protection measures. but i also think it is essential to take a closer look at the problem of victims of gender-based violence. for this purpose, reference is made to the provisions contained in the proposal for a directive on the rights of victims. to better meet the needs of victims of gender-based violence, i would like to see appropriate training for civil servants who may have to deal with cases where a person's physical, psychological or sexual integrity could be threatened - particularly cases of violence against women. the work of civil society including ngos, women's associations and other voluntary organisations providing specialist assistance is recognised by the member states, which are encouraged to support and work with these organisations providing assistance to victims of violence, including women.
in writing. the eu-canada agreement is part of a broader process and strengthening of activities in the field of supply chain security and risk management over the past decade. the union's vision and policies to increase global supply chain security have been based on enhanced and multi-component risk analysis and management to target and inspect high-risk consignments. the rapporteur welcomes this risk-based approach to ensuring the security of global supply chains, which facilitates legitimate international trade without imposing an unnecessary economic burden on authorities or trading partners. it therefore encourages the european union to conclude a mutual recognition agreement with canada. the new customs cooperation agreement with canada develops and extends the scope of customs cooperation between the two developed partners. however, that does not mean that we will accept ceta if it endangers the freedoms of european citizens!
in writing. in order to ensure that the european banking authority is fully functional within the new banking union, which will certainly increase its workload, sufficient human and budgetary resources should be provided. in the more general context of the commission's proposals for banking union, it seems to me that part of the ecb's budget for its new supervisory activities should be set by the budgetary authority (parliament and council), as these are tasks which have nothing to do with the ecb's main task, namely the conduct of an independent monetary policy. the treaty provisions specifying that the ecb's budget is not part of the union budget were intended to guarantee the ecb's independence in the conduct of its monetary policy. from a budgetary point of view, the new functions which fall within the scope of the internal market should therefore be considered as forming part of the union budget and be subject to the same decisions as the union budget.

in writing. the eu's generalised system of preferences (gsp) gives non-reciprocal trade preferences to developing countries. in this context, exporters from these countries benefit from a reduction of duties on all or part of their exports to the union. this system gives these countries vital access to the union's markets and contributes to the growth of their economies. however, the sgp states that these preferences may be temporarily suspended in the event of serious and systematic violations of principles laid down in international conventions. these concern fundamental rights at work, such as ilo convention 29 on forced labour. in this context, the tariff preferences granted to myanmar/burma under the gsp were suspended in 1997 due to the widespread practice of forced labour. since 2011, myanmar/burma has undertaken serious efforts to open up and reform. following the ilo conclusions confirming these results, the council lifted the sanctions and, by this proposal, re-established the country's participation in the gsp. i therefore supported this proposal.
in writing. the union negotiates investment protection agreements with third countries such as canada, the united states, japan, india and china. these investment agreements are likely to provide for an investor-state dispute settlement mechanism allowing companies to bring claims against the union in the event of a breach of certain key provisions of the investment agreements. this regulation aims to create a legal framework in the event that an investor brings a case against the union. who is the defendant, the union or the member state? who's got to pay? the main issue in this case is a dispute between the member states and the commission over the allocation of powers in the field of investment policy. several member states, in particular germany, finland and the netherlands, wish to leave the member states with maximum powers. our group, on the other hand, is clearly on the community side and supports the commission's strong role in defending the union in investment arbitration cases.

in writing. a country may be excluded from the gsp in the case of serious and systematic violations of human and/or labour rights, in breach of the main international conventions. in 1997, burma was therefore temporarily suspended from the gsp due to widespread forced labour practices, in violation of ilo conventions. burma, because of its level of development, is eligible for the special arrangement for the least developed countries and could therefore export its products duty-free (except arms), but because of its suspension, exports from the country are subject to the taxes and quotas in force in europe. this therefore deprives burma of significant export opportunities within a key market such as the european union and effectively limits the country's growth and development prospects. under eu law, preferences can be recovered as soon as the international reference authority confirms that the 'serious and systematic violations' of human rights and labour law have ceased. in the case of burma, the ilo must ensure that the practice of forced labour is no longer practised in the country.

400 000 new cases a year - and who must follow a regular diet with medical supervision. i would like to mention three concrete achievements which are a real step forward compared to the situation we have today. the scope of application will now be limited, and strictly limited, to the categories of population that really need these specific foods: newborns and children under three years of age, obese patients and long-term ill or hospitalized patients. this means that all other food products, cereal bars, snacks, meal replacements, etc. - and there are dozens, even hundreds - will be transferred to the general food regulation, the general food law of 2002, which is a good thing as abuses are known in the labelling of these foods that use and sometimes abuse the health argument without actually being specific foods. which also means that growth milks marketed for babies aged 12 to 36 months as well as products for athletes - it's hard to define what an athlete is, isn't it? will wait at least a few years before eventually bearing this 'special food' label. other products also covered by our work and by this legislation are those products which are aimed at food intolerances (gluten intolerance, lactose intolerance) and which were one of the priorities of our committee's work. these products will now be incorporated into the food information to consumer regulations which already provide -
