in writing. the fish stocks of the north sea are a real source of food for european citizens. it is therefore essential to ensure that fisheries are ecologically sustainable, in line with economic and social objectives, and that this long-term plan contributes to the availability of food resources. a precautionary approach to fisheries management must therefore be applied to ensure that the exploitation of marine biological resources maintains populations of species fished above levels that can produce maximum long-term yield.
in writing. the european union is the third largest player in the global fishing industry and has always been a pioneer in the fight against illegal fishing. some species are particularly threatened, such as the endangered cod. the special management plan for its conservation, put in place in 2008, imposed automatic annual fishing quotas. a very controversial plan because of its impact on employment and the survival of the fisheries. that is why parliament adopted its revision this afternoon, with the aim of making it more flexible by introducing exceptions on a case-by-case basis and implementing a gradual phase-out of cod discards to stop the excessive mortality of the species. it is essential that europe should fight on two fronts, namely ensuring the survival of fisheries on the one hand and ensuring the preservation of natural resources on the other. i wonder, however, whether it is appropriate for parliament to legislate on a case-by-case basis for different species of fish. it would probably be more consistent and effective to leave the matter in the hands of the commission and its fisheries experts.
in writing. as this regulation is one of the first acts in the fisheries sector to be aligned with the feu treaty, it is particularly important to find a solution with a sound legal basis that guarantees the rights granted to parliament by the lisbon treaty. in addition, the solutions adopted for this regulation may influence the decision-making process applicable to other multiannual plans. the rapporteur broadly endorses the commission proposal in that it suggests the use of delegated acts to adapt fishing mortality rates and spawning biomass levels to scientific findings; to adjust the fishing effort in the event of the exclusion of a group of vessels from the effort management regime or the reintroduction of that group into the regime; to specify the rules on the method of calculating fishing capacity and adjust the maximum capacity levels; to lay down rules on the method of calculation allowing member states to adapt the maximum allowable fishing effort in connection with quota management and following a transfer of fishing effort between effort groups.

in writing. directive 2003/8/ec was a very important piece of legislation to ensure that europeans with less financial means also have access to justice in other member states. however, only 12% of citizens are aware of this right, so it is important to make people aware of its existence so that they can benefit from it. in addition, a competent legal service must be established, including directories of legal practitioners with language and comparative law skills and access to legal aid in the country of residence or the country where the dispute occurred, in order to deal properly with cross-border cases. improving access to justice in the union is essential, which is why i supported this text.
in writing. in order to improve the levels of competence, member states could also consider designating a single transmitting or receiving authority for each jurisdiction, so that the officials required to handle such cases have sufficient experience in this field. where cross-border legal aid is managed in a decentralised manner, the different offices often have only a small number of cases to deal with, which means that the officials concerned do not have the opportunity to acquire the necessary experience to deal with such applications effectively. another problem that is currently being raised is that there are disparities between member states as regards the thresholds applied and the guidelines for the granting of legal aid. it follows that a person could be entitled to legal aid in his member state of residence but not in the member state where the dispute occurred. applicants should have the possibility to qualify for legal aid either in the member state of residence or in the member state where such aid is required. this would allow each authority to apply its own thresholds and set its own guidelines.

in writing. i welcome the report by mrs frédérique ries, which is the culmination of a long-term effort. food is health. the legislative framework had to be simplified and the food policy updated in the light of recent technological innovations in this field. the report sets out stricter provisions, in particular on product labelling, which are essential for the protection of consumers and the most vulnerable groups. the reform of this legislation will enable consumers to make informed and healthy food choices, and labelling will no longer be able to mislead them.
in writing. following the adoption of the parliament's first reading position in plenary on 14 june 2012, informal negotiations with the cypriot presidency have started with a view to reaching an agreement at an early second reading. after three rounds of trilogue, the negotiating team of parliament and the council reached an agreement on this matter on 14 november 2012. the text of the agreement was submitted to the envi committee for a vote of approval on 18 december 2012 and was approved by a very large majority. in view of this approval by the committee, the chairman of the committee decided, in his letter to the chairman of coreper on the same day, to recommend to the plenary session that the council's position at first reading be approved without amendment. after a linguistic check, the council adopted the position at first reading confirming the agreement on 22 april 2013. since the council's position at first reading is in line with the agreement reached at the trilogues, we have followed the rapporteur's recommendation that the committee adopt it without amendments.
in writing. the financial crisis and budgetary constraints should not be used as an excuse for a reduction in the protection of workers. electromagnetic fields have short- and long-term effects on the health of workers and it was therefore essential to take measures to protect them. the derogations provided for in this report also allow the electromagnetic fields to be maintained in certain areas such as magnetic resonance imaging, which is of crucial importance for the detection of a whole range of diseases.
in writing. this afternoon, the european parliament did a great deal for the protection of workers by adopting the report by mrs morin-chartier on exposure to electromagnetic fields. the legislation, which has been awaited for many years by medical personnel, now provides workers with a comprehensive safety net, as it is in addition to the directives on noise, vibration and chemical agents. this delay was largely explained by the strong concerns raised by the original 2004 directive which directly impacted the use of medical imaging (primarily mri). that is why it was important not to break the dynamic of non-radiation imaging research, when we know its importance, for example in the recent advances in diseases such as alzheimer's. so i say "bravo" to the mri waiver. the european commission must do more and from now on seriously consider the long-term health effects of exposure to electromagnetic fields. these are waves which are invisible, inaudible and odourless, but which are increasingly worrying european citizens. for one simple reason: we are immersed in a cocktail of waves, 18 hours a day. it's anything but insignificant!
in writing. health and safety at work is one of the main concerns of business leaders. but while these issues have long been integrated by large companies, smes still have difficulty in seeing the value of implementing a health and safety policy. however, failure to comply with these two principles can have serious consequences for the business. increasingly encouraged by legislation that emphasises the employer's responsibility for safety, small businesses are starting to take an interest in the issue and to discover the organisational, financial, human and image gains that can be the key.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. when determining the course to be followed in order to modify the cod stock plan, we must take into account the opinion of the scientists, who, as noted above, believe that the current plan has not produced the expected results. the interested parties would no doubt agree. the amendments to the commission proposal aim to achieve the objective of restoring cod stocks while ensuring that the actors concerned win the support of the commission. it should be noted that the implementation of a new long-term plan for cod stocks is widely seen as an interim measure, and that the objective is to replace this plan with multi-species fisheries plans, when scientific progress allows. as the current levels of fisheries management vary from one area to another, the timing of the transition to multi-specific plans for all areas covered by the cod plan remains uncertain. there is therefore an urgent need to improve the existing plan and make progress in this area.
in writing. − it is good that this report lists clear measures against the online gambling mafia. after all, online gambling is growing at a rapid pace and is increasingly being used by organised crime organisations to launder money. this has made the danger of match-fixing in sport much more acute, as several bribery scandals in european football in recent years have clearly shown. the fight against such practices must be stepped up urgently. we must further increase cooperation and coordination at european level. a number of measures are crucial in this respect. the european commission should adapt the european legislation on money laundering so that it also applies to sports betting. gambling on home matches should be banned and there should be a protection mechanism for whistleblowers. in addition, it is necessary to establish a specialised european 'match fixing unit' which can disseminate and exchange all information on cross-border online gambling activities between the different member states and stakeholders. finally, member states need to harmonise their criminal laws so that match-fixing is treated as a serious crime throughout the eu.
in writing. organized crime is a real threat to the security and freedom of european citizens. its related activities are undermining the european economy by diverting billions of euros from the economy every year, to the detriment of european taxpayers. these are transnational crimes which require action in close cooperation with the competent authorities. to combat such phenomena means to guarantee the freedoms of our european citizens, but also their well-being. the european union must act without further delay because we cannot tolerate these criminals to impose a sword of damocles on our economies.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. organized crime is no longer a phenomenon limited by historical and territorial boundaries: the traditional mafia-like organizations present in certain regions of southern europe have gradually expanded their sphere of action, exploiting the opportunities offered by economic globalization and new technologies, by allying themselves with criminal groups from other countries and other continents, by sharing the market and areas of influence, in the context of innumerable criminal activities and prospects for profits. the impact on local economies, societies and institutions is increasingly evident in different regions. organized crime has become a player in the global economy, taking advantage of huge illicit competitive advantages and polluting the real economy through fraud. violence and intimidation are now part of the normal activities of organized crime, along with corruption. money laundering is also a common side effect of the activities of organised crime and is closely linked to corruption, tax evasion and tax avoidance. it follows that organized crime, corruption and money laundering are often linked by objective evidence.
in writing. housing is a primary good and access to it is an inalienable right. having a decent housing is a prerequisite for a productive life. the current crisis is creating significant financial pressures and increasing demand for social housing in europe. the need for social housing is increasingly affecting people and now also those with average incomes. the construction of more social housing will boost the economy and employment and improve the energy efficiency of the housing sector in general. social housing should not be grouped together like ghettos but should instead be spread over the whole territory, which would avoid social segregation. finally, i would like to thank the rapporteur for emphasizing the importance of giving priority to single mothers in the allocation of social housing on the same basis as other vulnerable groups.
in writing. - i support this report on social housing because it provides a lever against the growing poverty in europe. some 25 million europeans are housed in social housing and waiting lists are long. in flanders, only 6% of the housing stock is social housing. however, social housing meets the right to adequate and affordable housing for all in several respects. in addition, all new housing must be low-energy. low-income households are particularly affected by high energy bills due to inefficient heating appliances and/or poor insulation. we call on the european commission to create a regulatory framework to better coordinate national housing policies and to include social housing as a touchstone in the budgetary control of the union. europe also needs to urgently develop a strategy to combat homelessness. we ask national parliaments to impose minimum quotas for social housing, with a view to social diversity within the neighbourhoods themselves. the evictions of the poorest people must also become more difficult, especially during the winter period. finally, we call on the european ministers for housing to meet at least once a year and to evaluate policy or progress in consultation with the partners concerned.
in writing. it seems clear to me that there is a social emergency to invest in the social housing sector. europe is experiencing a serious housing crisis which persists and may be widening despite the shocks which regularly strike european public opinion at the time of winter when the situation for the homeless seems untenable. social inequalities are widening, unemployment is skyrocketing, 120 million europeans are poor or at risk of poverty, and the private housing market is becoming less responsive to the growing demand from the most precarious households across europe. sufficient supply of social housing helps to mitigate the magnitude of property cycles and property bubbles that destabilise economies. investments in social housing need to be better reflected in the union's macroeconomic and budgetary surveillance system. the added value of the structural funds and european investment bank loans to stimulate investment in social housing should be emphasised. these funds make it possible in particular to develop continuing and vocational training in the green sectors and to create thousands of local, decent and non-delocalizable jobs.
in writing. - i abstained from the final vote on this own-initiative report on social housing in the european union, not because i do not believe in the absolute necessity of good social housing, but simply because this report goes against the division of powers between the member states and the european union, and moreover does not offer adequate solutions to the existing problems. social housing is a crucial part of social policy and needs to be given extra attention in these times of crisis. however, the formulation and implementation of social housing policy is primarily a matter for the member states, so that account can be taken of the wide disparities between member states in terms of both housing and institutional organisation.

in writing. in the coming years, europe will face major challenges in making the labour market even more open and accessible. firstly, there is the objective of vocational mobility, which highlights the need to better adapt education and training systems to the new requirements of the labour market, to stimulate lifelong training and the acquisition of skills and to improve the mechanisms for the recognition of vocational qualifications. secondly, the still too low degree of labour mobility between member states shows that the benefits of the internal market are not yet fully exploited. in many cases, changing jobs can mean more than just changing one company for another, or even one sector for another: it can also mean starting a new career or a new trade. it is therefore essential to ensure that the mix of learning opportunities meets the requirements of ensuring employability and adaptability of employees throughout their working lives, which is one way of increasing their capacity for occupational mobility.

in writing. illicit, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing is a major threat to the sustainable exploitation of aquatic biodiversity by depleting fish stocks, destroying marine habitats and distorting competition for honest fishermen. it is therefore necessary to limit access to the european market to products from certified fisheries that comply with the regulations in force. this text, which i fully support, aims to prevent, eradicate and discourage iuu fishing in eu and international waters.
in writing. - i voted today in favour of a report by my green colleague, raoul romeva, which aims to combat illegal and unregulated fishing. it accounts for about a third of the world's fish catch and is the backbone of any policy to make fishing more sustainable. and that is precisely what the european parliament is trying to achieve together with the european commission, environmental organisations and some member states. the text adopted today provides for a rapid procedure to blacklist countries which do not cooperate in combating illegal fishing. the european commission can now add more countries to the existing list of eight (belize, cambodia, fiji, guinea, panama, sri lanka, togo and vanuatu). this is a means of pressure to put countries that don't seem to care about sustainable fishing, like south korea, in the right direction, because once they are on the list, they will be subject to possible sanctions. although the eu itself has drawn up strict rules, illegal fishing remains a problem, with south korean vessels fishing in african waters, for example, as well as in parts of the european fleet. some european shipowners have ships flying the flags of countries on the blacklist and engage in illegal practices.
in writing. from an economic point of view, illegal fishing can often be a lure. because it is caught without respecting ecological and social standards, among other things, it is usually sold by fishermen at a lower price. wholesale and retailers prefer to buy cheap, although they may not know that the fish has been caught illegally. that is why there is relatively strong opposition to the regulation on illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. it is easy to oppose illegal fishing on principle. however, illegal fishing becomes much more difficult to counter when opposing it may result in interruptions in the supply of fish to the union market, a decrease in profits or interference in trade with 'important' trading partners of the union. i am generally satisfied with the commission's choices in this matter when it proposes amendments. however, i consider that, where recourse to delegated acts is proposed, the delegation of power should be limited in time in order to allow for a regular evaluation of its use.

i voted for the report on eurodac because it can be a useful instrument in the fight against illegal immigration, against organised crime and against terrorism. it is good that the police services of the member states can have access to the data of eurodac. the left in this parliament is opposing this without offering any alternative. i do have reservations about a number of amendments which have been incorporated in this proposal. for example, amendment no 41, which states that the fact that a person is temporarily or permanently unable to provide usable fingerprints should not have a negative impact on the legal situation of that person or on his application for international protection. such a thing could open the door wide to abuse. what if people refuse to give a fingerprint and dress that refusal as an impossibility? people with bad intentions will eagerly take advantage of it.
in writing. the aim of the asylum package voted on today was to harmonise european asylum policy so that every asylum seeker who needs protection gets it. in this way, every asylum seeker would have the same rights and equal treatment of his or her asylum application in each member state. however, this objective has been completely eroded by the member states, which means that there is no longer any question of an efficient and humane treatment of asylum seekers. the dublin iii regulation, the procedural and reception directives were already approved in the parliamentary committee. i am voting against the eurodac regulation today because it encourages discrimination and criminalisation of asylum seekers. the eurodac regulation concerns the storage of fingerprints of asylum seekers and the use of these data in the database. police services, including europol, could use this data in the fight against terrorism and organised crime. even after asylum seekers obtain status, their data is retained for three years instead of being deleted immediately. the greens maintain that law enforcement and bodies such as europol should have as little access to the database as possible and that it should be strictly controlled. because asylum seekers are not criminals, they're just running away.
in writing. third country organised crime networks attempt to abuse the asylum system in order to bring criminal members of a network into a member state of the union and to make contacts with them in the course of their criminal activities. once on the territory of a member state, these members of the organised crime network apply for asylum under false identities in order to be able to stay legally in the european union with a clean criminal record. in addition, reports suggest that traffickers also attempt to abuse the asylum system by lodging asylum applications by lying about their country of origin. to address these concerns, i welcome the possibility for the designated authorities of the member states and the european police office (europol) to request the comparison of fingerprint data according to a match/non-match system with those recorded in the eurodac database for the fight against terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences. i believe that giving access to eurodac for law enforcement purposes is a significant step forward compared to the previous proposal. i support the commission's proposal, however.
the report on common rules on the temporary reintroduction of internal border controls in exceptional circumstances is a measure for nothing, as is the commission's proposal. this report further weakens the commission's already weak proposal, inter alia by amendment no 4, which states, and i quote, 'complete freedom of movement within the area without internal border controls must be guaranteed and the reintroduction of internal border controls by member states for political reasons must be avoided'. this is a perfect summary of the alien philosophy of eu meddling. a philosophy which in no way takes account of the situation on the ground. the member states must once again be able to determine who enters their territory and under what conditions, and all without eu interference.
in writing. − the free movement of persons is one of the european union's most important and tangible achievements. but that free movement and open borders are only sustainable if security is also guaranteed. our area without internal frontiers can only be sustained if it is accompanied by far-reaching and intensive cooperation between the member states in the field of justice and police. criminals are using open borders as a tool to evade police forces, whose powers are often limited to their own national territory. for example, the border region in south-west flanders and northern france is all too often confronted with criminals who commit robberies just across the border and then disappear as quickly as possible across the border, where they can no longer be apprehended efficiently by the police of the neighbouring country. therefore, it is important that member states also have the possibility to temporarily reintroduce border controls as a last resort when there is a serious threat to internal security, in particular as a result of organised crime.
in writing. − the free movement of persons is one of the european union's greatest achievements, and eu citizens benefit from the possibility of travelling from one member state to another without being stopped or checked at the border. the schengen agreement is therefore an important building block of european union unity. the reform of the schengen area is an essential subject of this report. in order to ensure the free movement of eu citizens and to avoid unilateral and opaque national decisions, uniform rules for the reintroduction of border controls should be established in the future. these arrangements do include the exceptional cases and the time limit which member states may provide for the reintroduction of border controls at the internal borders of the eu. however, the decision to reintroduce border controls remains a matter for the member states alone. i welcome that as well as the fact that it is envisaged that the eu commission should monitor the actions of the member states.
in writing. migration as such is not a threat to public order and national security. zero immigration does not exist, has never existed and will never exist. no coercive, repressive or security measures can ever prevent a person from taking his chances elsewhere to secure the minimum of dignity to which every human being legitimately aspires. migration flows alone cannot justify the reintroduction of internal border controls. the right to free movement may not be affected by a decision of either member state. the schengen borders code already allows for the reintroduction of internal border controls in the event of a serious threat to public policy and internal security. the new possibility of reintroducing internal border controls must remain an exception and can only be possible as a last resort following persistent shortcomings in external border controls. the commission will then make the proposal after an in-depth evaluation. free movement is one of the most important achievements of european integration. the commission's proposal is to be based on the principle of subsidiarity, which is the basis for the european union's policy on the environment.
in writing. free movement is a founding principle of the european union, and the ability to move within the union without having to undergo internal border controls is one of its greatest achievements. i would stress that immigration, in itself, does not constitute a threat to public order and national security. i therefore categorically oppose any attempt to introduce new grounds, such as migration flows, to justify the reintroduction of internal border controls. the root cause of these problems is not external but internal. indeed, these recent events are symptomatic of the fact that the current schengen system, which is based on an intergovernmental peer review system, is not strong enough to address the weaknesses of some of its members and to prevent possible abuses. the european union must now act to ensure that such events cannot happen again and that the proportionality of any measure to reintroduce internal border controls is properly assessed, as requested by the european council in june last year.
i voted against the coelho report because it shows a profound alienation from the world. for example, amendment no 3 states, and i quote, 'the schengen area is one of the greatest achievements of the union and is most appreciated by citizens because it guarantees free movement'. we might wonder if this is a passage from a satirical text. we might wonder if it's meant to be sarcastic. if schengen is indeed one of the greatest achievements of the union, then the union must be urgently and fundamentally called into question. the internal border controls have been abolished, but the external borders are as leaky as a sieve. all of this leads to even more immigration nuisance and a plaster on a wooden leg, like setting up an evaluation mechanism, will not change that at all.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which introduces a genuine community method for assessing the application of the schengen rules. the method used to be purely intergovernmental and the european commission will now be much more involved in the evaluation process. there will be more scope for compelling member states which are resistant to compliance with all agreements to incorporate corrective processes into their national policies. the commission's evaluation action will also be monitored by parliament, which implies better democratic control and greater transparency.
in writing. − the reform adopted today is an excellent way of strengthening the mobility of european citizens. i am pleased that the european commission, as guardian of the european treaties, is now given the opportunity to identify serious shortcomings in the application of the schengen rules and to propose solutions, with the involvement of the council and the european parliament. this should prevent trade-offs between member states over border controls and provide more leverage in situations that put great pressure on countries. the circumstances in which border controls may be used as a last resort are now more clearly defined. the eu must do more. strengthening external border controls through a reinforcement of frontex and a common european asylum and migration policy are both necessary to maintain freedom of movement without internal border controls. fortunately, the community method has succeeded in this case. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. finally, we have managed to find a balanced european approach without sacrificing the prerogatives of the member states to be able to do what is necessary in exceptional circumstances to guarantee public order or internal security.
in writing. i consider this new mechanism more european, more transparent, more efficient and more rigorous to be a huge step forward compared to the current situation. it provides the tools to identify and correct, from the outset, any shortcomings in the application of the schengen rules by member states, thus contributing to the preservation of the schengen area as an area without internal borders and to the protection of the free movement of citizens. for all these reasons, and in view of the satisfactory guarantees given as regards the institutional role of the european parliament, i nevertheless approve of this compromise.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text. i believe that annual financial statements prepared in accordance with the principle of prudence should give a true picture of the financial position of the company. annual financial statements have different objectives and do not simply provide information to investors on capital markets but also report on past transactions and serve corporate governance. european accounting rules must strike a fair balance between the interests of the recipients of the financial statements and the interest of an undertaking not to be unduly burdened with information requirements.
in writing. transparency of information in a company is a good indicator of the dynamism of the governance of that company. country-by-country reporting is of considerable importance to extractive companies but also to investors promoting good governance at the global level. therefore, in order to promote transparency, equal conditions of competition throughout the eu and the opening up of financial markets, i wholeheartedly support this text.
in writing. in a context of increasing volatility in global financial markets, investors are increasingly demanding information on investor practices. it is clear that they want more transparency so that they can have a complete economic picture of investments and risks. in addition, transparency in terms of the publication of information is a good indicator of the dynamism of corporate governance. companies are increasingly adopting corporate governance standards, including transparency, by joining global reporting systems such as the extractive industries transparency initiative (eiti), in addition to voluntary guidelines for multinational companies. in the light of all these initiatives, there is a risk that the question of transparency will now be answered in a fragmented way. this legislative proposal is part of the european union's corporate responsibility initiative and follows on from work on financial sector reform, the main objective of which is to promote the transparency and openness of financial markets and to establish higher standards of corporate governance.

in writing. competition policy is an integral part of the union's genetic code. the three instruments of competition policy aim to maintain a level playing field and an open and dynamic market. this encourages companies to seek success on their own merits (price, quality and innovation) in order to meet the needs, preferences and wishes of intermediate and final consumers. the european social market economy would be unthinkable without competition. competition allows for fair price formation, proper allocation and use of resources and social progress. from a strategic point of view, it is fundamental for the survival of the union's businesses, economy and societal model in a globalised world. it is a matter of values and therefore of added value. to succeed, competition policy needs greater legitimacy and efficiency. progress requires involving the european parliament in the formulation of competition policy, ensuring that the commission has sufficient resources and enhancing the involvement of civil society stakeholders. our ambition is to consolidate the culture of competition in the union and in the world.

in writing. the turkish authorities must take urgent measures to prevent further injuries, to enforce the fundamental rights of protesters and to ensure the safety of the population as a whole. other civil society organisations have taken similar action. the extremely brutal repression of the totally peaceful demonstrations in taksim square is truly outrageous. it has greatly aggravated the situation on the streets of istanbul, where dozens of people have been injured. european observers found that water cannons were used against both peaceful protesters and those who threw stones at police. the inappropriate use of tear gas has had particularly devastating effects on the safety of protesters, causing countless injuries. some protesters were seriously wounded in the head after being hit by tear gas canisters fired by the police. at the protest site, the ground is still littered with hundreds of empty tear gas canisters.

on behalf of the s&d group, president, commissioner, first of all i would like to thank the three rapporteurs and apologize to our shadow rapporteur, mrs ţicău. unfortunately, she was unable to attend today. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the frequency of checks is based on a middle ground: four two two. we were in principle in favour, commissioner, of going for four-two-one, but we did not get enough support for that. but as you know, it remains possible for member states to carry out more frequent checks and therefore to be more stringent. as you know, there has been a great deal of discussion on the introduction of new types of vehicles into the system. my group is in principle in favour of developing tests for this in a generalised way throughout europe, because figures show that in countries which have introduced tests for motor vehicles there are indeed positive effects which reduce the number of accidents. i also know that a lot of motorists are fighting this and are very upset about it, but it is for their own safety and the safety of other road users that we have to go in that direction. the least we could do if we don't find a majority for that is do some extra study; we would then be able to come up with new proposals at a later stage if necessary. it is a positive thing that the caravans are also being integrated, for example, and that the directives are being refined as regards inspection equipment, training of inspectors, etc. it is also important - and this is the last point i want to make - that a number of positive points are added to the parliament's proposal on meter fraud, which should be generalized.
for the greens/efa group mr president, i shall deal with one point only, namely the technical inspection of two- and three-wheel motor vehicles, as provided for in the commission's proposal. the number of victims has dropped sharply in europe, and that's very good. nevertheless, motorcyclists are still overrepresented among the victims and, in particular, among the injured. i think it is therefore difficult to imagine that two- and three-wheel vehicles, because they have one less wheel than four-wheel vehicles, are exempt from technical inspection. i think motorcycles, especially big motorcycles, are as sophisticated as cars today. so, since nobody is disputing the technical control of cars, i don't see why, because we have one or two wheels less, we should escape this importance of technical control. although technical failures are only rarely the cause of motorcycle accidents, independent studies show that in five to ten per cent of cases they greatly aggravate the circumstances. so i don't really understand why we are deviating from this commission proposal, and i am defending the idea here that an amendment has been tabled to the effect that the date should be set at 2016 for large motorcycles, and 2018 for small ones. and the commission will show us if we must do otherwise.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i would like to thank the commission and the rapporteurs for their work. contrary to what some colleagues say, i am convinced that we need european regulation here. it's the holiday season. imagine if today the technical inspections were different in 27 countries and then they had to be repeated in each country. you should explain this to your citizens at home, that europe can also make life easier and not just harder, as you always say. the technical controls, as discussed here in the past, have, as i have just said, contributed to the improvement of technology. we have never had technology as good as we have today, which also serves to improve safety. thank god, the number of fatal accidents has dropped very sharply, by up to 40 percent in the last ten years. and last but not least, there is a positive impact on the environment. we have been right in supporting all this in parliament over the last few years. but we also don't want the control to become a nuisance tomorrow. control should further support this added value. i therefore believe that - perhaps because i come from the border region - we should look for the added value of cross-border checks. we have suggested that information on, for example, vehicle mileage or major accidents involving a car should be available at least to the buyer, because it has been shown that over 80% of the figures are wrong when a used vehicle is sold cross-border. this is also the european added value that we can create with such legislation. it is a simplification for the citizen who takes it to heart. the last point: the subject of trucks has been raised. it is true that there is, of course, not only a technical aspect to truck inspections, but also a socially important aspect. because if you drive a truck like this every day, you need to know that it's technically sound. but there is another aspect to be emphasized here: our legislation at eu level can be as good as it is, if the member states do not participate and do not carry out the control themselves, it will not do any good. there is a shared responsibility here. we are carrying it at eu level, and we want the countries to carry it at home by means of good controls.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, honourable members, serious road traffic injuries are of course a real problem. around a quarter of a million people are reported to be seriously injured on eu roads every year. their lives are often changed forever. this is why the commission made the goal of reducing serious road traffic injuries a new and a key element of our road safety strategy, which was reflected already in the white paper of 2011. however, i must say that this idea met with considerable opposition from experts. new initiatives on serious injuries must be based on fact and for that we need to know how many serious injuries happen every year. the figures we have today are not reliable or comparable. member states use different definitions and methodology to gather data. there are also problems of misreporting and under-reporting. two months ago, as mr simpson mentioned, we proposed a common eu definition of serious injuries. this is a very important step forward. this will allow us to carry out the necessary cost-benefit analysis and then choose the most effective ways to reduce injuries. a common eu definition and reliable data are also a pre-requisite for setting an eu target. i very much appreciate parliament’s support for the idea of setting a strategic injury reduction target. that approach proved very useful for reducing fatalities, so i hope that we can repeat this success with reducing injuries. what happens now is that member states will collect the first figures during 2014. based on this information the commission will propose an ambitious target for reducing injuries. the areas we may want to look into together could include tools and techniques to limit the impact of a collision, to reduce the severity of injuries which cannot be avoided. this has been included to a certain degree in our proposal for the amendment of the weights and dimensions directive. as regards first-aid and emergency services: the aid received in the first hour after a crash is crucial for reducing the risk of severe consequences. again proposals have been made to introduce an ecall system and for in-depth crash injury research to support the development of safety measures and to better understand the causes of accidents. progress made towards reaching the injuries reduction target will be monitored, as will the fatality reduction target. here we have a common objective with member states. the objective of achieving a reduction in road deaths has been a common one; the work towards it has been very united, with a voluntary commitment from all actors.
i am speaking on behalf of the ppe group. the commission has already done so. i believe that all the political groups are very broadly in favour of this initiative, that road safety remains a major issue for us in the committee and that we should continue to take initiatives on this at european level. there are at least two good reasons for this: in the past, we have been able to prove through very concrete programmes and also very concrete targets that the number of deaths on the roads has been reduced by at least 40%. and if we have the courage to continue to do that in this area with the seriously injured, i believe we can achieve similar goals. and let those who think that europe is interfering too much here not intimidate you, because i believe that we can learn good things in every country and adopt good things, perhaps even in some legislation. the principle of subsidiarity has no place at all when it comes to this sensitive subject. we need really good numbers - you said that - we need reliable numbers. 70% are delivered. the figures could also be used to objectify the debates. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to give us a clear answer. but the figures can also be a guide to decision-making. if we know tomorrow that, for example, in cities where you drive 30 km/h, there are much fewer accidents, then this is information that is useful for everyone. this is not interference with the subsidiarity of the member states. we need to pay particular attention to the less protected participants. but there is a very clear insight. driving behaviour remains one of the most important aspects of accidents: 1. speed, 2. drugs, alcohol and last but not least fatigue these are aspects that are important. but what is very often underestimated and where all authorities can work together - from the european to the local level - is infrastructure. we know that the infrastructure in many countries can be used to prevent injuries and even deaths on the road. and so i hope that tomorrow we're not just supporting four-star cars, but that tomorrow we're maybe supporting four-star roads in all countries. i think it would be good for all of us.
for the greens/efa group mr president, i do not know, ladies and gentlemen, whether any of you have ever had the opportunity or the sad circumstance, in the course of a previous mandate, of going to an announcement to a family about the death of a child, the death of a person, of a close friend, in a road accident. it's a traumatic experience! and even though the numbers are better today, the reality is that it is still a massacre, and a massacre with thousands of orphans, thousands of bereaved parents. so we have to act faster and stronger. and i would like to emphasize one aspect. i welcome the commission's strategy on the wounded. i think this is a great initiative and will help us to have more standardised figures and approaches, but i would like to go further on one specific aspect, namely the protection of the most vulnerable road users. in this sense, the whole conception of the car's place in society and, particularly, in our cities, needs to be revised. this requires work on the quality and design of infrastructure, of course, but also clear choices on how to share public space. it is not just a question of space left to the car, but also a question of speed and behaviour. just as traffic congestion makes public transport less attractive, the speed and dangers of cars are a real obstacle to walking or cycling, and in particular to daily school trips. and that is why i support the european citizens' initiative to make 30 km/h a universal feature in cities. but we also need an even more comprehensive approach to the safety of vulnerable users in urban areas. i am addressing myself to you, commissioner, but this problem may also concern your successor. i think we have come a long way at european level on the issue of more stringent regulations on passenger rights. that's good. that's good. i also believe that it is time to take the right of disabled people to travel safely a step further in the next parliament. it is high time that the right to move safely as pedestrians and cyclists should also be considered as one of the priorities of the european union.
as a member of the committee on human rights, i am concerned with human rights outside the eu, but also within the union. the way spain treats basque political prisoners has long been controversial. there are reports of human rights violations, specifically the prison regime, the incarceration of terminally ill people. last week i was in the basque country with some members of my group. in the prison of the neighbouring logroño we wanted to visit one of the prominent basque political prisoners. he has a number, but he also has a face and a name: i'm not sure i understand. at the beginning of june we submitted an official written request to the competent services to see him. we never got any answers. when we tried to contact them, we were sent from the locker to the wall and stopped at the prison gate. the way in which we have been treated as members of the european parliament by the spanish authorities is quite clearly outrageous. i therefore ask the president of this parliament to call the attention of the spanish authorities to this unacceptable attitude and to demand respect for the work of members of parliament.

the fact that negotiations with the council have finally produced an acceptable compromise should not make us forget that the basic proposal adopted by the european council in february is a missed opportunity. by proposing a mff that is lower than the previous one, the european council has failed to make available the necessary resources for the objectives it has set itself, such as europe 2020, the growth pact for jobs and the new powers. and then it will be said that europe is not achieving its objectives. the reason is that the european budget is financed from national budgets. in order to meet the budgetary requirements of the european union, member states must save money and they want to do so on the european contribution. this is included in their budget as an expense. the only way out of this schizophrenic situation is to return to the treaties which stipulate that the european budget must be financed from own resources. new own resources for the eu will be accompanied by a reduction in the gni contribution, which will provide relief for national budgets. an intermediate step could be to place eu contributions outside the national budget and not to count towards the national deficit. this contribution will then be definitively acquired for the european union. the gni contribution will then be eligible for consideration as union own resources. this will immediately guarantee full flexibility at european level and put an end to a difficult debate on payment appropriations. finally, we must also abandon unanimity, because that is the way to negotiate.

in writing. − the green group decided to vote against the staff regulations for the failure to burden officials in higher grades progressively and fairly. this is evident not just in the allocation of the sacrifices demanded (the rate of the solidarity levy for example: 6% for all grades with the exclusion of grades ast 1 to ast 3 step 1 – no change from the old system – in addition to income tax, and only 7% for the two highest grades), but also in the privileges and allowances that this reform does not touch (i.e. expatriation allowance).
in writing. the reform in progress should only concern what needed to be changed. my argument is that the major reform of the statute, which has made substantial savings, was carried out a few years ago and is still having an effect and that the timetable for the adoption of the changes currently proposed should be strictly adhered to. it is vital to keep in mind the deadline of the end of 2012 as the deadline for reaching an agreement between the european parliament and the council. otherwise, when the method and the special levy expire, not only will no savings have been made, but new expenditure will have to be met, charged to the union budget.
in writing. in order to address the lack of homogeneity among member states as regards the rules governing the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of decisions in the field of nuclear damage, the commission has committed itself to extending, in a future proposal, the solution of giving priority to union rules for member states which ratified the 1997 protocol before their accession to the european union, such as latvia and romania, and for member states which are parties to the paris convention. the council therefore proposes to authorise the member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention, namely bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia, to ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol. a similar solution was suggested for the protocol amending the paris convention in 2004. i agree with that.
in writing. i welcome this report as it comes in the context of the modernisation of eu state aid policy so that it contributes to both the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and the consolidation of public finances. the measures envisaged in this report will improve the handling of complaints and ensure the efficient and reliable collection of information from market players with the ultimate aim of ensuring the smooth functioning of the single market. the commission will also be able to make complaints conditional, which will make the procedure faster and more efficient and allow the european commission to concentrate on the most important cases to ensure the proper functioning of the single market.
in writing. the improvements proposed by the commission are twofold: firstly, to improve the handling of complaints and, secondly, to ensure efficient and reliable collection of information from market players. these two aspects are intended to address the problems associated with the complaint procedure and to increase the speed, efficiency and transparency of the procedure, as well as to enable the commission to focus on the 'big' cases, which are more important to ensure the proper functioning of the single market. on the whole, i fully support the commission's proposal and its objectives, and i have merely proposed a few minor amendments to the draft regulation. it is essential, in order to ensure the proper functioning of our single market and to ensure that illegal state aid does not impede competition within the european union, that the commission is provided with effective instruments to verify that member states grant state aid in accordance with the agreed rules.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of these measures on aviation. this sector is very important, not only in terms of employment, where we are talking about more than 5 million people working in this field, but also in terms of the economic figure represented by the sector. these measures are necessary to remain competitive with emerging countries, but also to maximise the use we make of the infrastructure currently available, and thus to ensure its efficiency.
in writing. − the eu is interested in maintaining a strong and competitive eu air transport sector, which provides over 5 million jobs and accounts for 2.4% of eu gdp. the sector is strongly international in character and this makes it imperative that in aviation we should look primarily for international solutions rather than european ones. the fluid management at airports and the emissions trading system are good examples. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on competition are applied in the air transport sector. the eu must be a serious negotiating partner at international level, particularly on security, environmental protection and social matters. this is reflected in particular in the bilateral air transport agreements. the eu must negotiate more closely with its partners, and bring european standards in the fields of environment, employment and safety to the forefront, as this is the only way to ensure that european aviation continues to prevail in the face of increased competition. the first important step towards this is the implementation of the single european sky. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval.
in writing. aviation is by definition cross-border and requires a common policy in the eu. a strong aviation policy at european level will advance the internal market and bring benefits to all member states while opening up new opportunities for eu airlines.
in writing. aviation has become a key sector of the european economy. it contributes €365 billion to the union's gdp and employs 5.1 million people. however, seven years after the publication of the commission communication on the development of the community's external aviation policy agenda, much remains to be done. the time has come for rapid progress in european aviation. new economic challenges are being launched from regions of the world where much more permissive legislation allows the construction of huge modern airports, which divert a large proportion of travellers from european airport platforms. the european union urgently needs to increase the capacity of its airports so as not to risk becoming less competitive than other regions experiencing exponential growth (think in particular of the asia-pacific region, the middle east and south america). investment in airport infrastructure should be seriously considered, even if demand does not yet exceed supply. the commission has also decided to extend the scope of the aid to cover the costs of the infrastructure and the maintenance of the airport infrastructure.
in writing. the global crisis has shown the importance of adequate financing for global trade. credit agencies play a vital role in supporting the interests of european exporters, but it is vital to ensure that export credit agencies operate in a transparent manner. transparency and disclosure of data at european level are crucial to make the eu's human rights and democracy policy more coherent. i therefore support the idea in this report to ask member states to include in their annual activity report an assessment of compliance with international regulations and with the rules governing eu exports.
in writing. the annual reports of the member states and the commission's evaluation of these reports do not meet parliament's expectations of being able to carry out this evaluation. this is particularly true for the reporting of annex i non-financial items, such as the treatment of environmental risks in the calculation of the oce premiums and compliance with the union's foreign policy objectives. this lack is, to some extent, not surprising. some member states are making commendable efforts to report on these difficult issues, such as germany, italy, belgium, the netherlands and denmark. however, we must recognise that there is still no established methodology for reporting non-financial items, and member states, as well as european institutions such as the european investment bank, still need to comply with the lisbon treaty requirements for proven compliance with the union's objectives for its external action.
in writing. - the hungarian government has already introduced a number of controversial reforms. the only correct course is for the european commission to continue to monitor this process and ensure that hungary, like all other member states, respects the eu's fundamental values. we do not need a new political forum, which will turn this 'state written in the stars' into a political reckoning. eu commissioner reding has proven in the past that she can tackle breaches of eu law efficiently and courageously. i assume she will in this case.
in writing. we voted by a large majority to lift the immunity of marine le pen, thus opening the way to legal proceedings against the president of the national front. racist remarks are undignified, especially when they come from the mouth of a european politician who is supposed to defend all his fellow citizens, regardless of their origin, beliefs or colour.
in writing. - the european parliament has once again shown its most narrow and intolerant side by lifting the parliamentary immunity of marine le pen. the great laureates of the sakharov prize for freedom of expression have once again shown that freedom of expression should not be granted to politically incorrect politicians who say what a great many of our citizens think. and yes, i too believe that the conditions which are already prevailing in many of our cities, where muslims are taking to the streets to pray towards mecca without being asked or given permission, are particularly disturbing and indeed resemble an occupation. however, marine le pen will have to answer to a court of law. in any case, don't ask me to be present at the sakharov prize ceremony. dissident sakharov, faced with so much cowardice and hypocrisy, would probably turn in his grave.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the parliament's resolution on the statute of the european foundation. these foundations pursue public interest objectives, for example in the fields of health, education and research. this new status will make it easier for the foundations to develop cross-border projects and pool their resources. this new statute also gives these foundations a clear european character.
in writing. the foundations are active in key areas such as research and health. they also have a significant economic impact on the whole of the european territory and create jobs for nearly one million people throughout the european union. however, they face difficulties in acting across national barriers on cross-border projects. the creation of a european foundation statute will facilitate the cross-border activities of foundations and enable them to support causes of public interest more effectively across the eu. such a status will also make it possible to put greater resources at the disposal of the member states in key areas such as training, research, social action, health, culture and the environment.
in writing. we encourage member states to take advantage of this current momentum to work towards the comprehensive and rapid introduction of the statute, with full guarantees of transparency, to remove obstacles to the cross-border activity of foundations and to encourage the creation of new foundations that meet the needs of persons residing in the territory of the union or pursuing missions of public utility or general interest. it should also be stressed that the creation of such a statute would contribute to the implementation of genuine european citizenship and would pave the way for the elaboration of a statute for the european association.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which updates the eu's port state system, an update which is necessary to reflect the new conventions that have been adopted in recent years, including the maritime labour convention adopted by the international labour organisation in 2006 which provides comprehensive protection rights for all seafarers. safety at sea is not negotiable and a robust and effective port state control system must be put in place, as stipulated in the provisions of the 2006 convention. in this way, the appropriate standards will be adopted and respected by all ships calling at eu ports. the maritime labour convention will come into force in august this year and i call on all member states which have not yet ratified the convention to do so as soon as possible.
in writing. parliament has long supported measures to establish minimum standards for working and living conditions on board ships. given the global nature of the maritime transport sector, those standards should apply to the entire sector. measures to ensure compliance have a particularly important role to play in achieving these objectives. ships which do not meet the standards are unacceptable both in terms of workers' rights and in the interests of safety, security and environmental protection. it is therefore appropriate that the european union establishes mechanisms to verify that the relevant standards are applied on board all ships calling at european ports, irrespective of the nationality of the seafarers or the flag of the ship. this is also a means of limiting social dumping which deteriorates working conditions and penalises ship owners who offer decent working conditions in line with ilo rules.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of these measures on vehicle registration, as part of the 'technical control' package. this proposal will make it possible in the future to improve the control of vehicles for granting or refusing registration, in order to guarantee safety on our roads and to limit the danger to the maximum. it will also make it possible to monitor pollution from vehicles and to avoid excesses by facilitating vehicle control.
in writing. this report on vehicle registration documents is aimed at administrative simplification by reducing the number of registration documents that motorists must carry at all times. the creation of an electronic database must be implemented as soon as possible. similarly, national databases should be available for road safety and efficiency purposes. reducing bureaucracy and harmonising registration records will facilitate the exchange of information between member states and combat the illicit trade in stolen vehicles.
in writing. this proposal, as part of the 'technical inspection' package, aims to promote and enforce the rules on the technical inspection of motor vehicles in order to enhance road safety and environmental protection. the aim is to improve the application of roadworthiness and roadworthiness systems, particularly where the technical condition of a vehicle represents a direct and immediate danger to road safety, by introducing measures such as temporary suspension or permanent cancellation of the vehicle's registration. in order to be placed on the market, a vehicle must meet all the requirements of type-approval or individual approval and ensure that it meets an optimal level of safety and environmental protection. each member state shall carry out the first registration of any vehicle which has passed the stage of european type-approval on the basis of a certificate of conformity issued by the car manufacturer. this registration officially authorises the vehicle to be used on public roads and the various vehicle requirements take effect. what bothers me, however, is that it is a regulation and not a directive.
in writing. road safety is essential throughout the eu and we need to ensure that technical standards for maintenance and inspection are common across all eu member states. at present, the quantity and quality of controls and inspections vary from one member state to another. this report therefore sets out common minimum standards for the frequency of technical and maintenance checks, to reduce the number of road fatalities, and to meet our objective of at least halving the number of road fatalities by 2020. a regulation is more necessary than a directive, because the latter leaves too much freedom to the member states, leaving them the choice of the means and form to achieve the objective set by the directive. finally, i welcome the inclusion of light commercial vehicles in the scope of roadworthiness testing activities provided for in this report and the establishment of a system of classification of vehicles for risk assessment.
in writing. a clear legal framework for the compliance of commercial vehicles is essential. we therefore propose amendments to make it clear that companies operating commercial vehicles should always be responsible for ensuring that their vehicles are fit for use. companies should ensure that regular checks are carried out on vehicle parts affecting the rolling capacity of the vehicle.
in writing. - i welcome this report because it sets out to harmonise the technical surveillance of motor vehicles by setting minimum technical standards without preventing member states with stricter standards from maintaining their regulations. the minimum frequency for regular road and roadworthiness tests is 4-2-2 years, although countries with more stringent regulations, such as belgium, may maintain their 4-1-1 interval. i also support the decision to dispense with mandatory testing of two-wheelers and to leave the decision on such testing to the member states themselves, because in 11 out of 27 member states there is no provision for mandatory regular road and traffic safety testing of mopeds and motorcycles. it is particularly welcome that the mileage and information on major accidents throughout the life of vehicles will be included in an electronic database which will allow for exchange between member states and that the commission will monitor the introduction of such a system. a similar system already exists in belgium in the form of the 'car-pass'. this will reduce odometer tampering in used car sales, which is currently 5-12%, and is even much higher in cross-border sales. this proposal will not only benefit the eu's internal market, but above all road safety, which can benefit every eu citizen.
in writing. road safety is essential throughout the eu. harmonisation at european level is necessary in the training of inspectors and in the approaches to technical inspection in order to subsequently improve inspections and to reduce the number of accidents due to technical failures.
in writing. the main elements of the new proposal are as follows. as regards the mandatory european-wide technical checks for scooters and motorcycles, the categories of vehicles to be subject to a technical check should be extended to the group of road users most at risk; light trailers (less than 3.5 tonnes) would also be subject to controls. these categories of vehicles are currently excluded from the european system and the decision to subject them to a technical inspection is a matter for the member states. the commission is also considering increasing the frequency of periodic technical inspections for certain categories of vehicles. but i think the directive goes too far, for example, with regard to the weight of the trailers under inspection.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution, which adds new chemical substances to the 33 pollutants already monitored in eu waters. this resolution will further improve the control of water pollution in order to combat it as effectively as possible. the aim is to ensure that all european citizens have access to quality water, a subject on which they are particularly attentive and react.
in writing. water is a public good. clean and pure water is essential not only for the protection of the environment but also for the health of human beings. i therefore welcome this report, which aims to improve water quality and will therefore have a positive impact on the health of citizens. this report is essential because it allows the list of pollutants to be updated and a regular monitoring system to be set up. the report includes provisions to reduce the concentration level of these bioaccumulative and toxic pollutants and to have equal standards for new pollutants. there are also provisions for the chemical nature of water to make the public aware of the quality of their water in their environment.
in writing. 'water is not a commodity like any other but a heritage that must be protected, defended and treated as such', reads the first recital in the preamble to the new directive on priority substances in the field of water policy. a clear message that sounds like a call to protect this resource that is essential for the good of humanity. european citizens are also very concerned about water pollution: according to a march 2012 eurobarometer survey, 80% of them believe that chemical pollution is a threat to the water environment. this call for improving water quality was heard by the european parliament and the irish presidency of the council, which agreed to strengthen existing standards by including in the eu list of 12 new priority substances dangerous to the aquatic environment. these are mainly industrial chemicals, biocides and pesticides. another important point of the agreement is the inclusion of a provision to ensure the consistency of european legislation on chemicals (water, reach, pesticides, biocides, etc.). it is obvious that any lack of regulation is exploited by certain private or public actors to circumvent the polluter-pays principle.
in writing. the proposed directive sets out a list of priority substances in the field of water policy, namely chemical substances presenting a significant risk to or from the aquatic environment at union level. to meet the definition of good chemical status for surface water, bodies of water must meet environmental quality standards (eqs) established for these substances. the most dangerous of these substances are listed as priority hazardous substances (phs) because of their persistence, bioaccumulation or toxicity. measures adopted under the water framework directive aim at a gradual reduction of emissions of priority substances into the aquatic environment or, in the case of psds, at a phase-out or phasing-out. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. this report is part of the modernisation of state aid policy to simplify the supervision of the single market without compromising its effectiveness. i welcome the measures contained in this report, namely the extension of the exemptions from notification to focus on cases with a particularly significant impact on the internal market.
in writing. in a time of economic crisis and reduced spending in the eu, it is important to find new growth potential to exploit while using the wealth of our planet in a sustainable way for our ecology. blue growth in the eu's marine, shipping and tourism sectors could create 7 million jobs by 2020
in writing. man's interest in the sea and oceans could address the major challenges facing the world. new technologies, such as advanced underwater robotics and equipment, are now enabling eu researchers and businesses to turn to the sea to help combat climate change, develop therapies for serious diseases, exploit rare minerals, etc. europe's long and important maritime tradition is being strengthened by new development actions such as offshore wind energy and aquaculture. at the same time, broader concerns are pushing the union to turn to the sea. the need to reduce carbon emissions allows for a focus on short-sea shipping and opens the way for renewable energy on the high seas. the over-exploitation of natural resources on land is driving up their prices on world markets and encouraging the exploration of mineral resources in the sea. i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. cooperatives can play an important role in crisis management and in the integration of jobseekers. there are over 150 000 cooperatives in the eu, employing over 5 million people. cooperatives play a significant role in the face of production crises and business restructuring. they help companies to survive the crisis by implementing restructuring measures that allow them to continue their activities. this report stresses the importance of creating a regulatory framework and of highlighting and recalling the role of cooperatives in this time of crisis.
in writing. cooperatives, as well as social economy enterprises, play a key role in the european economy, especially in times of crisis, by combining profitability with solidarity, creating quality jobs, strengthening social, economic and regional cohesion and generating social capital. cooperatives are becoming increasingly important in the european union. there are about 160 000 cooperative enterprises owned by 123 million members and employing 5 400 000 people, including some 50 000 cooperative enterprises in industry and services employing 1 400 000 people, and cooperatives contribute, on average, 5% of the gdp of each member state. in recent years, several hundred cooperative enterprises in the industrial and service sectors have been created as a result of restructuring of enterprises in crisis or without successor, which has helped to preserve and develop economic activity and jobs at local level. the text voted on today and the amendments attached to it offer a positive outlook on this matter.
in writing. we are facing an increase in energy demand and a shortage of natural resources. sustainable solutions must therefore be found and i believe that the bioeconomy is an adequate solution to meet the challenges of the future. the bioeconomy represents a real opportunity for europe. it is a profitable investment for the future. the bioeconomy holds enormous potential to address our dependence on fossil fuels, to address food security and to get out of the economic crisis we are in in a smart way.
in writing. supporting this sector is an investment in the future and it is up to europe, which has the capacity, to take the lead in achieving this objective. to achieve this, it is necessary to lay the foundations for a clear and stable regulatory environment and to ensure the harmonisation of agricultural, industrial, environmental, fisheries, research and innovation policies, which are relevant to the bioeconomy sectors. i agree with the need to encourage an interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral approach, while ensuring an exchange of knowledge at regional, national and european levels, in order to promote a uniform development of the bioeconomy across the union.

president. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we have two choices tomorrow: we must either accept in whole or in part the amendments tabled by mrs gräßle, myself, mr bové and mr de jong on behalf of two groups, or reject them. what are these amendments? these amendments seek to draw lessons from what happened after mrs gräßle had reached agreement with the council. we have learned, or should learn, from the monitoring committee's activity report and in particular from annex iii. i think that's important. we can't just make legislation out of nothing. we have to face reality. the reality is that there is a great conflict between the director of olaf, the management of olaf and the supervisory committee. and the monitoring committee is important because it monitors the legality of investigations, the proper conduct of proceedings, the protection of the fundamental rights of witnesses and accused persons. fellas, we have two choices tomorrow. either we approve these amendments and then we are in a strong position vis-à-vis the council to say: "let us bring these negotiations back into the conciliation procedure, let us legislate, based on reality, on practice", or we do not. and then we'll act, with all due respect, like a bunch of cowards. we'll act like cowards. we'll just tell the council: "we stand by our conclusions". so, ladies and gentlemen, i ask you to accept the amendments tabled by mrs gräßle, myself, mr bové and mr de jong. that is how we, as a parliament, will have shown our teeth.
