i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr de gucht, for his report. we have reached a good agreement together, which shows the citizens of the european union that european cooperation can bring very concrete benefits. a health threat, such as a pandemic, does indeed have international dimensions. good cooperation between member states and the commission can save lives. what we have achieved with this agreement is not insignificant: the joint procurement of vaccines to control price and ensure supply, a group of experts to assess potential threats and advise on measures, an electronic database to exchange data smoothly and to disseminate a warning and risk assessment when a threat arises. moreover, the proper functioning and implementation of this measure is guaranteed by transparency regarding the independence of experts and - which is also important for federal member states such as mine - by involving the competent länder in the implementation. i thank the rapporteur and the other members and i hope that the report will be supported by the whole house tomorrow.

in writing. i abstained because, despite the progress made in the text, there are also serious disappointments. we are of course pleased with the greater flexibility, so that unspent appropriations can be carried over from one year to the next and from one item of expenditure to the next, in particular to finance the fight against youth unemployment, erasmus or research and development, or the addition of the billion requested for the european fund for aid to the most deprived. this flexibility will also make it possible to maximise the use of appropriations. in the previous budgetary framework, more than 50 billion had been returned to the member states. but some points of the agreement remain too weak: a high-level working group to consider hypothetical own resources from 2020, as if the issue had not already been extensively studied. this is essential if we are to 'no longer depend on the goodwill of certain member states in the annual budgetary discussions'. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the situation of the small and mediumsized enterprises in the community, such as the introduction of a mid-term review clause which is too light and which the next commission can easily abandon, whereas this framework, for the first time in decline, does not meet the needs of europe's recovery.
in writing. the agreement on the next multiannual budget is a thinly veiled one. it may be the maximum that can be expected of the member states at the moment, but the result is still far from the minimum requirements set by parliament in its previous resolutions. the agreement gives the eu a budget for the next seven years that looks to the past, when we need more than ever a policy that looks to the future. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. for that reason, i am not at all happy with this result and cannot support this agreement.
in writing. at international level, the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) develops harmonised requirements to remove technical barriers to trade in motor vehicles between the contracting parties to the revised 1958 agreement and to ensure that such vehicles offer a high level of safety and environmental protection. the aim of this proposal is to simplify and speed up the procedure for the commission to vote on unece regulations on behalf of the union, and thus to reduce the time taken for the adoption of these acts within the unece. this is all the more important as the eu vehicle type-approval system is increasingly based on unece regulations, which replace eu legislation (see regulation (ec) no 661/2009 on general safety). in addition, faster adoption of legislation will allow faster response to regulatory demands from operators.
in writing. at international level, the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) develops harmonised requirements to remove technical barriers to trade in motor vehicles between the contracting parties to the revised 1958 agreement and to ensure that such vehicles offer a high level of safety and environmental protection. the aim of this proposal is to simplify and speed up the procedure for the commission to vote on unece regulations on behalf of the union, and thus to reduce the time taken for the adoption of these acts within the unece. this is all the more important as the eu vehicle type-approval system is increasingly based on unece regulations, which replace eu legislation. in addition, faster adoption of legislation will allow faster response to regulatory demands from operators.
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to help workers who have suffered massive economic redundancies as a result of the increasing globalisation of trade and major changes in industrial structures. the new measures proposed in this report will make resources more accessible and more efficient and thus avoid the social crises that are now affecting workers in the automobile and steel industries.
in writing. created in 2006, this instrument has helped thousands of european workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the increasing globalisation of trade. more recently, he has helped victims of the economic crisis. the proposal for the new european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to ensure the continuity of the work of the fund in the next programming period, in line with the principles defined for the multiannual financial framework (mff) for 2014-2020. the proposals put forward by the european parliament's committee on employment and social affairs will improve the fund by making resources more accessible, especially to workers wishing to return to work; more efficient, by reducing the time taken to process applications; the commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. we also want the egf to help workers prepare for the closure of industries in difficulty. the aim is to avoid social crises such as those which are now affecting workers in the automobile and steel industries.
in writing. after more than six years of negotiations, a new draft olaf regulation is being put to the vote at second reading. after a year of trilogues (informal meetings between the commission, the council and the european parliament) held from october 2011 to june 2012, the ep's committee on budgetary control endorsed the compromise reached in october 2012. the council adopted the proposal for a regulation at first reading in february 2013 and the commission unanimously endorsed a recommendation for the european parliament to approve the proposal on 18 june 2013. the european parliament wants to reach an agreement at second reading as soon as possible. the new regulation increases olaf's powers in the field of investigations, procedural guarantees, protection of fundamental rights and strengthens the agency's capacity to cooperate with third countries and international organisations. the proposal is a good compromise. its implementation will be evaluated in the near future (two years after its entry into force). the legislative procedure must not be held hostage to political differences of opinion on a single case of inquiry.
in writing. this report deals with the fifth revision of the directive on undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities, a revision which aims in particular to protect consumers in the areas of deposit banks and to implement fair sanctioning practices between the different member states. this is important in light of what happened with the madoff scandal where depositors lost large sums of money.
in writing. directive 2009/65/ec of the european parliament and of the council should be amended to take account of market developments and the experience gained to date by market participants and supervisory authorities, in particular to address divergences between national provisions on depositary obligations and liability, remuneration policies and penalties.
in writing. i welcome this report which aims to freeze the auctioning of 900 million allowances in the coming years. due to a growing surplus of emission allowances on the market, the price of co2 emission permits has become so low that companies have little incentive to emit less greenhouse gases. the measures proposed in this report should raise the price of co2 emission allowances to a level that provides sufficient incentives for european industries to pollute less and invest more in low-carbon innovations, which will reduce greenhouse gas emissions and combat climate change.
in writing. the european emissions trading system (eu ets) has created the first major global carbon market, with an eu-wide carbon price as a tool for cost-effectively reducing industrial emissions in the union. although the ets has reduced carbon emissions since its implementation, it still has serious imbalances. the current economic crisis, combined with the increase in credits during the first two cycles of the allowance trading scheme and a large influx of external credits for emission reductions from the clean development mechanism (cdm), has led to a considerable increase in surplus allowances and resulted in the price falling to around €4/tnco2 (compared to the €3/tnco2 envisaged when the energy and climate change package was adopted). the eu ets is one of the pillars of our climate policy. concentrating the system at the end of the period to delay the auctioning of certain allowances is only a short-term measure, which should not be seen as a solution to the current imbalances, but rather as an option to ensure the stability of the system, pending the adoption of the indispensable structural measures.
in writing. − i welcome this report, which recognises that health crises are a priority to be addressed at national level, but recognises that no country is able to tackle cross-border health threats on its own. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the commission shall also ensure that the national authorities are able to provide the necessary information to the competent authorities of the member states in order to ensure that the national authorities are able to fulfil their obligations under this regulation. uniform and coordinated communication strategies and cooperation in crisis situations are necessary. in particular in border regions, this cooperation is essential not only to prevent health threats but also to enable the quickest possible exchange of information across borders and to develop common strategies to combat these health threats, based on the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. i welcome this report on serious cross-border health threats which aims to provide a more effective and coherent eu response to potential threats by drawing lessons from recent previous health crises. the new rules aim to equip the eu with means, networks and structures that complement its existing ones to effectively protect citizens across europe against a wide range of serious crossborder health threats. the text introduces an early warning system, facilitates the common purchase of vaccines and will make it possible to declare a health emergency at european level in the event of a crisis. more conflict of interest control and transparency on the independence of experts will also be put in place.
in writing. the european parliament set an example this afternoon by adopting the pargneaux report on serious crossborder threats to health. the report also has an educational value in these difficult times for the european project: yes, the european union, even with limited powers as in the case of health, brings real added value. by definition, viruses and the species that carry them do not stop at the borders of the european union. it is clear that the european centre for disease prevention in stockholm will have to play a more important role in the years to come. from sars in 2003 to avian influenza in 2009, europe has learned the right lessons, which are based on two pillars: on the one hand, the right communication; on the other hand, the right communication; on the other hand, the right communication. it is not a question of reassuring the citizens, but of telling them the truth. we all remember the lies of chernobyl. on the other hand, there is the need to ensure good coordination between the competent authorities and not to repeat the cacophony about vaccine stocks during the avian influenza crisis. the rest is a matter of intellectual honesty, and i would like to hear more often from health ministers supporting the commission when a pandemic threatens.
in writing. the commission proposal is a response to recent crises such as the 2009 avian influenza pandemic, the 2010 volcanic ash cloud and the 2011 e. coli outbreak. it aims to strengthen measures to protect the population by addressing these serious cross-border health threats more effectively and efficiently. it proposes better planning of preparation and coordination, to be developed in the context of a discussion between the european commission and the member states; extend the early warning and response system for communicable diseases established in 1988 by improving its resources, networks and structures; it extends the scope of risk assessment and coordination measures to all threats to health, whether biological, chemical or environmental in nature; and strengthens the role of the health and safety committee. only a well-prepared, coordinated and effective approach at union level will enable member states to provide the public with the protection and information required in the event of a health pandemic.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this measure which will allow cooperation between several member states in the field of taxation of financial transactions. this is an important subject which is close to my heart and which i have been advocating for a long time. in these difficult times for european citizens, this tax could provide a significant boost as the european union's own resources, which could then be reinjected into projects of common interest and thus relieve the national budgets of the member states.
in writing. − i very much welcome the introduction of a financial transaction tax, as the financial sector had a large part of the responsibility for triggering the financial and economic crisis and should therefore now also contribute to the costs of crisis management. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to impose a tax on the financial sector in the form of a tax on the supply of services, which would be a tax on the supply of services. however, this may lead to double taxation and thus to a fragmentation of the internal market for financial services. a common approach to the financial transaction system should therefore be sought. this should allow for increased cooperation between the 11 member states, but also give the other member states an opportunity to at least participate in the relevant discussions. however, this participation should not result in those who do not participate being able to block enhanced cooperation by others. the taxation of financial transactions is intended to avoid any distortion of competition between financial instruments and to avoid future crises by specifically preventing certain transactions. the creation of this balance is a real challenge which the council can meet if the member states are aware of the added value of european cooperation in financial and economic matters.
in writing. i fully agree with the need for a tax on international financial transactions. i was the initiator of a working group within the adle group on this issue. my aim was to create a tax on international financial transactions to support development aid. member states had committed themselves, under the european consensus for development, to allocating 0.7% of their gdp to development cooperation aid by 2015. it is clear that many states will find it difficult to honour their commitments. on 23 october the commission adopted a proposal to enable 11 european countries, including belgium, germany, italy and spain, to introduce a tax on international financial transactions. the introduction of such a tax is a sign of social justice. the eu must urgently make a gesture towards citizens by showing them that the bulk of the crisis is not limited to rescue measures financed solely by taxes and significant social restrictions.
in writing. the global financial crisis of 2008 highlighted the weaknesses of a long period of deregulation of financial services. moreover, it was commonly accepted that the financial sector was undertaxed compared to other sectors of the economy, since it was exempt from vat, and that it had to bear a fairer share of the cost of the crisis. in this context, the european parliament called for the introduction of a financial transaction tax (ftt) for the first time in 2010. the ftt is a progressive and socially equitable tax and is the preferred instrument for shifting the burden from taxpayers to the financial sector, due to its multiple functions: it can generate substantial new revenues, while significant fiscal consolidation efforts are made by shifting the burden from employment and the productive economy; it can discourage harmful speculative transactions. it is a first step towards reducing the fragmentation of the internal market in direct taxation.
in writing. − a well-designed financial transaction tax is clearly a useful instrument to ensure that the financial sector makes a fair contribution to public finances and to discourage excessive risk-taking and short-term thinking in this sector. but especially in these difficult economic times, it is crucial that the 'design' of this tax is carefully designed. in particular, we must avoid europe shooting itself in the foot by introducing a tax which would hit our economies hard. i am therefore pleased with the corrections made by the european parliament in its opinion. they include the exemption or lowering of certain transactions which are normal and necessary for the 'geolied' functioning of our real economy. i also fully support the choice of maximum harmonization of tax rates. the minimum harmonization proposed by the commission would only lead to further fragmentation of the internal market, and that must be avoided.
in writing. latvia has implemented deep reforms of its economy in the aftermath of the deep recession of 2008-2009. these reforms have borne fruit to such an extent that we can now give a favourable assessment of the country's economic performance in the light of the convergence criteria laid down in the treaty on the functioning of the european union. latvia is also expected to have the highest economic growth this year among eu countries. finally, integration into the euro area will increase the country's still weak popular support for the single currency.
in writing. latvia is in a position to join the euro area. "latvia has achieved a significant degree of convergence with the euro area", the commission said in a statement. the latvian experience shows that a country can overcome its macroeconomic imbalances, even serious ones, and emerge from them strengthened. following the deep recession of 2008-2009, latvia took decisive measures, supported by the eu/imf financial assistance programme, which improved the flexibility and adaptability of its economy. and it paid off. latvia is expected to grow by 3.8% this year and 4.1% in 2014, according to the commission's economic forecast published in early may. the other indicators reflect good economic health and are in line with the budgetary convergence criteria. the country has corrected its public deficit from 8.1% in 2010 to 1.2% in 2012, well below the 3% threshold set in the stability pact. riga is also in the norm for debt, which stood at 40.7% of gdp last year, well below the fateful 60% mark.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text. in order to achieve greater resilience of the banking sector to potential financial crises and to eliminate the risks and costs of banking activities to public finances, it is essential that the reform of the union banking structure establishes a safe, stable and efficient banking system that serves the needs of the real economy, customers and consumers, and supports the provision of credit to the economy, in particular to smes and start-ups. this own-initiative report sets out several key principles, namely reducing complexity, enhancing competition, limiting the porosity between commercial and risk activities, improving corporate governance, introducing a responsible remuneration system, creating an effective bank recovery and resolution regime, strengthening banks' capital and providing liquidity to the real economy, which are essential to achieve a change in banking culture.
in writing. - it is good that the european parliament is today giving its opinion on structural reform of the banking sector, even though there is no concrete proposal yet. in our report on emu we asked the commission to adopt rules where necessary to legally separate certain particularly risky financial activities from the deposit banks within a banking group, as indicated in the liikanen report. the report adopted reflects the caution of our recommendation and urges the commission to base its proposal on a thorough impact assessment, taking into account, among other things, the many measures already taken. the report nevertheless strongly advocates a european framework for structural reforms to avoid the divergent national proposals further fragmenting the internal market. i welcome the nuanced approach of this report. it is clear that the socially crucial core functions of a bank, lending, deposit-taking and payment services, should not be jeopardised by excessively risky investment and trading activities, which benefit from the 'safe image' and the state guarantee. however, we must avoid a fundamentalist approach that deprives banks of the ability to carry out customer-related trading activities that are useful to the real economy. i support this report and look forward to the commission's legislative initiative.
in writing. i welcome the vote on this report on the fight against fraud in 2011. fraud is first and foremost a crime and must be punished. the report, which only covers data provided by the member states, unfortunately shows that there are still sometimes considerable differences in the treatment of these offences between countries. we will therefore work for greater harmonization in this area in the future.
in writing. the 2011 parliamentary report on the protection of the european union's financial interests (pif), by derek vaughan, notes the improvements made during the year, while stressing the need for better collaboration and a standardised approach to fraud reporting by member states. the report also welcomes the work being done on a directive on the fight against fraud affecting the union's financial interests (in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and the committee on budgetary control). the s&d group will table an amendment in plenary calling for an urgent improvement in the working relations between olaf (european anti-fraud office) and its supervisory committee. the european commission has understood the need to contribute to this process, but more active collaboration is still expected from both components of olaf.
in writing. the roadmap is designed to bridge the gap between the existing control framework and the control model developed by the court of auditors. the 'one-stop-shop' model proposed by the court is based on an integrated chain of actors working in a coherent way on the basis of common principles and responsible for their own controls at each stage of the process. implementing such a model requires the commission to take the necessary measures at its level, but also requires the member states to be fully involved in the reform, as they currently manage 80% of eu funds under shared management. the commission decided, on the basis of the evaluation of the discrepancies, to undertake 16 concrete actions, divided into four themes. the first theme concerns simplification and common principles for control. the second theme relates to management declarations and audit assurance. the third theme relates to the maximum increase in the level of control. the fourth and final theme of the action plan addresses the heterogeneous nature of the various union policies and therefore includes actions to close sectoral gaps.

in writing. the purpose of the draft legislative resolution is to provide macro-financial assistance to georgia to cover unmet payment appropriation needs. the 2008 global economic crisis had a negative impact on the georgian economy. the compromise reached on the granting of financial aid will enable the country to deal with the consequences of the crisis, to create jobs, to combat unemployment, especially among young people, with a view to restoring economic growth and stabilizing the country financially. the eu must help emerging democracies such as georgia to develop adequate democratic institutions and thus move closer to european integration.
in writing. the conciliation stage of the co-decision procedure on the additional macro-financial assistance (mfa) to georgia allowed the council and the european parliament to reach the following agreement: application to georgia of the principles of the joint declaration on the mfa; application of the advisory procedure for assistance below the threshold of eur 90 million (as requested by the european parliament); the council also adopted a decision on the application of stricter conditions to the payment of funds where the conditions are not met (as requested by the council). the european parliament delegation has remained united throughout the process, and our group is now meeting in the final agreement. the s&d group welcomes the fact that this regulation will finally allow financial aid to be granted to georgia. the agreement is also satisfactory from an institutional point of view because it respects the powers of the european parliament.
in writing. the purpose of this directive is to approximate the criminal laws of the member states in order to suppress attacks against information systems by laying down minimum rules on the definition of criminal offences and penalties in this area, and to strengthen cooperation between the competent authorities, in particular the police and other specialised law enforcement services in the member states, and the competent specialised agencies of the union, such as eurojust, europol and its european cybercrime centre and the european network and information security agency (enisa).

in writing. the eu is the world's largest exporter of services. services are the backbone of our economy, accounting for 70% of gdp. trade in services is a vital sector of our economies and trade in the 21st century. the world economic crisis has led to a protectionist drift which requires new bilateral or multilateral initiatives to combat all measures which would restrict trade in services. the opening of negotiations on a multilateral agreement on services is a step in the right direction both for the recovery of economic growth and for employment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which rejects the opening and continuation of multilateral negotiations on the agreement on trade in services (acs), given that the wto ministerial conference is not empowered to accept a multilateral agreement negotiated within a subset of wto members in the services sector, for which a plurilateral agreement based on the most favoured nation (mfn) clause is already in place. i would also like to stress that, at the moment, developing and emerging countries are not taking part in the negotiations on the saa and that some of them are strongly opposed to this initiative. it should also be noted that the european union has already concluded or is currently negotiating bilateral trade agreements with some of the partners in the acp negotiations, which agreements include important chapters on services that better reflect the bilateral issues specific to each country.
in writing. the introduction of tariffs on imports of agricultural products by norway can be considered a protectionist measure and a barrier to trade and is contrary to one of the eu's fundamental principles, namely the principle of trade liberalisation. however, norway is a member of the european economic area and must respect the principle of the eu's trade liberalisation commitment. an appeal must be made to the norwegian government to withdraw these measures and thus to respect its commitments to the eu, especially since this measure was taken without prior consultation with the european commission.
in writing. i deplore the recent measures imposed by the norwegian government, which i consider to be protectionist and prohibitory to trade, and in clear breach of the letter and spirit of the bilateral agreement. i would point out that these measures were proposed by the norwegian government without any prior consultation with its counterparts in the european union, as would have been appropriate in the context of the strong bilateral relations that exist between the two sides. finally, i wonder about the economic logic behind these measures, which could have the effect of reducing trade, harming all parties concerned, particularly norwegian consumers, and in the long term also harming norwegian farmers.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution, which allows us to move a little further towards a complete digital market. this market offers very significant economic and employment prospects, thanks to the many smes in the sector. the latter are helping to drive up employment figures in europe. this market is also a boon for the consumer, who will be assured of a wider offer, and therefore a better price, and greater security for his purchases.
in writing. e-commerce in a 28-country europe with more than 500 million consumers is strengthening the single market, boosting cross-border purchases and bringing distant regions closer together. the digital single market has considerable economic potential in the eu which should be fully exploited to deal with the crisis we are going through. its completion will increase the eu's competitiveness, create jobs and bring financial benefits to consumers. the digital market is one of the eu's main assets, creating 2.6 jobs for every job lost in the rest of the economy. in some member states it accounts for 25% of net job creation.
in writing. this resolution is intended to follow up on the european commission's declaration on the completion of the digital single market. it lists specific policy demands for future legislation to be proposed by the commission in this area. these requests cover areas related to the digital single market such as privacy and data protection, information and communication technologies and the economic and legal interests of consumers. the committee also calls for the commission to be given the power to adopt and implement the measures necessary to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the internet.

in writing. i did not support this report on connected tv. it is true that it is essential to adapt the current legislation to the changing media landscape of today. there are currently more than 40 million connected tv sets in europe. by 2016, the majority of european households could be equipped with them. the traditional boundaries between consumers, broadcasting and the internet are becoming blurred. however, a level playing field for all public and private actors must be guaranteed. that is not the case in this report. the measures provided for therein distort competition by proposing, inter alia, that content provided by public broadcasters should be found more easily than content offered by private providers. in addition, content offered by private providers should be subject to quality control.
in writing. unlike my group, i of course supported the resolution on hybrid television which was voted by a very large majority in the european parliament this afternoon. the possibility of surfing the internet via the big screen is already a reality and has become part of many european homes. the european parliament has wanted to examine this development. our parliament is of course only expressing an opinion here, but it was essential to recall the vote we had less than a month ago on the cultural exception, namely that audiovisual services do not come within the framework of the free trade agreement between the european union and the united states, which will be negotiated from 8 july. ensuring a level playing field for all operators, public and private, is essential, but so is the availability and access of media content to all, which is why i supported this very balanced resolution.
in writing. at first sight, it seems that the issues concerning connected tv are purely technical. the issue is the availability, accessibility and accessibility of media content and whether and, if so, with what instruments media offerings can be treated differently in a convergent world. the media have a dual nature: they are products, but they are above all a cultural asset and, as such, they have a particular political importance in society. media pluralism and freedom of opinion, press and information are essential to the functioning of our democratic societies. the media have a function of disseminating knowledge, information, entertainment and surveillance. this is the main reason why media policy in the union and the member states is not subject only to competition law and/or economic rules, but that there are specific regulations which take account of this particular character and the specific importance of the media in society. the convergence of technologies, which has reached its highest point so far with connected tv, will not change this.

i would like to thank the rapporteur and the other members for the good cooperation and the successful conclusion of this dossier. because after five years of crisis, some people may have already forgotten what caused this financial and economic crisis, namely mortgage loans from ordinary consumers. we have seen the dramas in various countries throughout the european union. people who were evicted from their homes or were unable to pay off their mortgages. we have now put an end to that with this legislation. and that is important. i am also very pleased that we have also looked at examples which do work. in belgium, for example, we do have a well-functioning credit market with a high level of consumer protection, with clear transparent regulations and clear information to consumers. that example has also helped to achieve a compromise that can now be applied throughout europe. we have tried in every possible way to give consumers more and better information before they conclude a contract. we have also tried to ensure that the incentives of banks and creditors and consumers are better matched, so that clear, flexible contracts can once again be concluded in the interests of consumers. we have also found a balance between the freedoms enjoyed by banks and creditors on the one hand and the interests of consumers on the other. we have also made it possible for consumers to better understand the risks involved in concluding contracts, both in the case of flexible loans and variable interest rates. we have also tried to cover the risk in countries where contracts are in different currencies in a better way. we have also made sure that each family can have a tailor-made credit in its own way, possibly together with insurance or other products, so that a menu can be created that consumers can again benefit from. in short, we have found a good compromise that can now be applied across europe, that can tackle the causes of this financial crisis and prevent people from being evicted from their homes, from people getting into trouble when taking out mortgages, which is one of the most important decisions a family has to make in a lifetime. i am very glad that we can do this today, it is timely and i hope that we can also apply this in the member states as soon as possible.
for the greens/efa group mr president, we greens are a small team and we must therefore be able to play every position on the pitch. i'm filling in for sven giegold, who's busy with another meeting. i thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. it is true - philippe de backer said it, the commissioner said it too - the systemic importance of mortgage lending in the health of our economy cannot be underestimated. we know that 80 percent of all speculative bubbles are real estate bubbles. so tackling this problem is also a way of protecting our economy against shocks - it's a weak word - she has known. in this respect, the text was more than necessary. while there are reasons for rejoicing in this text, there are also reasons for some concern. i welcome the consumer protection aspect, as do the other speakers. we have clearly made important steps forward towards greater transparency in the offers that are made to consumers, but also in the dangers of these offers, for example loans in foreign currencies or variable rate loans, which may appear very attractive at first sight and which ultimately turn out to be financial holes on arrival. it is also gratifying that the text provides for the possibility for consumers to pay back their loans in advance. i am, however, reserved about the systemic, macroeconomic aspect of the matter. as too often, we have hesitated and therefore have not been able to get a majority to set standards that limit the size of the loan in relation to the value of the property. this is called loan-to-value or loan-to-income, i.e. the strict limitation of the loan amount to the borrower's ability to repay. i think we should have gone much further on this plan. i find that when it comes to debts, there is a bit of a double standard. we are very strong when it comes to public debts, but when it comes to private debts - in writing. i am generally satisfied with the choices made by the commission when it proposes amendments. however, in my view, some of the measures proposed as implementing acts do not require uniform conditions for the application of the regulation, as referred to in article 291 of the tfeu. they are in fact exceptions and therefore amendments within the meaning of article 290 tfeu and should therefore be covered by delegated acts. secondly, i consider that articles 39, 40 and 41 of council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 of 20 november 2009 establishing a community control system for ensuring compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy provide a framework for the monitoring, certification and verification of the power of fishing vessels and that this issue should therefore not be covered by implementing acts. furthermore, i consider that, where recourse to delegated acts is proposed, the delegation of power should be limited in time in order to allow for a regular assessment of its use.
in writing. i propose to extend to registered partnerships the relevant solutions put forward for matrimonial regimes. this is mainly a question of integrating the new provisions on inheritance into other union acts, in particular the regulation on successions and the brussels i regulation. this approach concerns in particular the definition of the scope (exclusion of the compensatory distribution of pension rights between spouses provided for by german law and equivalent schemes in force in other member states), the revision of the provisions relating to the competent courts, the adoption of the provisions of the regulation on succession relating to the adjustment of rights in rem and the recognition, enforceability and enforcement of judgments and the acceptance and enforceability of acts. i also propose extending the revision clause so that we can carefully analyse the practical effects of the various points of divergence which still exist between matrimonial regimes and the property effects of registered partnerships and, on this basis, examine the means of harmonisation.
in writing. the law governing matrimonial property regimes varies considerably from one member state to another, as do the rules on jurisdiction. in practice, it may therefore happen that, in the same case, the competent court of one member state considers the matrimonial property regime differently from that of another member state. however, if the estate is large, this disparity may lead to a court battle in which each party hopes to see the property law applied that it considers most advantageous to it. the advantage then clearly goes to the party with the best advice. in addition, there is a general lack of legal certainty, which is accompanied by financial risk. we need to resolve this legal ambiguity.
in writing. i am particularly concerned to achieve the union's objectives of reducing energy consumption, traffic noise, air pollutants, greenhouse gas emissions, accidents and land use, so as to mitigate the impact of transport on climate change and contribute to improving the health and quality of life of the citizens of the union. at present, many difficulties remain in better aligning research and innovation (r&i) with transport policy. the need to respect certain general principles such as technological neutrality, complementarity, accountability and transparency should be emphasised. i am particularly concerned that duplication of research efforts at national and union level may impede urgently needed progress and i call for an efficient and coherent use of r & i resources. i also believe that small and mediumsized enterprises deserve special attention and that more research opportunities should be given to them.
in writing. − despite being widely debated, the council and parliament differed on several core issues. these included the exclusion of certain 'minor offences' from the scope of the directive; derogations from the rights granted under the directive and the conditions that would apply; the principle of confidentiality between the accused and their lawyer; the legal remedies available to suspects deprived of their rights; and the link between this directive and the european arrest warrant (eaw). the overall agreement reached during negotiations is clearly a compromise. at the insistence of the s&d shadow rapporteur, the principle of confidentiality was successfully included in the directive without derogations. the s&ds also established clear rules on the use of derogations so that they will be proportionate, strictly time-limited, not based solely on the seriousness of the alleged offence and will not prejudice the overall fairness of the proceedings.
in writing. − this directive is significant as the first piece of european legislation in the field of mortgages and the first bill relating to financial reform which focuses on a retail banking product. mortgages are the most important financial commitment most european families make and the mortgage market represents more than the 52% of the eu’s gdp. the agreement reached with the council will contribute to reactivating the economies of many member states, while avoiding the irresponsible mortgage lending and borrowing which was a major cause of the financial crisis. this directive sets out the path and principles for a profound reform of the european mortgages market, to be implemented by member states over the next two years.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the functioning of the internal energy market which calls for the implementation of a genuine european energy community. this market should enable the eu to combat energy price rises effectively and thus protect the purchasing power of european consumers. in addition, this community will promote the security of electricity and gas supply and will create jobs that cannot be relocated. this report represents a real step forward in the integration of the energy market at european level and i welcome it.
in writing. i welcome the main points of the communication and the accompanying action plan, which summarise the progress made so far and the difficulties to be overcome in the future in order to achieve an internal energy market. however, it must be acknowledged that the upward trend in energy prices is likely to continue, as they are currently linked to the price of a barrel of oil for gas and to the volatile prices of fuels for electricity, and that their evolution is also influenced by europe's dependence on oil and gas imports, the effect of intervention measures, the inadequacy of energy efficiency measures and the lack of investment in the maintenance and modernisation of energy networks. it is therefore essential to dissociate the mechanism for fixing gas prices from the oil price indexation by opting for more flexible solutions.
in writing. cohesion policy plays a key role in achieving the eu's target of reducing its overall energy consumption by 20% by 2020. the aim is to improve the eu's energy bill and thus increase its competitiveness, while having a positive impact on the environment and consumer purchasing power. for these reasons, i welcome the adoption of this report, which will double the share of the budget allocated to cohesion policy to achieve the energy efficiency objective and ensure its effective implementation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text. indeed, at the heart of the european strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, the benefits of energy efficiency have long been recognised in europe. however, the union is facing serious difficulties in achieving its target of reducing its overall energy consumption by 20% by 2020, to which energy efficiency policies could and should make a greater contribution. improvements in energy efficiency are crucial for european competitiveness and have only advantages in the fight against climate change. investing in energy efficiency measures has immediate and tangible benefits for households and businesses, whether in terms of cost reductions, job creation and growth, or in encouraging the transition to a low-carbon economy.
in writing. − the commission recently signalled approval for a draft maritime strategy for theadriatic and ionian seas, one of the four pillars which are intended to promote sustainable fishing. the s&d group believes that this should also be a basis for introducing a regional eu strategy for the adriatic-ionian area and that the measures relating to the fisheries and aquaculture sector should take account of the sea basin’s specific features, including its relatively shallow, sandy seabed and its lagoons, islands and coastal areas. the s&d group calls on the commission to adopt the action plan and a regulation dealing with the management of fishing activities in this region at the earliest opportunity. the group’s position was also endorsed by the fisheries committee, with a large majority.

in writing. - the multilingualism of the european institutions is one of the cornerstones of european democracy. it guarantees our citizens the right to communicate with the institutions in their own language and to follow meetings and consult documents in full transparency. it also guarantees that we, as elected representatives, can carry out our representative task properly. because everyone can work in their own official mother tongue, our power relations are equal. but we must also realize that we are working with taxpayers' money and that we must be economical with it. the enlargement of the eu has made multilingualism more expensive. in recent years, parliament and its interpretation services have already made a considerable effort to reduce the cost of interpreting without sacrificing quality. the report we are adopting today is a further step in that effort. i therefore support these proposals for efficiency gains. i believe that we can manage taxpayers' money more efficiently and maintain high quality interpretation. so let us continue to work for a 'smart' multilingualism in the years ahead, combining our democratic aims with appropriate economy.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, draft amending budget no 2 for 2013 presented by the commission in march calls for an increase in budgetary payments for 2013 of eur 11.2 billion, necessary to cover payment claims arising from the implementation of the current budget. this amending budget is the natural consequence of the joint declarations at the highest level on payments agreed last year at the close of the conciliation procedure for the adoption of the 2013 budget. this is therefore an amending budget which is expected to enable the 2013 budget to be fully implemented. i recall that in those statements - which were decisive for the agreement for the european parliament - reference was made to the need to proceed in the first part of the year with this amending budget in order to cover the expenditure on unpaid invoices during 2012 with new, fresh resources capable of enabling the 2013 budget to be implemented correctly. following the negotiations for the new multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 and in the agreement of 27 june, the council agreed to approve a first instalment of the amending budget of eur 7.3 billion, committing itself to cover the remaining payments in the autumn, after the presentation of a new amending budget by the commission. it is clear that following the adoption tomorrow of the first part of amending budget no 2, we are asking the commission to make every effort to present the new amending budget as soon as possible in order to meet the additional payment needs, which we all know, for a proper implementation of the 2013 budget and to avoid significant payment needs from 2013 being passed on to the 2014 budget. in our resolution we strongly stressed the need for the council to approve this new budget as well in order to finance important development, employment, youth and small and mediumsized enterprises policies, thus avoiding any possible problem of payment execution for the financial year 2013. as a result, the political agreement given in parliament in july on the new multiannual financial framework and the approval of the same or the 2014 budget, as anticipated by the chairman of the lamassoure committee, are subject to the condition - which is essential for us - of the approval of the entire 11.2 billion, not only the first tranche which we will vote on tomorrow, but also the second, which we are waiting for in the terms proposed by the commission. i would remind the council that our demands are nothing more than a reflection of the trust and credibility which the institutions must guarantee in keeping with their word and the commitments they have made. i hope therefore that the presidency and the council will take note of the needs of the moment and act accordingly, also in view of the understanding shown by parliament of the consolidation efforts under way in the member states in accepting payment in two instalments. the council should follow up on what was decided by the heads of state and government in june and not act with the sole aim of cutting resources, because that is not the right way out of the crisis. the crisis is overcome by efficient investment and by a commitment not only in words and slogans but in deeds, which in this case are the payment of the invoices relating to the commitments made.

in writing. - today we propose to limit first-generation biofuels. we are correcting a wrong policy. such biofuels were hailed 10 years ago as the solution for renewable energy in transport. meanwhile, many of these fuels have been shown to have little "bio" content. in fact, the overall environmental impact is often negative. i am also pleased that stricter criteria are being put in place to determine which biofuels are sustainable and which are not, and that from 2020 onwards the indirect environmental impact of biofuel cultivation will be taken into account. in flanders, large investments have been made in the past in the production of biofuels, including in the port of ghent. these new proposals from the european parliament do not jeopardize these investments. i'm very concerned about the safety of my investment. it is not the intention that entrepreneurs should be the victims of a european policy based on miscalculations. existing projects can therefore continue, but a signal is given to steer future investment in a more sustainable direction. this creates room for new investment, including in advanced biofuels, derived from waste or algae, and that is good news.
in writing. i welcome the european parliament's consideration of indirect land use change. renewable energy sources, and therefore those receiving public subsidies, will have to take direct and indirect effects into account in calculating the greenhouse gas emission rate. in addition, the european parliament has established a framework to limit the transition from food crops to energy. however, i regret the lack of ambition in the compromise. the race to new agricultural land for energy purposes has disastrous social and ecological consequences. the cap on biofuels at 6% of total energy consumption is a minimalist compromise and the implementation target for 2020 is very late.
in writing. it is clear that first generation biofuels, from the oilseed or ethanol sectors, are replacing food crops. it is equally true to say that such support policies need to be reviewed in europe because they involve many land grabs in developing countries. that is why the signal given this afternoon by the european parliament in favour of the corinne lepage report is the right one, even if the vote was close and the plenary was divided. the text not only supports the european commission's objective of capping the addition of first generation biofuels to traditional fuels, with a ceiling of 6%, but also sets out the way forward and identifies the investments to be made in so-called advanced biofuels, produced from agricultural or forestry residues, non-food materials such as algae, or industrial and municipal waste. europe and its member states must maintain the target of 10% renewable energy in transport by 2020. it's good for innovation, it's good for the climate, and it reduces the volatility of food prices!
- food shouldn't disappear into a gas tank. we voted today to continue to restrict the increasing use of food crops as fuel. the difference of opinion is a small percentage, but the hard truth is that this small difference can mean whether or not to eat for 17 million people a year. biofuels are bad for the wallets of european consumers and can have dramatic consequences for people in developing countries. it is good that in 2020 no more than 6% of transport fuels may come from food-based biofuels. but that does mean that the current share of food in the fuel mix may increase by about 20 percent. it's still too much, but it was the most politically feasible thing to do at the moment. the important thing is that it's now clear that by 2020 we really need to be done converting food into fuel. that's important for investors and energy companies. unfortunately, negotiations with the council of ministers cannot begin immediately, since a right-wing majority of the european parliament voted against these direct negotiations. this also creates a prolonged uncertainty for industry. the epp has a great and negative responsibility in this respect.
in writing. biofuels: eat or drive, you have to choose! the resolution on biofuels will be voted on wednesday. the pressure on agricultural land exerted by the agrofuels industry has the effect of creating a risk of food shortages and increasing food prices. agrofuels started out with good intentions, but isn't hell paved with them? the production of these must therefore be limited and the concept itself must be re-examined. for every % of agrofuels in a fuel, just over 1 million hectares are removed from food production (i.e. practically all the arable land in belgium). the energy mix of biofuels must therefore be changed in favour of those that are the most efficient and neutral in terms of their impact on the soil, agrofuels produced from waste or plant residues, which do not compete with food for humans or animals, and the trail of algae and non-food plants.
in writing. - the critical state of the european eel stock is certainly not to be overlooked. the national council for marine exploration reports a recruitment rate of less than 1% in the north sea and less than 6.5% outside the north sea, the lowest level in history. we cannot continue on this path. it is imperative that action is taken before we see the complete eradication of this species. it is for all member states to ensure the enumeration and definition of the different water catchment areas on their territory which constitute the natural habitat of european eel. member states will also need to implement adequate measures to reduce mortality from various factors, such as commercial or recreational fishing.
in writing. the european eel stock is facing a multitude of problems: overfishing, loss of vital habitats, pollution, pests, changes in ocean currents due to global climate change, etc. the solutions are not easy and several culprits are indicted. to further complicate an already complex issue, there are many unknowns surrounding several major aspects of eel biology and management: uncertainty about the size of the stock, misunderstanding of the conditions that lead to the determination of the sex of the eel, and the question of whether reintroduced eels will actually succeed in reproducing, to name a few. there is also some confusion about the monitoring and control of the exploitation of eels, due to discrepancies in the catch and export figures recorded in the various registers, about the fate of a considerable part of the eels caught, and about a recognised but unquantified international black market in eels. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which sheds a positive light on this matter.

in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes. over time, the network has evolved and extended to all member states that have subsequently joined the union. so far, it is the only harmonised data bank to include microeconomic data, and the approach is the same in all member states. it is an important instrument for the development and evaluation of agricultural policies, since it collects data on income, costs and turnover from a representative sample of agricultural holdings in the union each year. this sample currently comprises some 80 000 farms out of the 6 million or so in the eu-27. this information is important in the context of changes to the cap, as it helps the various research institutes which analyse and simulate agricultural and rural development policy.
in writing. within the european union, it is important to ensure the separation of powers and the role of each institution. the explicit delegation of the power to the commission to amend elements will have an impact on the product names, definitions or descriptions. this is beyond the scope of the delegated acts (the only derogation provided for by article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union). it is necessary to ensure that this delegation will only concern non-essential elements. it is imperative to keep a record of the changes made by the commission. a five-year limitation and a report will therefore fulfil this function.
in writing. the new text proposed seems to be more precise and allows the commission to amend the technical characteristics relating to the descriptions and definitions of the products in the annexes. however, this explicit delegation of the power to amend characteristics that will affect the descriptions, definitions or names of products which are essential elements of the directives goes beyond the scope of the delegated acts. in order to ensure that the delegation of power properly concerns only non-essential elements and to avoid any ambiguity as to the extent to which the commission may adopt delegated acts which will affect essential elements such as the definition of products, your rapporteur proposes to limit the delegation of power and to delete the provisions relating to the power to adopt delegated acts which concern technical elements affecting the descriptions, definitions, sales denominations or names and characteristics of products. the rapporteur also proposes to limit the delegation to a period of five years (renewable) and to control the delegation of powers by asking the commission to report on this before the end of each five-year period.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are now beginning the debate which precedes the important vote you are going to take shortly on the fundamental element of banking union. five years to the day after the collapse of lehman brothers, no one can deny that together - parliament, finance ministers and the commission - we have implemented a series of strong initiatives to respond to this crisis, to learn from it, to meet the expectations of citizens and taxpayers - who have too often been asked to redress the mistakes or the manipulations of certain banks - and to stabilise the banking sector. with the crd iv capital requirements directive, thanks to the work of your rapporteur othmar karas, we have strengthened the soundness of banks. we have also laid the foundations for a uniform regulation applicable to 8 200 european banks. this is our best weapon against the risks of fragmentation of the single market, while preserving the diversity - which i value as much as you do - of the european banking landscape. with the single supervisory mechanism for banks - which was drawn up by sven giegold and marianne thyssen and which will be put to your vote shortly - we are going further by subjecting more than 6 000 banks in the enlarged euro area to high-quality, harmonised, coordinated supervision under the authority of the european central bank. in this respect, i would like to welcome the efforts of president mario draghi to ensure that the new supervisory board is fully operational in the coming months. this new system both preserves and respects the single market. all member states wishing to join the single supervisory mechanism will be able to do so. however, ladies and gentlemen, this is certainly not the time - at least not for me - for complacency or the idea of resting on our laurels: we still have a lot of work to do. the single supervisor is of course essential, but it is only a first step towards the banking union. first, we must continue to clean up and strengthen bank balance sheets so that banks are more robust. moreover, the banking union, which is perhaps our biggest joint project since the creation of the euro, must be based on its second pillar, the single resolution mechanism for banking crises, which is based on precise and predictable rules. let the banks pay for the banks, not the taxpayers, as we have seen for five years! the first priority in this respect is to secure the adoption of the directive on the recovery and resolution of banks. systematic public bailouts should be avoided, by ensuring that the losses of failing banks are borne in the first place by the shareholders and creditors, and not by the taxpayers. negotiations on this text have now been under way for over a year, which is not unusual for a reform of this magnitude. the difficulty for us is to reconcile the need for legal certainty for shareholders and creditors who must know in advance the losses they will incur in the event of bankruptcy and a degree of flexibility allowing, in certain cases, the resolution fund to substitute for the creditors to absorb the losses. despite these difficulties and complexities, the first political trilogue took place in july in a positive atmosphere, and i would like to commend the determination of the co-legislators, and in particular your rapporteur, gunnar hökmark, to reach an agreement quickly. such an agreement is essential for financial stability and the smooth functioning of the resolution mechanism. apart from these rules for resolution, which will feed and consolidate the uniform regulation, the other priority, ladies and gentlemen, is of course the establishment of the single resolution mechanism, which i proposed on behalf of the european commission on 10 july last. a clear and functioning decision-making mechanism, based on a single resolution board, is needed to implement rapid and consistent decisions to resolve the failures of all institutions located in the territories covered by the banking union. furthermore, in addition to the bailout by shareholders and creditors, our proposal includes a single resolution fund, fed by the banking sector banks must pay for banks , which will need to be sufficiently staffed and mobilisable quickly to ensure the success of the resolution of the failures and the viability of the bank's core functions. on these various points, a first ad hoc working group met with the member states on 19 july. i shall be discussing this with the finance ministers in vilnius tomorrow and the day after. i am also pleased that parliament has appointed your colleague elisa ferreira as rapporteur, who has voluntarily committed herself to this text and has set an ambitious timetable with her by the end of november. our initial discussions with you and with the member states have enabled us to provide clarifications and assurances on the legal basis for the future resolution mechanism,
