for the greens/efa group mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that this is first and foremost a question of democracy. in other words, how can political power regain control over a financial sector which has largely been freed from all control and regulation over the past decades? first, of course, because there has been a great deal of deregulation, but also because those who were responsible for enforcing the remaining rules have obviously not done their job. national supervisors have not prevented german, belgian, french, italian and british banks from investing - if one can speak of investments - in the spanish or irish property bubbles. they have not prevented these same banks from speculating in the subprime markets in the united states and thus taking reckless risks. they didn't want to stop megalomaniacal mergers and acquisitions like the one that ultimately cost fortis her life, which went after much bigger than her by trying to buy abn-amro. in this respect, we very much welcome the significant progress that has been made in implementing what this parliament - and the green family in this parliament in any case - has been calling for from the beginning, namely integrated supervision, a single policeman for european banks. the relationship between this european policeman and the banks will probably be a little more tense, a little more difficult than that between the national supervisors and 'their' national banks, which were trying to seek their protection. it's a breakthrough that will have to pass two tests. the first test will be the test of credibility, first initial credibility. in other words, when we examine the quality of the balance sheets of the banks in the coming months, will this be done in a more robust way than the stress tests we have known and which - we have seen this clearly - were completely absurd? this will be the first test of the european central bank's credibility. then there is the question of credibility in the diet. will the european central bank, which has no experience in banking supervision, be able to build the necessary expertise and have a keen enough eye to bring these institutions under real control? the second test is of course that of democratic control, as sven and other speakers have pointed out. there is no question that an institution like the european central bank, which has a fierce tradition of independence and even contempt for democratic institutions, should not be held accountable. in this respect, the successes achieved through the interinstitutional agreement are a good omen. we shall see whether the european central bank will actually comply with them in spirit and in letter.
in writing. i thank mr diamandouros for the important work he has done for over 10 years as european ombudsman. although an increasing number of citizens accept the intervention of the european ombudsman, progress remains to be made, particularly with regard to the transparency of the european administration. europe suffers from a democratic deficit. it is essential to communicate in a clear and transparent way, giving the european citizen all the information he wants. i invite the european institutions to cooperate more closely with the ombudsman in order to deepen the dialogue with citizens, civil society and all stakeholders, which will help to improve the image of the european union.
in writing. in 2012, the ombudsman opened 465 inquiries (an increase of 18% compared to 2011). it closed 390 (an increase of 23% compared to 2011). more generally, as in 2011, the ombudsman helped over 22 000 people by dealing with their complaints (2 442 cases), answering their requests for information (1 211) or providing advice through an interactive guide on his website (19 281). the number of complaints under the ombudsman's mandate was 740 and the number of complaints outside his mandate (1 720) is the lowest in the decade. in more than 75% of cases, the ombudsman assisted the complainant by opening an inquiry (18.3% of cases), referring the case to a competent body or advising the complainant on the procedure to be followed (57.1%). in total, 67% of complaints received in 2012 were lodged via the internet. the ombudsman's work is important.
in writing. we have reached an agreement, although this is a highly sensitive subject. free movement is a fundamental principle which gives the union the opportunity to open up to countries that so wish. this agreement will ensure greater coherence in the european union's external policy. full visa reciprocity must become an objective for the union to achieve in its relations with third countries. however, the inclusion of a suspension clause in such an agreement is still relevant to prevent abuse.
in writing. i welcome the creation of the european system of banking supervision, which is a major step forward in eu banking supervision. the system will supervise around 150 of the largest eu banks by transferring banking supervision power from the national to the european level, thus allowing for more effective prudential supervision. in addition, it should be noted that the european parliament will have a wider right of access to the data managed by the ecb and will be able to hear the chairman of the supervisory committee on a regular basis, whose responsibility may be called into question in the event of any errors being made. finally, it is a good sign that this system, which is mandatory for euro-zone members, will remain open to other eu members with attractive conditions for participation.
in writing. the establishment of a single supervisory mechanism is a first step towards the creation of a european banking union, based on a genuine single regulatory body (the 'uniform regulation') for financial services, and also including harmonisation of the different national deposit guarantee schemes and a common european framework for the resolution of bank failures. the banking union should be based on appropriate accountability and power-sharing mechanisms between political institutions, at national and union level, and bodies with supervisory responsibilities at both union and national level. at all stages of the implementation of the banking union, due consideration should be given to any mutual effects on the euro area which would affect member states which are not members of the euro area. to that end, appropriate preventive measures should be adopted to avoid any possible disturbance of the internal market. in particular, the ecb should be required to ensure that it carries out its supervisory tasks in a non-discriminatory manner that is conducive to the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. − the main factors in the financial and economic crisis were the excessive budget deficits of some countries and the irresponsible speculation of the banking sector. now the council and the ecb have finally accepted parliament's proposal and opened the way to a 'european banking supervision'. this decision was overdue because the national authorities had little control over the internationally structured banks. the european parliament has gained greater insight into this activity through the negotiating skills of marianne thyssen, which thus gives greater transparency to this supervision. the european parliament is thus drawing conclusions from a crisis which, unfortunately, is not yet over.
in writing. five years after the bankruptcy of the financial giant lehmann brothers, the european parliament voted to establish the first pillar of a european banking union by putting over six thousand financial institutions under supervision. this first step seemed unrealistic even three years ago. however, europeans had no choice but to come together to prevent such an economic disaster from happening again and taxpayers from paying for the irresponsibility of the financial sector. we have taken a first step and there is still much to be done to achieve a real banking union. although this is an excellent agreement, i have some reservations about the situation of non-euro area countries, which i believe needs to be clarified. i also welcome the agreement reached between the european parliament and the european central bank on strengthening the democratic control of the european parliament over the new powers conferred on the ecb.
in writing. − with this proposal on access to genetic resources and the fair sharing of their benefits, the eu aims to implement the nagoya protocol and to meet its international obligations. however, the commission proposal is a very minimalist interpretation of the use of genetic resources and does not impose any general rules on access to genetic resources. this was left to the individual member states. the green rapporteurs made substantial changes to the commission proposal. it provides for progressive compliance so that the large amount of genetic material already collected in european databases will gradually be brought into line with the new legislation at each new application. this is to avoid 'biopiracy' and requires the countries of origin to give prior informed consent and to be properly compensated. the commission has also introduced controls and set up a biodiversity fund with the proceeds of genetic material whose country of origin cannot be determined. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal. it is not possible for modern industry to appropriate the rights to traditional knowledge and genetic resources of developing countries and make a lot of money from it without the consent of the original owners and a fair compensation.
in writing. the loss of biodiversity is increasing and accelerating. it is estimated that one in four mammals, one in eight birds, and more than one in three amphibians are threatened with extinction worldwide (iucn, 2012). nearly 60% of ecosystems have been degraded in the last 50 years (fao, 2010). beyond an ethical and moral responsibility, the economic and social impact of such a decline is immense: 7% of global gdp lost annually by 2050. in order to contribute to the conservation of biodiversity, its peoples and associated knowledge, it is now necessary that the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge be shared in a fair and equitable manner. this sharing should contribute to the preservation of biological and cultural diversity in situ and ensure its sustainable use by local populations.
in writing. in the implementation of a strong european energy policy, the european union must attach importance not only to transnational energy projects but also to micro-projects enabling european citizens to become energy self-sufficient. this micro-aspects will directly contribute to making the european union energy independent. moreover, this market is a source of growth and innovation, allowing a proliferation of smes specialising in this field. this micro-energy policy must be part of an ambitious european policy which should take the form of a european energy community.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. 'microgeneration' refers to the whole range of small and medium-sized electricity generators, including solar, wind, hydro, biomass and waste. more broadly, it also includes combined heat and power (chp) or cogeneration equipment, which feed the heat produced during the generation of electricity either directly into households or into local heat and power grids. proponents of microgeneration (also known as distributed or decentralised power generation) argue that a decentralised energy market is a prerequisite for achieving europe's renewable energy and energy efficiency targets, but they lament the significant barriers to their ability to compete with the largest electricity producers.
in writing. i am pleased that the eu is committed to making equal pay for men and women a reality. unfortunately, the finding is irrefutable. there has been too little progress in this area and there are even regressions in some eu member states. it is therefore necessary to recall that we cannot accept that there are differences between the pay of men and women. the principle of equal work, equal pay must now become a reality for european citizens and this motion for a resolution strongly encourages it.
in writing. while equal pay for men and women has been enshrined in the treaties since 1957, it is clear that in 2013 the situation is still not effective. in fact, at present, about 16% of women are still victims of this discrimination. for these women workers, this is a clear violation of their fundamental rights. it is unacceptable that for the same job, under the pretext that you are a woman, you are paid less. it is important to ensure that all eu member states will work to solve this problem. this is all the more so as 70% of european citizens consider this pay gap to be serious.
in writing. i voted for this resolution! equality between men and women is one of the founding principles of the european union. it dates back to 1975, when the principle of equal pay for work of equal value was incorporated into the treaty of rome. belgium also has important legislation against discrimination and for the promotion of equality between women and men in the field of employment. despite this equality in law, women continue to bear the brunt of de facto inequalities and indirect discrimination which restrict their opportunities in terms of access to employment, career and working conditions. often they have to combine their work with the daily tasks of housekeeping and child rearing. as a result, the various forms of time-credit or parental leave which allow for a better reconciliation of work and family life, as well as the use of parttime work, are almost exclusively women's affairs.
in writing. in the digital age, we are faced with an increasing number of threats and attacks that are becoming increasingly sophisticated. the internet provides criminals with the opportunity to engage in almost any illegal activity anywhere in the world. more importantly, cybercrime is no longer the work of an isolated criminal but is now the work of traditional criminal organizations. we must find concrete answers to ensure the security not only of our freedoms and private rights but also of our entire economic system. the legislation must apply to both real and virtual life. the european union and its member states must invest in a clear and effective response to the problems of cybercrime, the transnational threat par excellence.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. the cybersecurity strategy 'an open, safe and secure cyberspace' sets out the eu's overall vision on how best to prevent and respond to disruptions and attacks in cyberspace. it aims to promote the european values of freedom and democracy and to ensure that the digital economy can develop safely. specific measures are provided to increase the resilience of information systems, to reduce cybercrime and to strengthen the union's international cybersecurity and cyberdefence policy.

in writing. i voted in favour of the text. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. i think that, by virtue of an internal agreement, the committee on employment and social affairs should be involved in the procedure, so that it can contribute and contribute constructively to the evaluation of requests to mobilise the fund.

in writing. i am pleased that the european parliament is reiterating that the fight against corruption is an absolute necessity, especially in these times of crisis when a lot of effort is required from european citizens. corruption is not only a moral offense but is all the more shocking when it concerns the financing of the union's external aid to third countries. these fraudulent actions call into question some of the basic principles of democracy, namely equality and justice. it is essential to combat this kind of practice from another age. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. as the shadow rapporteur for this report for my political group, i would like to thank the rapporteur for the good report which covers the subject very broadly. the red thread in the report, which we as a group would also like to see, is the vicious circle of corruption which has a negative impact on human rights, and the fact that human rights which are not adequately defended give rise to more corruption. europe must provide support in this area, especially in its foreign policy. but the question is, of course, how do we break this vicious circle? the present report provides a useful starting point and i believe it sets the right tone. the eu must coordinate its internal and external policies: start with yourself, then teach others. it is the only way to speak with sufficient weight.
in writing. corruption accounts for 5% of global gdp. which is unacceptable. the european union must react swiftly and firmly. while it is important to severely punish any person or organisation responsible, it is also important to work upstream in terms of prevention. corruption often fuels crime, fuels conflict, and keeps governments fragile, thus holding back development. we must therefore work ahead of corruption and terrorism on development programmes, education, health to ensure a minimum standard of living for the citizen. to paraphrase algerian president abdelaziz bouteflika, i would say that 'the fight against poverty is perhaps the first indispensable element in the fight against terrorism, because it is a factor destroying human virtues and the basis of human solidarity'.
in writing. the european union can only become a credible and influential actor in the fight against corruption if it responds appropriately to the problems of organised crime, corruption and money laundering within its own borders. i hope that the commission's identification of areas vulnerable to corruption in the member states will help to strengthen efforts to combat this phenomenon, facilitate the exchange of best practices, identify european trends and stimulate peer learning and greater respect for european and international commitments. the strengthening of the regulation and transparency of business and trust registers in all member states of the european union is a prerequisite for the fight against corruption, both in the union and in third countries. european regulation should impose an obligation to register all legal structures and beneficial ownership data, and that these data should be published online, marked electronically and in a searchable format so as to be available free of charge.
in writing. following the success of the pilot project, the two arms of the budgetary authority decided, at the initiative of parliament, in the 2012 budget that the project could, by moving to the next phase, be converted into a preparatory action covering three years, from 2012 to 2014. the aim of the action is to set up an 'interinstitutional system for forecasting long-term developments in the major policy files of the european union'. the aim is to produce joint analyses of the likely outcomes of the major dossiers for the use of policy makers. in addition, to achieve this objective, it would now be appropriate to study in detail the design of specific mechanisms for promoting closer cooperation between the research services of the different institutions and the different union bodies responsible for analysing policy developments in the medium and long term.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which proposes two amendments to the 'brussels i' regulation on jurisdiction in the field of labour law: firstly, a court reserved for disputes concerning collective action, in accordance with the rome ii regulation, namely that of the place where the collective action is to be or has been brought; secondly, when the worker takes legal action against the employer, the withdrawal clause, when there is no habitual place of work, should be reworded to refer to the establishment which gives or has given him his daily instructions rather than to the place where he was employed. the aim of these amendments is to protect workers collectively and individually, who are generally the weakest party in an employment relationship, and to ensure legal consistency and avoid undermining national legal traditions in the field of labour law by ensuring, as far as possible, that jurisdiction and the applicable law overlap.
in writing. we have reached agreement on the responsibility of each member state to fulfil its obligations as flag state effectively and to verify that vessels comply with directive 2009/13/ec. the adaptation of european standards and rules to those expressed in the maritime labour convention, and their uniformity for all member states, are important issues in order to avoid social dumping and unfair competition between member states. in order to ensure this standardisation and to ensure that member states comply with their obligations, it is crucial to have a control and certification system in place.
in writing. i believe that the provisions of the maritime labour convention 2006 on flag state control should be incorporated into eu law in a more detailed and specific way. the main advantage of incorporating the maritime labour convention into eu law is that it will be much more strictly enforced within the union, for example through eu infringement procedures, which will ensure even greater compliance with the provisions. the european union provisions on flag state control should take much better account of the specific and explicit requirements of the maritime labour convention in order to avoid differences of interpretation between member states, which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping.
in writing. i welcome the fact that parliament has recalled that tobacco is the most serious preventable cause of death in europe, with almost 700 000 deaths a year. in order to ensure that this industry does not lure our children into this deadly addiction, i voted in favour of all the amendments which could make tobacco consumption in europe less attractive.
in writing. tobacco kills about 700 000 people in europe each year. it's the number one cause of premature death. in the face of these alarming figures, we had to act. that is why we voted for a directive that focuses mainly on protecting european citizens by ensuring good information (65% of the surface area of tobacco packaging must be reserved exclusively for warning messages and illustrations), by tackling excessive marketing techniques put in place by producers, and by prohibiting any additions of attractive flavours or sophisticated packaging. as far as electronic cigarettes are concerned, i believe they should be regulated in the same way as any other tobacco product. the introduction of electronic cigarettes will give tobacco consumers access to a so-called substitute product that is much less harmful to health.
in writing. 700 000 european citizens die each year as a result of tobacco use. i have spoken in favour of banning fine and flavoured cigarettes, of warning labels covering 65 to 75% of the surface of the packaging and of a border on electronic cigarettes. a blow to the cigarette industry, which is already preparing for the parade. these multinationals are not defeated and are starting to buy the companies that make electronic cigarettes to sell the disease and its cure. ethics are in the wind! there's drinking and smoking in this vote. we could have gone further, but this is a step forward because the tobacco industry is no longer invulnerable in europe, so the symbol is strong. we wanted e-cigarettes to be sold in pharmacies because they are not sufficiently controlled and there are still too many mysteries about their side effects and their components. we must regulate this product so that it never harms the consumer or becomes a gateway to cigarettes for teenagers.
in writing. i welcome the fisheries agreement signed between the european union and the islamic republic of mauritania. it is a balanced agreement. in exchange for financial compensation, the european fleet is granted access to a limited amount of marine resources, equivalent to the surplus of the mauritanian seabed. despite this limitation, it is still the most important fisheries agreement in terms of volumes and marine diversity for the european union. on the mauritanian side, the fisheries sector is essential to the economy. it accounts for 50% of exports, 29% of gdp and 36% of local employment. this agreement allows europeans to actively contribute to the development of the country while preserving the sustainability of mauritania's seabed. i also welcome the effort to incorporate human rights clauses into this agreement.
in writing. mauritania is a country of nomadic culture which, although rich in one of the world's richest fishing grounds, has no fishing tradition. the absence of a national fishing fleet may be explained by nomadism, lack of economic resources and lack of political will. the mauritanian government has therefore chosen to let foreign fleets, including union vessels, exploit its resources. from an economic point of view, fisheries account for 50% of export earnings and 29% of gross national product (gnp). export and processing enterprises are mainly mixed capital enterprises. in its relations with mauritania, the union must endeavour to help the country develop economically and socially, in order to create the right conditions for encouraging foreign investment. the union should also provide sectoral assistance to enable mauritania to manage fishing activities in its waters in a sustainable manner in the long term and to combat illegal fishing by applying the principles of good governance and by respecting international standards on the law of the sea.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on gendercide, a worldwide phenomenon which involves killing a person on the basis of his or her sex, usually female. it is necessary to combat this kind of practice, which is based essentially on prejudice, in order to move as quickly as possible towards a society in which gender equality is the law. it was important for the european parliament to recall that nearly 100 million women are victims of this every year around the world to raise awareness and reaffirm our principles and values.
in writing. i voted for this text, of course, gendercide is a neutral term to describe the deliberate killing of a person of one sex simply because of that sex. recent estimates of the male-to-female ratio show an increase in the number of "absent" women in the world population, with the number approaching 200 million. this is an extreme increase since 1990, when the number of women "absent" was 100 million. girls continue to be the target of relentless discrimination in terms of sex-determination, abortion, abandonment and infanticide of girls simply because they are female. sex selection may occur before pregnancy is established, during pregnancy through prenatal sex detection and selective abortion, or after childbirth through infanticide or child neglect. sex selection is sometimes used by families for balancing purposes but it is most often practiced to favor boys, given that in some cultural traditions, girls are considered a burden.
in writing. - i voted today in favour of the report on the impact of budgetary constraints on regional and local authorities. this report highlights the implications of the current european austerity policy for subnational authorities and stresses the importance of public investment, particularly in relation to the european structural funds. in the wake of the financial crisis, budgetary rules in europe have been tightened considerably. the balance shifted to a policy of strict austerity, with far too little attention paid to sustainable investment and socioeconomic recovery. this also affects regional and local authorities. their expenditure is included in the national debt calculation, including expenditure as co-financing of eu structural funds. this is in the context of very significant investment by local authorities, largely in public goods such as streets, squares and cultural heritage. i am therefore very pleased that this report has been adopted by a large majority. the european parliament calls on the member states and the commission to exclude public expenditure by member states for the co-financing of the structural and investment funds from the public expenditure required to meet the strict european budgetary standards. it is precisely this kind of investment, in sustainable development, employment, innovation and support for smes, that europe needs most.
in writing. the current crisis places significant constraints on the public finances of the member states. moreover, in the context of the current financial and economic crisis, local (regional and local) authorities are increasingly faced with the problem of solving a conundrum concerning their capacity to guarantee productive investment. on the one hand, they are experiencing a sharp decline in their incomes as central governments reduce transfers and ask regional and local governments to contribute to austerity measures, while on the other hand, they are increasingly required to provide, because of the crisis, highly demanded social services which are putting additional pressure on their public finances. in this particular context, i believe that concrete proposals should be made to ensure the greatest possible flexibility in the national co-financing of the union's development expenditure in a context of strict implementation of the csf. to achieve this, the extent of the impacts of the current crisis on the ability of local authorities to achieve the growth and employment targets set out in the europe 2020 strategy needs to be analysed. it is necessary to suggest ways of improving the financial capacity of these entities for productive investment.
in writing. the european union, as the world's largest provider of official development assistance, must intervene by putting in place a comprehensive eu fisheries strategy for the pacific region, consistent with fisheries, trade and development policies. this overall strategy aims to improve the union's relations with the pacific and to help the states of the region to make progress in their fisheries management. in order to foster this development, it is crucial to put in place more transparent policies to combat illegal and unregulated fishing and to improve the judicial security of european vessels.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. the aim of this report is to recommend the development of a long-term fisheries strategy in the western and central pacific that takes into account the need to coordinate european policies in order to enhance potential synergies, to achieve a multiplier effect that maximises the beneficial impacts for both pacific states and those of the european union, and to increase the visibility of the eu in the region. the pacific offers a very high fishery value, being the main producer of highly migratory species, including tuna, as it represents 80% of the world catch, and in particular the western and central pacific, which totals 49% of the catch in 2010 and 52% in 2011.
in writing. in order to make fishing sustainable, in the face of the increasing population and urbanisation along the mediterranean coast, it is imperative to take account of resources and therefore avoid depleting marine stocks and resources. it is also crucial to establish better cooperation between member states and third countries in order to resolve conflicts concerning maritime zones and the delimitation of the boundaries of these zones peacefully. eu waters are equipped with all the conditions necessary for economic, social and environmental benefits to be derived from fishing. it is therefore essential to bring elements of coastal control, surveillance and safety to this policy in order to develop this sector in a sustainable way that is beneficial for fishermen, citizens and the marine environment.
in writing. the mediterranean sea supports 30% of the world's maritime traffic, and about 75% of the mediterranean sea's fish stocks are overexploited i am very concerned about the increased competition for dwindling marine stocks and resources, which is creating regional tensions and can lead to disputes between coastal states over maritime zones. in this context, i call for intensified efforts at regional, national and european level to improve the regulation of access to resources. i also urge all coastal states to intensify their efforts to phase out overfishing in the mediterranean and black seas, as the decline in fish stocks will increase the potential for conflict in these areas.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission proposal on flight time limitations is not a typical legislative proposal. it is a safety regulation. it was approved by the competent regulatory committee of member states’ representatives on 12 june 2013 by an overwhelming majority. the european aviation safety agency has been authorised to develop safer rules in aviation. my personal view is that safety regulation details should not be for political debate. they must be for authorised mandated experts. when we negotiate with our partners abroad – and we have quite difficult aviation negotiations, especially with countries in the east and south – we always strongly request from our partners with whom we negotiate that political interference in safety matters must be excluded. to facilitate constructive decision-making, i would like to give some clarifications concerning this regulation. first, as regards recital 5 of the proposed commission regulation, member states may apply and enforce on their operators provisions of a more protective nature than those in the regulation, providing that the member state’s request has been processed in accordance with the required procedures and that an equivalent level of safety is met or exceeded. second, the eu rules on home standby have been developed in such a way that no crew member will be on flight duty after more than 18 hours awake. the commission will request easa to adopt its certification specifications in such a way that no crew member will be on flight duty after more than 18 hours awake. third, on the question of night flights: the commission will request easa to prescribe in its certification specifications that airlines will be required to apply appropriate fatigue-risk management for flight duty periods longer than 10 hours at night. and fourth, stakeholders, including aircrew representatives, will remain involved in all future developments on the flight time limitation file, and so will parliament. parliament can decide to veto or not to veto the proposed regulation and keep the existing national rules for several years. flight time is not an unregulated business. the commission will respect your decision.

i would like to say, mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, that i am aware of the complexity of the subject and the emotions it arouses in many of those involved. but i also think we should take a moment to look at the facts and then draw conclusions. i should like to say a few words about the procedure, which has been the subject of a great deal of criticism. but that is - as has already been said - the result of legislation which this parliament itself adopted some years ago. it has been said quite deliberately: "look, we should actually leave these kinds of technical issues in the hands of experts". easa has been working on it for three years. the commission has been taking over the work and consulting stakeholders for the past six months. at a certain point, a decision was taken, which was approved by the experts of the member states. and now we are presented with this file and we have only the choice to resist or not to resist. we've heard a lot about that file over the past few weeks. i certainly sympathized with some of the criticisms, but the fact is that we can only use a veto. in substance i think - and my colleague brian simpson has stressed this - that if you objectively compare what is now on the table with the national security rules, in 95 per cent of cases this is an equivalent and usually even a better proposal than the current national rules. the problem in the discussion is, of course, that it is not the current national regulations that are being compared, but the current practice. and fortunately, in many situations, it is more favourable than the minimum safety rules, because more favourable flight and rest arrangements have been obtained in the form of collective agreements or other arrangements. and i am glad to hear you, commissioner, repeat tonight that existing schemes or, of course, social legislation going further, but also safety legislation going further, will always remain possible if the right procedures are followed and if the result, of course, is greater safety. i will not go into the many examples we could give, but the non-regression clause is an important point. the fact that it is clarified that 18 hours is really the limit is important, that fatigue risk management will be organised on night flights. but above all, that this is only a foundation on which we can build in the coming years, with the involvement of all stakeholders and all parties concerned. i thank you and my personal advice is therefore not to support the motion for a rejection but to support the commission's proposal, in view of the clarifications that have been given in the meantime. thank you, sir.
mr president, the procedure under which we are to vote on the proposal before us no longer gives our assembly any possibility of correcting or strengthening it, and certainly not by last-minute proposals. in these circumstances, the question is whether or not these proposals would represent an improvement on the very incomplete and imperfect european and national rules currently in force. it's just pointless. this is not a false debate. because in the face of this proposal, which is for us to take or leave, the questions we have to ask ourselves today are the following: are we really convinced that after 11 o'clock in the night, or even 12:30 if departing in the afternoon, a pilot will still be alert and alert enough to handle any delicate manoeuvre? do we really believe that this will still be the case after a period of home detention which may result in flying hours after waking periods of 8 to 10 hours? are we really prepared to accept the idea that a few hours of rest on board a commercial airliner will enable the pilot to be fully operational after 16 hours in the air? various scientific studies, including one commissioned by easa in the preparation of this regulation, tell us exactly the opposite. so, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is the safety of the crew and passengers, but also of any victims on the ground in any air disaster, that is at stake. we have no right to make mistakes unless we are convinced that all scientists are wrong, unless we believe that no unforeseen situation or adverse weather condition will ever require the intervention of pilots but also of flight attendants and stewards in full possession of their resources, both physically and mentally. we have no choice but to reject this proposal, the commission's proposal, and to ask you, commissioner, perhaps even with the last-minute elements, to get back to work without delay, taking this time fully into account the most recent recommendations from the scientific world. here's your warrant! answer is "blue cardboard". listen, mrs meissner, i think that we have no room for error on security and i think that today the commission is making last-minute proposals. let it do so very seriously, after a vote in which we rejected the regulation, and let it come back with comprehensive proposals which are likely to satisfy us, not us environmentalists, but the safety of everyone! that is what we ask, nothing else, we are obliged to take it or leave it. we do not accept, and we ask the commission to come back with serious proposals which take account of scientific studies and which this time allow real harmonized progress for all without each of us having looked at our own national situations. aviation is by definition a transnational and european issue.

in writing. on 12 september, the european parliament introduced the first pillar of a european banking union, placing over six thousand financial institutions under the supervision of the european central bank. the guarantee of the safety and solvency of financial institutions could not be at the expense of democracy. an interinstitutional agreement was therefore signed between the european parliament and the ecb. it gives meps a power of scrutiny over the ecb's new powers and ensures real transparency between the two european institutions.
in writing. the interinstitutional agreement under consideration is the result of complex negotiations which were completed at the beginning of september 2013 and which led to the positive vote of the european parliament on the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) regulation. the negotiations on the agreement between the european parliament and the ecb took place from may to september 2013 and were completed before the european parliament voted on the proposed regulation on 12 september 2013. the agreement provides for strong parliamentary scrutiny of the exercise of the ecb's supervisory powers, through regular exchanges of views with the relevant parliamentary committee, closed-door meetings with the committee's bureau and, finally, through improved access to information, including the non-reserved part of the minutes of the supervisory board. it also ensures full cooperation between the two institutions in the context of investigations. finally, the draft interinstitutional agreement provides for parliamentary scrutiny of the selection procedure for the appointment of the chairman of the supervisory board.
in writing. - the adoption this afternoon of the interinstitutional agreement on the democratic accountability of the european central bank for its tasks in the framework of the common banking supervisory mechanism has finally completed the first pillar of the banking union. i would first of all call on the council to complete the legislative process on the ssm regulation very quickly now so that the entry into force of the european banking supervisory mechanism is not further delayed. in the iia negotiations, the parliamentary negotiating team has always adhered strictly to the principle that any shift of oversight from the national to the european level should be accompanied by a corresponding increase in transparency and accountability at that european level. i think we got this one, too. the agreement not only provides parliament with strong parliamentary control over the ecb's supervisory tasks, but also gives it far-reaching powers in the appointment and, if necessary, the removal of the chair and vice-chair of the supervisory board of the ssm. but as always, the proof of the pudding is in the eating. the next step is to give the iia a foothold and to make the theoretical rights it contains concrete and politically enforceable.

in writing. - shale gas is highly controversial because of the potential impact on the environment of the so-called fracking technique. so it's good that we're linking this to strict environmental conditions. the same applies to the possible release of methane gas. the extraction of shale gas has potential advantages: it can reduce the price of our energy and our dependence on foreign suppliers. but a clear european framework is essential to minimise the risks to people and the environment. therefore, shale gas drilling should be preceded by a mandatory environmental impact assessment. this obligation should apply not only to commercial exploitation but also to the research phase when the controversial fracking technique is used.
in writing. as the sustainable environment is one of the main challenges for the future of our planet, i welcome mr zanoni's report on the assessment of the environmental impacts of private or public projects. it has many positive aspects, clear rules on conflict resolution and real environmental impact assessments. however, this extremely complex issue still needs to be discussed in depth on key aspects such as impact assessment in the exploratory phase.
in writing. the energy challenge is one of the most important challenges facing europe. by 2020, the european union will put in place an ambitious framework for an innovative energy policy, with citizens at its heart. they must be assured of the highest standards of quality, safety, and security for the production and use of energy. i supported this afternoon a european parliament resolution to measure the impact of projects on the environment. the text provides for the imposition of an environmental impact assessment at the exploration stage of shale gas projects, when assessing whether or not to extract it. shale gas could help reduce europe's energy dependence, increase energy security and create new jobs. so this is a real opportunity, but also a real challenge. there is no doubt that within the next decade, human engineering will develop techniques for exploitation that are environmentally and health-friendly. today, a compromise has been found to satisfy both economic interests and environmental concerns. but as a proof of the controversy, the rapporteur was given a mandate to negotiate by 21 votes to none. it therefore remains to reach a final agreement with the commission and the council.
in writing. - we voted today on this report, which is part of the revision of the 1985 european legislation on environmental impact assessment. it is a major improvement, as it endorses a number of important issues and conditions that an erc must meet and it offers the public and ngos the opportunity to be involved during the different phases of the project. in addition, the rules and conditions for appointing objective, independent experts to draw up the met are also tightened and it is mandatory to carry out an met when extracting shale gas. this kind of european legislation is exactly an example of where europe can add value. the amended directive should help to ensure that the environment of citizens and future generations is better protected, that resources are used more efficiently and that more sustainable growth is stimulated in europe. that is why i voted for this report with the european greens, even though the final result on shale gas is not 100% what we would have liked. the mer is not mandatory during test drilling but only during the final stage of production. the directive is very valuable in protecting weak but crucial values such as our environment and public health.
in writing. on the basis of the precautionary principle and as requested by parliament in its resolution of 21 november 2012 on the environmental impact of shale gas and oil shale extraction, it is necessary to include so-called unconventional hydrocarbons in annex i to the directive, so that exploration projects are systematically subject to an eia. the production thresholds provided for in the current directive do not, in fact, take account of the daily production levels of these gases and oils, so that projects in these areas are not subject to an eia. achieving a truly 'green' economy will also require ensuring the sustainability of projects to be carried out in our territory, but also designing and implementing them in line with their impact on resource efficiency, climate change and biodiversity loss, particularly in relation to major infrastructure projects. the adoption of the eia directive would make it possible to move from theory to practice and to equip the union with a fundamental operational instrument if the global challenges of the 21st century are to be met.
in writing. the proposed new directive on pleasure craft and motor yachts significantly modernises existing eu rules on safety and environmental requirements for boats for private use, i.e. recreational, sport and training activities, including when rented, with or without crew. in this directive the term 'boat' refers to vessels between 2.5 and 24 metres in length and covers 'pleasure boats' (motor boats and sailing yachts, including those equipped with inboard or outboard engines) and 'motorised watercraft', essentially sea scooters, which are now clearly subject to the relevant rules. an important distinction is that the directive applies to pleasure boats and motorised watercraft, whether designed for sea or inland waterway use, but does not apply to vessels designed and used for the commercial carriage of passengers. the directive covers all vessels, from the small outboard motor inflatable boat used for fishing on a lake to the large motor yachts that can be seen on the italian riviera for example.

in writing. − the whole debate on cooperation in border services and surveillance should also be an opportunity to underline the need for member states to show increased solidarity beyond cooperation. the refugee tragedies of recent months cannot be answered by resolutions of ministers or parliaments, but by political decisions. we cannot demand that 'europe should do something' as is so often the case in such cases, but those who do demand this do not want to give up the competence to do it in a european way. europe must be able to shape proactive development aid and migration policies.
in writing. it was with great emotion that i learned of the deaths of hundreds of people who drowned in the mediterranean in early october while trying to reach european shores. this tragedy joins the long list of previous tragedies and forces europeans to plan ambitious responses. this report is part of that approach. the aim is to set up a european surveillance system, called eurosur. this common framework for the exchange of information will allow for better coordination and cooperation between the different national territorial surveillance agencies and the european schengen agency - frontex. this is a necessity that will make it possible to secure more efficiently and quickly the migratory flows that are taking increasingly dangerous routes. together, we can end these tragedies.
in writing. the tragedy of last week in lampedusa reminds us that the tragedy of illegal immigration is played out daily in the mediterranean basin. 300 people died when their luxury yacht caught fire while the 545 people on board were illegally reaching italy. the european union has understood the urgency and is taking measures to prevent these macabre crossings. the european parliament adopted a new system for monitoring the union's borders this afternoon. this instrument, called eurosur, which i supported, makes it possible to better prevent, detect and combat illegal immigration and crossborder crime. the battle is complex because these migrants are fleeing the poverty and war in their home countries, so it is there that their living conditions must be improved so that they do not opt for a journey that will prove fatal. europe will not turn a blind eye and is taking measures to save the lives of migrants. the principle of non-refoulement prohibits the return of a person to an area where his life and liberties could be threatened. cooperation between member states is paramount and 18 countries have already committed to applying these new rules from december 2013.
in writing. free movement is a founding principle of the european union, and the ability to move within the union without having to undergo internal border controls is one of its greatest achievements. many people use this freedom, and public opinion consistently ranks freedom of travel among the main benefits of the union. for our economy too, free movement is essential to the success of the single market. schengen cannot be cancelled it should, on the contrary, be reinforced by better management of the union's external borders, guaranteeing full mutual trust between member states. that is why your rapporteur supports the commission's proposal in general. sharing information and improving cooperation between member states and between agencies are essential steps towards a better division of tasks within the management of the union's external borders. they are also essential to help member states comply with international maritime law and save the lives of migrants.
in writing. − cadmium is a highly toxic substance whose contact with the consumer should be avoided as far as possible. as several alternative cadmium-free compositions for batteries for cordless power tools (e.g. cordless drills, etc.) are currently available, the exception in directive 2006/66/ec was no longer justified. i am also glad that parliament has taken the initiative of amending this directive to eliminate the exception for the use of mercury in cell batteries. these are so small that they often end up unnoticed in the ordinary household waste instead of being properly recycled. the quantity of mercury released can be greatly reduced by the abolition of the exception.
we don't inherit the earth from our parents, we borrow it from our children. it is our duty as citizens to take action to ensure the future of our planet. europe must succeed in what jeremy rifkin calls the 'third industrial revolution' to ensure more sustainable development. the timeframe for 2015 and 2016 (2015 for mercury button batteries and 2016 for nickel-cadmium batteries) is short but we must respond quickly and effectively.
in writing. i suggest to extend the derogation for nicd batteries for a period of one year, until 31 december 2016. given the possibility of 100% recycling of collected nicd batteries, i would point out that the risk is minor and can be managed. the extension of the derogation for a period of one year would allow for a reasonable compromise in that it would protect the interests of consumers and businesses along the value chain while ensuring the protection of the environment and human health and also allowing more time for technological evolution, sharing of good practices, learning and innovation in this area.
in writing. this oral question is a follow-up to the own-initiative report on extraditions to the cia over the past year. it also called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's external borders are not blocked. it reiterated the political recommendations and urged their full and immediate implementation. the question had been adopted by a large majority in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. we are now in the process of drawing up a text which will serve as the basis for a joint motion by the main groups, and we hope to achieve a positive result.
in writing. as the borders are opening up, crossborder crime is on the rise. borders are no longer a protection for crime, criminals operate through networks. it is important to establish collaboration and cooperation between member states in order to develop instruments to combat these crimes. the exchange of information and data is essential in the implementation of anti-crime policy. it is important, however, that such exchanges of information take place in a manner that respects privacy and data protection. i therefore welcome parliament's resolution on crossborder crime.
in writing. i note that for a growing number of member states the prüm decision has become a common tool in crossborder police cooperation and criminal investigations. i regret that the implementation of this decision has been very late in several member states. this instrument should not be improved in collaboration with the commission until it has been fully implemented. i call on the member states concerned to implement the prüm decision fully and correctly so that it can be used to the maximum extent. the prüm decision was adopted under the old third pillar and its implementation is flawed by the lack of proper democratic monitoring and control by the european parliament. the commission must make proposals without delay to incorporate into the legal framework of the lisbon treaty the crossborder police cooperation instruments adopted in the context of the former third pillar, such as the prüm decision and the swedish initiative.
in writing. i welcome the motion for a resolution on caste discrimination. concern for human rights has always been at the heart of our parliamentary work. 260 million people are affected by this discrimination today. this is contrary to international law, human rights and is a structural factor in poverty. in addition, it generates discrimination in employment, education and access to land. it is therefore crucial and necessary to insist at european level that this kind of discrimination be recognised as a distinct form of discrimination rooted in a social and religious context and that the 'untouchables' be recognised as a group in their own right so that they can be taken into account in development programmes.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution. caste discrimination which is characterised, in both the public and private spheres, by practices of so-called untouchability towards communities stigmatised within a caste system is recognised as one of the most problematic human rights issues in the world today, as well as the main source of poverty and inequality in the countries where it occurs. the phenomenon thus represents a major obstacle to the achievement of the objectives of sustainable development and poverty eradication. an estimated 260 million people worldwide are subject to this form of discrimination, which not only violates the most fundamental principles of international human rights law but also leads to systematic violations of human rights in society, the perpetrators of which enjoy, in the vast majority of cases, total impunity.
in writing. the european parliament's information offices in the member states play an indispensable role as decentralised access points to all parliament services for civil society and official bodies. in particular, during information missions, the peti committee coordinates with the information offices to disseminate information to citizens and to organise press conferences. conversely, citizens sometimes submit petitions through their national information office of the european parliament, which forwards them to the peti committee. the right of citizens and residents of the european union to petition the european parliament, individually or on behalf of associations, is a long-established right conferred by the treaty on the functioning of the european union (article 227) and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union (article 44). the right to petition is an essential democratic tool because it allows meps to confront reality on issues that affect citizens and also shows that the european parliament is ready to intervene directly to promote and protect citizens' rights.

in writing. i believe that the proposed regulation is based on a reasonable analysis, namely that it seeks to level the conditions governing imports of wines from the western balkans into the union market. i would like to stress that the allocation of a specific tariff quota for wine from kosovo would not lead to a general increase in the overall tariff quota allowed for imports of wines from the western balkans, but would simply affect its distribution, by correcting the allegedly unfavourable position of kosovo wine exporters. furthermore, it appears that the level of wine quotas granted to kosovo is set on the basis of the past marketing of that product and that, as this is the method traditionally used to determine the levels of the quotas, kosovo wine does not appear to be allocated disproportionately compared to the individual tariff quotas allocated for wine to the other western balkan countries under the stabilisation and association agreements or the interim agreements. the rapporteur therefore does not wish to amend the commission's proposal at this stage of the procedure.

in writing. the commission proposal focuses heavily on product quality. however, experts and many international organizations, such as the council of europe, the oecd and the european society of human genetics, continue to assert that in many cases the context in which the product is applied is even more important than the quality of the product. in the case of dna testing in particular, it is very important to respect the principle of informed consent. the european parliament has also repeatedly called for this. a legal opinion concludes that it is possible and appropriate to introduce a corresponding text in the proposal. the rapporteur therefore proposes amendments on this point. there is a consensus that the european union should not seek to restrict access to dna testing for patients but that appropriate genetic counselling should be systematically offered to inform patients of the consequences of testing before it is carried out. in order to respect the principle of subsidiarity, member states should be allowed to regulate the modalities and go beyond what is required by the regulation.
in writing. - today we voted on two regulations to improve the safety of medical devices. unfortunately, parliament has not opted for a model with one single control at european level for the most risky devices. the elaborate conformity procedure for risky devices that we have approved today is too complex and contains too many exceptions. if we really want to provide european patients with certainty and to avoid a situation like the pip scandal ever happening again, we must eventually move towards a central european assessment procedure before risky devices can be placed on the market. a second point i would like to stress is the importance of good rules on the use of genetic tests (dna tests). these tests are often of questionable quality, the interpretation of the result is not obvious, and the consequences can be far-reaching for the individual and his family. a genetic test with a predictive function is not something to be taken lightly. i am therefore glad that parliament has voted by a very large majority to make the necessary medical expert assistance before and after the test compulsory.
in writing. the commission proposes to close the gaps in the current legislation governing medical devices: strengthening the supervision of notified bodies to ensure conformity assessment; strengthening the control of producers by means of unannounced inspections; improving public information by extending the medical device database; the introduction of a unique identifier to improve traceability and reminders in case of security concerns. the rapporteur welcomes the commission's efforts, but regrets the excessive focus on the speed of marketing medical devices, to the detriment of patient safety. the aim of the dagmar roth-behrendt report is to strengthen the aspects of legislation affecting patient safety. to this end, it proposes the establishment of a centralised pre-marketing authorisation procedure for high-risk devices involving an eu-wide public health agency (pha), the strengthening of the qualification criteria for notified body staff and the presence of in-house expertise, and the strengthening of the criteria for multi-purpose devices based on eu-wide withdrawal standards.
in writing. the dismantling of ships is a particularly complex and highly controversial problem because of its serious environmental and social consequences and its economic importance. with a view to the ratification of the hong kong convention in 2020, i welcome the report by mr carl schlyter which outlines the outlines of stricter legislation including a system of sanctions for the recycling and dismantling of ships. the establishment of an eu list for installations inside and outside the eu helps to reduce adverse effects on the environment and human health and to reduce disparities between operators. these different standards will make it possible to stop social and environmental dumping and provide an international framework between flag states and recycling states.
in writing. ships are brought as close as possible to a high-tide beach and are usually moored on mud flats near the beach in the intertidal zone. they are cut vertically into very large pieces with no other help than torches and gravity, the pieces then falling onto the muddy folds. workers are exposed to high acute and chronic hazards, proper containment of hazardous materials is not possible and hazardous materials that are collected separately are not adequately treated. what we're seeing is capitalism in its most crude form. most of the remaining ship owners seek to maximise their profits by selling their vessels to sites that meet low or no standards of worker and environmental protection and are therefore able to offer the highest price. we are facing a clear market failure, due to 'extreme cost outsourcing' at the expense of workers' health and the environment.

in writing. an average of 5% of hospitalized patients are affected by care-associated infections (cas). in other words, 37 000 people a year die directly from such infections in the european union. this is one of the commission's major concerns. in 2008, the commissioner for health, ms vassiliou, already stated that "patient safety is the cornerstone of good quality healthcare". since then, we've gone from 12 percent in 2008 to 5 percent of patients with ibs. it's still way too much. i strongly hope that patient safety, including the prevention and control of ibs, will be placed high on the political agenda of the european union.
in writing. access to safe healthcare is the cornerstone of a quality healthcare system. it is also a recognised fundamental right, to which the european union, its institutions and european citizens are committed. therefore, patients are entitled to expect that every effort will be made to ensure their safety. i voted in favour of this text. indeed, the health sector is a high-risk area in that adverse events related to care (not the medical problem being treated) can result in serious injury, complications or suffering, or even death, to patients in care. while some adverse events are related to the inherent risks of necessary interventions or medicines, others are caused by medical errors and by deficiencies or failures in the care chain that could be avoided.
in writing. financial losses due to deceptive trading practices in the eu are little known. analysis of some national statistical data shows that these practices cover a market worth several billion euros a year. it is essential to tackle this problem head on, especially in these times of economic crisis, because the first victims are not only the most vulnerable consumers, but also smes and micro-enterprises (essential drivers of growth in europe). these practices create serious market dysfunctions by preventing firms from making informed and therefore effective choices. an effective solution is to severely punish any person or organisation that engages in such practices, but also to adopt a preventive approach and a coherent jurisdiction across the eu.
in writing. the european parliament voted today by an overwhelming majority in favour of the de jong report on misleading marketing practices. examples of misleading marketing practices are numerous: fraudulent payment forms, abuse of internet domain names, false offers to protect the trade mark in other countries when this can only be done through official bodies, etc. this report aims to identify the most common forms of misleading advertising practices in commercial communications, both business-to-business and business-to-consumer. the report goes beyond the european commission's proposal in that it proposes additional measures for prevention and information, enforcement and prosecution, and also calls for more international cooperation. the system of information exchange between member states will be improved and a blacklist of misleading advertising practices and the companies that commit them will be drawn up. it is also proposed to increase the capacity and expertise of the legal and investigative services involved and to impose effective penalties and compensation. i therefore voted in favour of the report in its entirety, because i believe it is important that these criminal practices should be tackled and punished at european level, but even better at international level.
in writing. deceptive business practices can take many forms, the most common being directory publishers, where a dishonest company sends forms to businesses asking them to complete or update their company name and contact details, ostensibly for free. but the signatories later discover that they have, in fact, unknowingly entered into a contract obliging them, usually for a minimum period of three years, to be listed in a professional directory for an annual fee of about 1,000 euros. other deceptive commercial practices include misleading payment forms, in the form of invoices for services that are allegedly ordered by the trader when they are not, offers to extend domain names on the internet by means of which a dishonest trader provides false information and exerts psychological pressure to conclude a contract at a price far higher than that at which registration could have been obtained from official providers, and offers to extend the protection of trademarks registered in other countries, whereas such protection can only be granted by official bodies.
i think the message of this report is well and truly stated: that organized crime today is a professional multibillion dollar business that causes a great deal of human and economic damage. it is therefore clear that we urgently need to accelerate police and judicial cooperation. i think that no one in the european union today can remain deaf to the concrete recommendations contained in this report, in this resolution by mr iacolino. we must in particular work - as stated in paragraph 125 of the final recommendations - to establish a european public prosecutor's office with the necessary resources to tackle this transnational crime; we must also ensure that social and fiscal controls are effective, that inspections are carried out and that there is cooperation between national services. it is well known - and has been said here - that organised crime is able to exploit the benefits of the internal market in an efficient way and we as the european union must find a strong response to this. the commissioner, therefore, must put this issue at the top of the agenda of one of the next summits of heads of state or government, in order to ensure political support at the highest level. finally, commissioner, criminal practices are also increasingly taking place on the internet, especially in the area of the gambling industry in the context of sports matches, with the intention of laundering criminal money. that is a major threat to the integrity of our most important sport in europe. we have already raised this matter in the context of mr fox's report. so here too, strong cross-border cooperation and rapid exchange of information are essential.

in writing. the fight against drugs and drug trafficking is a global challenge. the fragile states are the eldorados not only of drugs but also of the trafficking of immigrants and small arms, before they reach europe. drugs ruin the lives of individuals and have a high cost to societies. the monitoring of trade in precursors, which are legal substances used to synthesise drugs, is therefore a crucial issue in this fight. we need to act quickly and in the long term because the sector is changing rapidly. that is why i welcome mr proust's report, which strengthens the control of these substances by creating a new category to be monitored, namely medicines. this surveillance must not, however, impede the trade in medicines which is vital for developing populations. we will achieve our objectives more effectively and more quickly if we strengthen our cooperation and control mechanisms in this area and if the european database of precursors is updated regularly.
in writing. i voted for this text. i think that medicines should be included in the definition of scheduled substances and that a new category of substances should be created which makes it possible to further clarify the controls to be applied to scheduled substances. the annexes will be adapted by means of delegated acts, which will allow the council to veto, if necessary, a decision by the commission to add a new medicinal product. furthermore, the definition of scheduled substances clearly states that the precursor must be readily extractable from the mixture in order to be considered a scheduled substance. the rapporteur believes that this should very much limit the number of medicines that could one day be considered as classified substances and thus limit the impact of the regulation on the trade in medicines. at present, only medicinal products containing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine fulfil this requirement.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. it should be noted that drug precursors are chemical substances which are used in a wide range of industrial processes (plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, perfumes, detergents, etc.) but which can also be diverted for the illicit production of narcotics. they are rarely manufactured by traffickers for illicit use, as this requires a large infrastructure. as a result, they are often the target of attempts to divert them from legitimate business channels, either by theft or by buying them back. this is why the regulatory framework in place provides for a system of authorisations and registrations of drug precursors. the scheme controls trade in these substances within the european union by imposing specific obligations on the companies concerned (anti-theft, customer verification, detection of suspicious transactions) and on the public authorities (administrative procedures and visits to companies). the level of control varies according to the product category.

in writing. following the proposal of the committee on the marine environment, the neves report put forward the mapping of the marine environment for the benefit of fisheries. it is an essential instrument if the fisheries sector is to be made sustainable, profitable and environmentally friendly. it is therefore important to use and exploit data collection through exchange. many private and public organisations have fisheries data which should be included in these maps through compatibility and interoperability mechanisms. it is therefore crucial to foster coordination and cooperation within the union. however, care will have to be taken to ensure that the confidentiality of this data and the protection of commercial interests are guaranteed.
in writing. in august 2012, the european commission presented a green paper entitled 'marines knowledge 2020: from seabed mapping to ocean forecasting', which is integrated into the promotion, development and expansion of the 'blue economy'. it serves the objectives of the 'europe 2020 strategy' as regards the sea, by combining knowledge and technological innovation, sustainable use of resources, competitiveness and job creation for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. to this end, it is planned to develop a continuous multi-resolution digital map of the european seabed by 2020. this is an ambitious, large-scale and multidisciplinary project, which aims to disseminate information to a multitude of stakeholders interested in ocean data at the level of public bodies, industry, education and research, and civil society. this digital map covers a variety of areas, including information on topography, geology, habitats and ecosystems of the seabed and human activities. it provides data on the physical, chemical and biological parameters of the water column above and makes oceanographic forecasts.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. the european union currently has no horizontal legislative framework to enforce its rights under the wto agreement and other international trade agreements. in a world where retaliation is on the rise, the proposed instrument is legitimately designed to strengthen the enforcement of the union's trade rights, to establish its credibility and, ultimately, to convince our trading partners to respect the rules of the game laid down in trade agreements. the proposal under consideration is also part of a strategy to widen the union's markets and aligns the decision-making process with the lisbon treaty.
in writing. the commission justifies its proposal for cfp reform by claiming that the european fishing fleet is overcapacity. this is very questionable: the commission does not define this notion of overcapacity, so that any overcapacity is difficult to establish. i therefore note that the commission proposes to catch the same amount of fish with fewer vessels, thus endangering many fishing enterprises, particularly small-scale or coastal ones, and thus many jobs. we are opposed to this approach and want strict control of fishing activity to lead to sustainable management from an environmental and social point of view. i would remind you of the obligation on member states to respect the capacity ceilings for their fleets laid down in the basic regulation. to strengthen this obligation, i propose that member states indicate in their emff operational programme the measures they are implementing to comply with these ceilings under this regulation.
