in writing. the european parliament voted today on the framework for the un climate summit in warsaw in november. these negotiations should set the stage for a binding climate agreement in 2015 in which all countries agree on their co2 emissions. the european parliament today set out the minimum european commitment for next month's negotiations. i voted for this resolution. parliament called on the commission and the council to set the eu as an example. the report sets out the link between europe's leadership role in international negotiations and europe's own climate policy. the negotiations are now entering a crucial phase with a view to reaching an agreement in 2015. europe must take a leading role in the negotiations and commit itself to ambitious objectives. the report stresses the urgent need for co2 reduction to limit global warming to 2 degrees and the importance of energy saving and renewable energy. the greens in the european parliament would have liked to have included suggestions for ambitious targets for 2030 and 2050 in the resolution, but unfortunately these proposals have not succeeded. nevertheless, this resolution proposes a good framework for the next round of climate negotiations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution. there is an urgent need to raise ambition by 2020 to reach the 2°c target. i would particularly stress the need to achieve results as a matter of urgency in closing the considerable gap between scientific findings and the parties' current commitments. the important role of other measures, including energy efficiency and the phasing-out of hfcs, in helping to bridge this colossal gap should be highlighted.
in writing. the transnational challenges of corruption, money laundering and organised crime are morally and economically unacceptable. these challenges hamper the proper functioning of the market and harm competition. strict, targeted and effective rules are needed to avoid impunity for such criminals. however, this legislative framework should not be established at national level. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are uniform throughout the community. the union must therefore be equipped with genuinely powerful tools to fight this problem more effectively. in addition, the european union must also strengthen its role as coordinator. the report calls on the european commission to take stock of the situation in europe and make recommendations based on a best practice approach, addressed both to the member states and to the european institutions. the efforts made by the latter to ensure greater transparency in their administration, in particular by guaranteeing a right of access to documents, can be seen as exemplary. the fight against tax havens and the opacity of financial institutions must also be intensified.
in writing. we have sought to suggest a homogeneous and coherent legislative framework to economically target organised crime and strengthen judicial and police cooperation at european and international level. the report aims, among other things, to promote a more flexible and therefore less corruptible public administration, a more responsible politics, a faster and more credible criminal justice system, healthier businesses, a more transparent banking system and business world, and timely anti-money laundering measures to prevent crime from remaining a lucrative activity that harms the legal economy, entrepreneurs and honest citizens. new technologies and the possibilities offered by the lisbon treaty, in particular with regard to the establishment and launch of a european public prosecutor's office, should help to achieve the objectives of this report.
in writing. the european neighbourhood policy establishes a special relationship between the european union and its neighbouring countries. we must see the neighbouring countries as genuine equal partners. the economic, trade, security and political successes of the enp benefit europeans and third countries alike. enhanced cooperation between neighbouring states and the european union makes it possible to respond concretely and more effectively to a set of transnational challenges that we all face. however, i prefer the need to establish, within this regional concept, individualized relations in order to ensure an optimal benefit for each party.
in writing. i believe that the european parliament should be fully involved in the implementation of the new enp and in the adjustment of european financial assistance, including through delegated acts, and should be kept regularly informed of the progress of reforms in partner countries and the resulting adjustments. i regret that he is not systematically consulted on the preparation of action plans and is not informed of the content of the discussions. i consider its resolutions to be an integral part of the framework of the european neighbourhood policy and i ask that meps be granted observer status so that they can take part in the meetings of the subcommittees on political affairs and human rights.
in writing. the european semester is a new six-month cycle in the coordination of economic policies in the eu. as part of the economic governance package (the 'six-pack'), it aims to strengthen the coordination of economic policies in countries by providing ex ante advice. we must continue to intensify our efforts to support growth but without neglecting fiscal consolidation. without growth, europe loses all credibility, without solidarity, it loses all legitimacy. as jacques delors said, we must combine 'competition which stimulates, cooperation which strengthens and solidarity which unites'.
in writing. i would like to remind you that the full potential of the services sector in terms of economy and employment remains untapped. i call for the full and proper implementation of the european services directive, while preserving the public service obligations that guarantee universal access to quality and affordable services for all. it is also worth recalling that some member states must invest in quality social services. wage and social standards must be respected. member states must remove barriers in the retail trade sector and excessive restrictions on professional services and regulated professions.
in writing. - the successive tragic events in lampedusa and elsewhere in the mediterranean are forcing us to accelerate. we can and must now tackle the criminal networks of human trafficking much more efficiently by launching eurosur quickly; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the refugees are not sent to the camps. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. with the reformed european asylum policy we now have a common framework for a correct and solidary approach. but many member states have yet to put the agreements into practice. and of course, we must also continue to tackle the causes of this migration. people are desperate and risking their lives to get out of their country, which is plagued by dictatorship, poverty and war. let us put this at the top of the agenda of the next eu summit and launch a new initiative that is a sign of hope, especially for the horn of africa.
in writing. tragedy is piling up. the number of casualties is growing. the european parliament, which could not remain indifferent, adopted a resolution in this connection, calling in particular on the member states to respect their commitments and to show greater solidarity and responsibility in dealing with the problem of managing the migration flow in the mediterranean. europeans now have a set of effective tools to respond appropriately to this type of human tragedy. but we need to use them better. i also call on the member states to introduce more stringent and systematic sanctions against smugglers who have developed a genuinely lucrative illegal trade out of the misery of the weakest. however, the management of the migration flow in the mediterranean is not done alone. it requires a global and international approach to forging privileged relations between the european union and its neighbouring countries. in this context, we must increase our humanitarian, social, political and economic assistance to these countries of origin. the cigem in mali is a good example of this. finally, i would like to stress the need to guarantee systematically and unconditionally the respect of the fundamental rights of survivors.
in writing. the human tragedy of lampedusa is still in the minds of all. 300 people died on a makeshift boat trying to reach europe by clandestine means. a week later, another shipwreck claimed 34 lives. according to the international organization for migration, 20,000 migrants have lost their lives in the mediterranean in the last 10 years. it is urgent that the whole of europe adopt a coordinated strategy on immigration. two weeks ago, mps voted to strengthen border security and tackle illegal immigration. the european parliament adopted a resolution on migration flows in the mediterranean this afternoon. the text, which i supported, also rightly calls for tackling the causes of migration. it is obviously by addressing the root causes of the problem that we can dissuade migrants from attempting a dangerous adventure that is too often deadly. we must neutralize the heads of networks and work on coordination with the countries of origin. the member states will then meet tomorrow for a european summit on migration. let us hope that words are followed by strong actions. cooperation and solidarity will be the keywords for a more humane and effective immigration policy.
in writing. the tragic events of the past few weeks must be a turning point and an incentive for europe to avoid a repetition of them by adopting a coordinated approach based on solidarity and responsibility. these initiatives should take the following forms: 1) full compliance with international obligations for rescue at sea, accompanied by a rapid agreement on the introduction of new interception rules for operations coordinated by frontex; 2) promotion of existing and new migration channels; 3) effective access to asylum procedures; (4) deepening cooperation with third countries, under precise and predefined conditions relating to their fundamental rights obligations; (5) strengthening solidarity within the union, to reduce the pressure on the member states most affected. in these circumstances, it is high time that everyone shoulders his or her responsibilities in order to put in place a comprehensive eu migration policy and avoid a repetition of the tragedies of the past few weeks.
in writing. - the tragic events near lampedusa cannot leave anyone indifferent. the victims are first and foremost victims of human traffickers who should not be rewarded by an even more lax immigration policy, on the contrary. the only way to combat this trafficking in human beings is a particularly strict policy of return to the countries or continents of origin, where only the exceptions confirm the rule. it goes without saying that europe should help those regions with food and shelter. the fact that we are not able to absorb all the misery of the whole world in our own countries - always at the expense of the least well-off - is equally true. it's too easy to play santa claus with taxpayers' money and other people's living conditions.
in writing. i voted in favour of temporarily suspending the eu-us terrorist financing tracking programme (tftp) agreement following the release of documents showing that the us national surveillance agency had illegally accessed the swift database, thereby breaching the personal data, in this case the banking data, of our fellow citizens. this is a serious breach of the agreement and undermines the eu's credibility. this breach of the agreement undermines respect for fundamental rights, in particular the obligations relating to the protection of privacy and the protection of personal data. we have a responsibility to the european citizen.
in writing. as long as the united states considers that all europeans are terrorists and that it is legitimate to invade their privacy by violating individual freedoms, we demand the suspension of the agreements. spying and mutual trust are not possible. there is a legitimate fear that european companies are being monitored for economic intelligence purposes, that opinion leaders or ordinary citizens are being tracked by methods supposedly reserved for hunting down terrorists: this is intolerable! trust is broken the moment the person you're supposed to be with spies on you. the legitimacy of the pnr agreements and the climate of the negotiations for the trade agreement between europe and the united states are certainly deteriorating. parliament's position in favour of a suspension of the agreements is constructive. we want to restore trust so that we can resume transatlantic cooperation. respect for the rights of european citizens and european businesses is a precondition for any agreement.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague mr la via on the council position on draft amending budget no 6/2013: revision of the estimates for gni and vat and gni bases, budgetisation of uk corrections and revision of gni cuts for the netherlands and sweden other revenue from the fine imposed on microsoft creation of the union trust funds. the council should be reminded of the artificial under-budgeting of previous years which it defended, and it should be pointed out in this connection that the total annual budgets for the period 2007-2013 are eur 60 billion below the overall agreed ceiling for payments under the cfp for the period 2007-2013 and that a cumulated surplus of eur 12 billion for the period 2007-2013 has been de facto transferred to the member states by reducing their cumulated gni contributions by that amount!
in writing. environmental concern is a matter of responsibility for the union, for third countries, but also and above all for the individual. i voted for the text. the environment must put the european citizen at the heart of the problem. educating, informing and training them, strengthening their involvement in everyday life, promoting their citizenship and their access to justice in environmental matters - these are the objectives that the new european programme must also pursue. so what better opportunity than 2013 - the european year of citizenship - to develop environmental citizenship in the union?
in writing. exposure to ionising radiation can have beneficial effects when controlled (e.g. medicine, research, agriculture, etc.) but can also be harmful. the uses of ionising radiation can thus involve health risks if misused or confined. measures were therefore needed to protect the health of those exposed to it. i therefore welcome the ulmer report, which contains major improvements on this matter. in order to ensure effective protection, member states will now have to harmonise their legislation in this area. there was a need for procedures that were simple and easy to understand and implement.
in writing. one of the aims of the revision is to eliminate inconsistencies between the different legislative acts. i think that the proposal has largely achieved this, so that only a few amendments are necessary. many of the radiation protection aspects covered by the 'basic standards' directive are working very well in practice, which also shows that little change is needed.
in writing. despite the progress made by the european union in the field of the common foreign and security policy, the union still faces many shortcomings. the brok report proposes a clear and decisive strategy that will enable the eu, as an international actor, to improve its efficiency and credibility. the european union's foreign policy is based not only on its political and economic interests but also on fundamental values and principles which define its highly normative identity. citizens' support for foreign policy will only increase its effectiveness. the european parliament's control of the cfsp is therefore crucial. coordination and cooperation of international actions and the strengthening of the role of the high representative are essential for the unity and credibility of eu action.
in writing. i voted in favour of this annual report, which takes stock of the european union's external action in different thematic and geographical areas. it underlines parliament's position on the key issues facing the union in the field of external policy. the s&d group has consistently supported a comprehensive approach to the union's foreign policy. it must be conducted for the benefit of all european citizens, rooted in core european values and supported by constructive cooperation with our strategic partners. given the volatility of the international landscape, the european union needs a coherent foreign policy internally and externally. only by making full use of the institutional tools provided by the treaty of lisbon, foremost among them the european external action service (eeas) and the high representative for foreign affairs and security policy, can the union assume its responsibilities and play its role effectively on the world stage.
in writing. digital will provide the growth and jobs of tomorrow. however, if the european union is to benefit from it, it must prepare for it. this sector is linked to all other markets and must therefore be subject to the same rules. the unification of the 28 national markets must therefore be the european priority today. a single european digital market will in particular enable greater competitiveness on the international stage.
in writing. the commission has set out some of the objectives of a possible revision of the framework as early as its 2007 proposals. these objectives are still relevant: the need for more efficient spectrum management, effective and simple regulation where necessary, and the completion of the internal market for electronic communications. since then, new issues have arisen due to the scale and speed of the evolution of the communications sector and user demand. we have already discussed some of these questions. in addition, fragmentation should be avoided, understood both as different rules applying to different member states and as the framework not forming a coherent whole. a well-designed framework, based on the existing rules, should be able to contain in itself the principles, rules and instruments to deal with these major issues.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i welcome the constructive spirit of debate which prevails in this house, as usual. i also note some prejudice, which is present as usual but, having spent part of my life striving for pluralist democracy, i acknowledge that there are also critical views of the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework (mff). however, i should like to make a brief response. while there may be cases of misuse – and they happen, reflecting the various cultures across europe and the various standards of 28 member states – the fact is that we are recovering, and that is not a waste of taxpayers’ money. to give a tiny illustration of the self-imposed discipline at european level: since 2000, only two national-level budgets have grown at a lesser rate than the european budget, and our budget has grown less than 25 national budgets, despite the ‘big bang’ enlargement, as we started the decade with 15 member states and we are now 28. as for the architecture of this new financial framework, mr callanan was wrong in saying that it is the same as the intergovernmental deal in february 2013. i am not talking only about the review clause coming up in 2016, nor about the high-level group on own resources reflecting on a better way of financing the european budget. the real game-changer is flexibility: unusual flexibility. yes, at the beginning of a financial framework period, we are normally returning money at a time when new projects are trying to accelerate. at the end there is a shortage of money. now with this unusual flexibility – maximum flexibility – we can move unused money and margins and thus respond to the typical logic of implementation of the european budget. mr cohn-bendit is right that in democracy, ‘il n’y a jamais une seule possibilité’, so let us reflect for a minute on what the alternative is. the alternative is annual budgeting, but annual budgeting deprives europe of the best qualities of the multiannual financial framework, namely stability and predictability as it responds to the multiannual nature of investment projects, and this is not the place for revolutionary ideas. this is the place for pragmatic solutions to bottlenecks and problems. it is easy to ask municipalities, regions and research institutions across europe competing globally whether they want a ‘no’ vote or whether they want delivery of the new generation of programmes. there is no magic answer to the european crisis. however, we have a partial, real solution for financing growth and jobs within the reality of fiscal consolidation across europe. with the old rationale of a common, united europe evaporating, legitimacy comes via utility, and our budget is about utility to european citizens. thank you for the spirit of cooperation you have shown.

in writing. the european satellite radio navigation policy aims to equip the union with two satellite radio navigation systems, namely the system resulting from the galileo programme and the egnos system. global navigation satellite systems (gnss) technologies, with their ability to provide highly reliable and accurate measurements of position, speed and time, are fundamental to improving efficiency in many sectors of the economy and in many areas of citizens' daily lives. the galileo programme will not be fully operational in 2013 as planned. since the gnss regulation does not provide a framework for the funding and governance of the galileo and egnos programmes after 2013, a new legal basis is necessary for the systems to be operational, maintained and managed in the long term. i strongly support the objective of the galileo programme, which is to set up the first gnss under civilian control, completely independent of other existing systems, interoperable with other different systems and intended to provide uninterrupted gnss services.
in writing. the economy of the hashemite kingdom of jordan has been particularly affected by the global economic crisis, the arab revolutions and the political transition in the country. external revenues have thus deteriorated considerably and public finances have been affected. the syrian crisis and the mass arrival of refugees have exacerbated this imbalance. despite significant fiscal consolidation efforts and financial support from foreign donors, jordan has launched an appeal for additional assistance. the european union has responded positively and will provide macro-financial assistance to further stabilise the country. the eu is a long-standing partner of jordan and supports its human rights efforts. however, efforts remain to be made, for example, with regard to the legal abolition of the death penalty, the nationality law, gender equality, the protection of all workers.
in writing. under the joint declaration of the european parliament and of the council adopted in parallel with the decision granting additional macro-financial assistance to georgia (adopted by parliament on 4 july 2013), the parliament and the council committed to 'fully implement the considerations and principles [set out in the joint declaration] in the case-by-case decisions to grant union macro-financial assistance'. therefore, the amendments contained in this report and amending the commission proposal for a decision granting macro-financial assistance to jordan reflect the considerations and principles set out in that joint declaration and harmonise the wording of that proposal with the recitals and articles of the decision granting macro-financial assistance to the kyrgyz republic (as adopted during the informal trilogue for a 'fast track second reading agreement').
in writing. the fight against drugs and drug trafficking is a global challenge. drugs ruin lives, threaten the security of citizens, and require considerable financial resources to eliminate. drug precursors, chemicals that can be produced for legal purposes or abused to produce illicit drugs, must be closely monitored. we need to act quickly and in the long term because the sector is changing rapidly. the proust report is particularly relevant. it aims not only to strengthen cooperation between the european union and russia to prevent drug precursors from being diverted from the legal trade but also to combat the illicit manufacture of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am particularly sensitive to the issue of the fight against drugs at international level and i would like to support the european parliament's approval of this agreement for several reasons. this proposal for an agreement between the european union and the russian federation aims to improve cooperation between these two major trading partners in the field of monitoring trade in drug precursors. these precursors are legal substances that can be used in the chemical process of manufacturing synthetic drugs. for example, acetic acid is used in the manufacture of heroin. they are subject to checks at export, import and transit which vary according to the risk of diversion.
in writing. i do not question the operational needs of member states who want europol to conclude agreements with brazil, georgia, mexico and the united arab emirates. i would argue, however, that the draft decision cannot be adopted on the basis of provisions which are not in accordance with the treaty of lisbon. concerns also remain regarding the current level of data protection in some of the states on the list. therefore, even if the draft decision were to be adopted, the director and the management board of europol should refrain from entering into any negotiation of operational agreements with the states on that list until the new europol regulation has entered into force.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a council regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 723/2009 on a community legal framework for a european research infrastructure consortium (eric) and approve the commission proposal.
in writing. − this regulation establishes the framework for the european structural and investment funds. the revision of the european funds should ensure that they are better used to reduce unemployment and poverty and that investments are sustainable and prioritised. during the negotiations parliament made important improvements. however, these are threatened by the macroeconomic conditionality which the commission and the council intend to impose. i am pleased with the increased participation of local partners and civil society through a binding code of conduct. bad spending will be better prevented by ex ante conditionality (e.g. anti-discrimination, gender equality and environmental impact assessment policies). in addition, environmental and climate protection is built in through the horizontal principles and conditions and there is a lower limit of expenditure for the european and social funds. i am in favour of this sustainability and social reform. i am, however, strongly opposed to linking these funds to macroeconomic conditionality. the extension of the conditionalities of the stability and growth pact to the regions completely undermines the purpose of the structural and investment funds. if this is imposed, we will deprive the regions of one of the few opportunities for much-needed public investment in difficult financial and economic times.
in writing. in the context of the continuing economic and financial crisis and related uncertainties, the need to consolidate public budgets has required greater innovation and a greater impact of the funds available. cohesion policy, through the use of its instruments, namely the structural funds and the cohesion fund, has long demonstrated its added value as an indispensable tool for effectively promoting growth and job creation by precisely responding to the investment needs of all regions. it has not only contributed to reducing disparities between member states and regions, but also to economic recovery and development throughout the union. the same applies to the agricultural development fund and the fisheries fund. however, i voted against this text because several of the amendments it contains jeopardise the objectives set out and i ask that this report be reconsidered because the instruments proposed threaten european solidarity and put at great risk those countries which are already experiencing the greatest problems. the conclusion of this text is to want to do better and do worse.
in writing. i regret that there are not more resources allocated to regional policy because it is a mobilizing element of european solidarity. austerity is not a unilateral cut in spending but the courage to choose priorities. the funds are being misused, and they are a real common investment in our future and a unique way of countering the effects of the crisis on the most disadvantaged people and regions. the european social fund (esf) is, however, an important vehicle for regional policy, fostering synergy between the 271 european regions. the esf shall contribute to supporting growth and job creation in the union; it is the world's largest human capital investment fund. i voted in favour of this text because it is through this fund that initiatives promoting employment are taken, including training to help the unemployed find their way back to employment and initiatives to better integrate disabled people into society.
in writing. the esf must remain a major eu policy, in particular in supporting regional authorities in financing continuing training. the european social fund also aims to increase employment opportunities, promote lifelong learning, strengthen social inclusion, contribute to the fight against poverty and help public administrations to better serve citizens and jobseekers. the european social fund is a major tool in the policy of recovery!
in writing. the text as approved provides a clearer and simplified framework for investment, as it ensures coordination with other fund-specific regulations, as well as with the regulation on common provisions, through the links established and the thematic objectives and/or investment priorities. this is a major step forward in improving coordination and strengthening synergies between the funds and the implementation of the funds to achieve smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in line with the europe 2020 strategy. the new elements of thematic concentration provide for a greater concentration of resources on a limited number of objectives, which should result in a higher added value of assistance. finally, the new erdf includes for the first time a mandatory urban dimension and ensures that a broader priority is given to urban development at a strategic level.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this text because we are now setting the foundations for the future of the whole of europe in our border regions. for people living in a border region, territorial cooperation is and will remain of paramount importance, especially in the fields of health, social security and training. to achieve these ambitious objectives, i believe that even more resources should have been allocated to regional policy. however, the need and importance of this text go beyond the question of the budget. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this regulation defines the scope of the european regional development fund for the european territorial cooperation objective. the commission has chosen to propose a separate regulation for european territorial cooperation in order to take full account of its specificities and its plurinational context. one of the novel features of the proposal is that it contains provisions on thematic concentration and investment priorities. the improvement in the strategic orientation of programmes and their focus on results is a positive development. in addition, it is necessary to reduce the administrative burden and to provide for greater harmonisation of the rules in order to facilitate the implementation of the programme and the overall success of cooperation. the rapporteur believes that the commission should provide, at the request of parliament or the council, updated reports on the effectiveness of cohesion policy and the added value and growth it generates.
in writing. under the legislative package for cohesion policy proposed by the commission, the cohesion fund is part of the new common strategic framework funds, which will cover the structural funds, the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development and the european maritime and fisheries fund. all these funds will be subject to common provisions in several areas of programming and financial management. in addition, as in the current programming period, the cohesion fund, the erdf and the esf will continue to be governed by another set of common specific rules on programming, management and monitoring. although the commission is proposing a new framework for the funds, the scope of the cohesion fund and its specific objectives have not changed significantly from the current programming period. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. i am in favour of this text because it is a matter of simplified and clarified rules which will help to increase legal certainty and encourage more future partners to strengthen territorial cooperation with the union and between regions of the member states and third countries.
in writing. the principle of gender equality is one of the fundamental principles of the european union. it is therefore worrying to see that this balance is still not being respected today and that there are still serious imbalances in this area. it is regrettable that we have to rely on a binding legal basis to ensure that this balance is respected, and that common sense is not enough to eliminate this discrimination. the proposed objective of raising the proportion of non-executive directors of the underrepresented sex to at least 40% by 2020 in privately listed companies and by 2018 in publicly listed companies is therefore an unfortunate necessity which i support. the european union must set an example and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. why compensate for inequality of fact by inequality of law? this is the question that the european parliament has clearly neglected when it adopted by a large majority the kratsa-regner report on the quota of women on the boards of publicly traded companies. a report that specifically targets the objective of at least 40% female representation on boards: as of january 2018 for public enterprises, and in january 2020 for private companies. i abstained on the final vote on the legislative proposal. i am not going to go into the details of the vote on the report, but i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware of the fact that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. what is the legitimacy of interfering in the life of private companies and of imposing penalties for non-compliance with the directive? if europe is serious about a gender policy that delivers results, then it must be concerned about the condition of working women in general and the difficulty they face, on a daily basis, in achieving a better balance between work and family life. it is another debate, but it is the real debate, the only one capable of ever meeting the goal of real equality between the sexes.
in writing. − in 2011, the european commission called on companies to make voluntary efforts on women's representation on their boards. in 2013, it was estimated that only 16.6% of women are in the highest decision-making bodies of large european companies. this is not because of a shortage of qualified women, since 60% of university graduates in the eu are women, but because the voluntary approach has failed miserably. compelling companies to change has already proven successful in closing the gender gap in several eu member states and encouraging these companies to tap into new talent. the report to be voted on today (20/11/2013) will continue this line at european level and will require large public (by 2018) and private (by 2020) companies to adapt their recruitment, selection and appointment procedures to increase female representation on boards to at least 40%. if two equal candidates of the opposite sex remain, the company is obliged to choose the underrepresented sex. i am convinced that a more diverse board of directors is an added value for a company and will benefit us all, and that is why i am voting for this report with my group, the greens.
in writing. the european parliament has just taken a big step in its fight for greater equality between women and men. the text adopted introduces a minimum rate of 40% of women on the boards of directors. what was only a request a short while ago is now a legal obligation under penalty of sanctions for the most unruly companies. equality becomes more than a concept! the european parliament has taken a decision of major consequence to break the glass ceiling which prevents european women from accessing positions of responsibility. it is a pity that we have to impose quotas, but it seems to be the only way of getting some companies out of their old ways.
in writing. after three years of intensive negotiations and political agreement, the european parliament gives its final agreement on the new common agricultural policy of the european union. for the first time, parliament took part in the legislative process as a co-decision-maker. this has considerably increased the legitimacy of this new policy. this reform has simplified the way the cap operates and has strengthened the necessary balance between food security and enhanced environmental protection. as regards direct payments, we supported the compromise proposals on greening, the right to payment, the optional scheme for small farmers, internal convergence and the scheme for young farmers. as regards the regulation of the common organization of the market, we considered that the compromise proposals were, on the whole, moving in the right direction. we have been particularly careful not to unravel the cmos. european funds will now be distributed more equitably to enable all european farmers to better meet the challenges of the market. new tools have also been introduced to ensure a degree of stability in this market, which is often subject to price volatility.
in writing. the european parliament finally votes on the new european common agricultural policy (cap). the two key words are "fairness" and "flexibility". the new cap is fairer because it distributes agricultural aid more evenly. it is also more flexible and will allow aid to be redistributed to sectors in difficulty such as livestock farming. the new cap is not perfect, but it is a plus for european agriculture and will help to avoid the worst. good quality and affordable food for a growing population, vibrant rural areas and sound and sustainable agriculture: these are the objectives of the common agricultural policy. agriculture must be preserved to ensure that the half billion europeans can still eat 'made in europe' throughout this century.
in writing. in july 2012, the european commission published three legislative proposals to strengthen consumer protection in financial services, including retail packaged investment products prips. the aim of the commission proposal is to improve transparency and the protection of retail investors in the eu retail investment market. consumers should be provided with a key investor information document in a standardised and easy to understand format. i voted against article 13d which caps the price of advice at 200 euros because it is hardly acceptable in a market where competition between advisers is particularly strong.
in writing. i voted for the report by mrs pervenche berès. this regulation lays down uniform rules on the format and content of the key information document to be drawn up exclusively by the originators of investment products, on the attachment to the key information document to be drawn up, where appropriate, by persons selling investment products, on the information to be provided to retail investors by persons selling investment products in accordance with the mif directive and the insurance intermediation directive of the european parliament and of the council (imd directive) and on the uniform rules on the provision of such documents to retail investors. it is intended to enable retail investors to understand and compare the essential characteristics of investment products and the risks inherent in them, and it places the responsibility for the preparation of the key information document on the originator of the investment product and the responsibility for the preparation of the notes on the accounts on the persons selling investment products.

in writing. - for the first time, the european parliament took part in the decision-making process on agricultural policy. unfortunately, that has not proved to be a guarantee of greening. in fact, farmers no longer have to comply with all existing directives on sustainable pesticide use, water management and nature conservation to qualify for income support. the commission's proposal to set aside a compulsory 7% of a farmer's area for nature, water and landscape management was reduced to 5%. in addition, the measures to be taken for greening were also elaborated. there's no breeding rotation, either, and i'm not going to. instead, mandatory crop diversification is introduced, but that too has been eroded. farmers who fail to comply with the reduced obligations may only lose part of their support if they have been in breach for several years. this reform misses the opportunity to give a boost to sustainable agriculture and to give agriculture a role not only in food production but also in landscape conservation and restoration, water policy, soil protection, biodiversity and animal welfare. the consumer pays three times: the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the environment, such as the reduction of the use of pesticides, the reduction of the use of pesticides and the reduction of the use of pesticides. for these reasons i voted against the compromise reached.

in writing. i welcome the agreement concluded between the european union and the republic of kiribati. this is an equitable partnership. in exchange for a financial contribution, the eu will be able to exploit the fishery resources of the republic of kiribati through its community vessels. the agreement provides a partnership framework which will ensure the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of resources. in addition, the fisheries sector is essential for the country's economy and development. agreements with foreign ships generate 20 to 30% of national revenues. the country has one of the lowest gdp per capita in the region and is thus one of the least developed acp states. this agreement is therefore essential for the development of the country but also for ensuring that the fisheries sector is a sustainable sector.

the rapporteur. - mr president, before this meeting with the commissioners began, we said to ourselves that if we did not take into account the presence at the meeting of those who are obliged to be there because they are associated with the report, there would be no big world left. i have indeed observed this, and i would therefore like to thank those who are not involved in the proceedings here, but who nevertheless do us the honour of being here. i am not joking, because my first disappointment with horizon 2020 is the gap between its size and the lack of interest in research and innovation issues, apart from the speeches, in the political class. it's something that worries me, i can't hide it from you. the commission's ambition was to spend 100 billion over seven years, which would have been a relatively modest but nevertheless ambitious step forward. we didn't get it. you and we have tried to get a budget higher than what we have been spending so far, namely to get the 100 billion. we are now at about 70 billion and i have to say that the responsibility lies with the council and the political groups which have accepted the budgetary perspectives for the next seven years. if we had to structure the program ourselves, we would probably have structured it quite well, as you have done. we therefore agree quite well with the commission's approach. i would like to stress that it was essential to focus our research and innovation efforts, in particular, on the societal challenges that lie ahead, and i think the societal challenges selected by the commission are the right ones. whether it is health or food, whether it is climate or the environment, whether it is the cohesion of our societies, their security - let us say that too - particularly in the energy sector, we are very pleased that 85 per cent of research expenditure in this area is now devoted to what can be called, in general terms, the energy transition - an area in which i believe europe can claim global leadership positions. if we want to be a competitive continent, it is by creating value, by innovating, by being at the forefront of innovation in these societal challenges that we can achieve this, not by reducing our costs everywhere, especially in the fields of labour and social protection. the third point concerns the question of access to research results and data. first of all, when public authorities finance research, it is normal that the results should be freely available to all. in general, i would be rather concerned that if we want societies to innovate, we need knowledge to circulate. we are increasingly in a situation where knowledge is 'commoditised' and therefore protected by intellectual property protection rules which have become an inhibitor of innovation. i am far from the idea that we should innovate and then make everything we do available for free to everyone, including our competitors. i am not naive, but i think that today, on the line between closed innovation and open innovation, the cursor is far too much on the side of protection and far too little on the side of information flow. we have been able to change this cursor during these negotiations - not quite to our liking, but it is progress. the fourth element concerns the question of social innovation. for example, we now waste 30% of the food we produce in europe. i don't think anyone here is happy about this situation. if we want to drastically reduce this waste of food - which is also a waste of energy and a waste of resources - it is obvious that we must provide the necessary innovations with a technological dimension but, above all, with a social dimension. how do we organise our food production and distribution systems? how do we organize our cities and our countryside to reduce food waste? in this respect, both social and technological innovation are necessary and i would really encourage the commission to take account, to the extent it is able, of the social innovation dimension in all areas that are part of the programme - where, of course, it makes sense. the fifth dimension i want to mention is that of small and mediumsized enterprises. many of us say when we talk about smes: "that's great! smes are innovating! smes create jobs! it is the smes that must be favoured". i find that this is often the case in the speech, until the point where you have to put money on the table. on this point we are rather disappointed, because while the nominal objective of devoting about 20% of the programme to actors who are smes is uniformly accepted, the fact of limiting to ringfencer, to speak french of money to smes was one of the hard points of the negotiation. in the end, we got 4% of the programme devoted to this. that's good. that's good. i welcome the fact that the management of this money is entrusted to a commission agency and i stress this point , thus proving that it is possible for the commission to work with smes; i would like to say that it is possible to find people in the commission who speak the language of smes, who have a way of working that is suited to smes. i think it is extremely important that we have made this agency the vehicle for the money we want to spend on smes. the last element - and probably the most troubling - concerns the question of leverage. today, with public money scarce, it is important that each euro spent has a maximum leverage effect, i.e. that it mobilises private investment and investment in the member states to the maximum. today, with the rules of participation you are about to vote on, the leverage of horizon 2020 will be weaker than that of its predecessor, the seventh framework programme. i think we should have done the exact opposite, which is why we will not vote on this part of the report.
first of all, mr president, i think we should thank the commission for the fight it has waged to finally release the budget available for horizon 2020. i think that we as a parliament and as a commission can be particularly proud of the fact that we have once again managed to reserve a substantial part of this amount for top-level research in the european union. we would naturally like to see a little more ambition from the member states, including a real shift in priorities towards innovation, because innovation will be needed to get back on track with economic growth in europe. the important thing about this programme is that we keep the focus on cutting-edge research, that we can bring together the best researchers there and in that way also deliver cutting-edge products back to the market. we really need that kind of industrial leadership in europe. in addition, cooperation with smes is extremely important in order to involve smaller companies in this type of research project and to make real use of their expertise. of course, the bureaucracy must be eliminated there too, as the commission has promised, in order to make it possible to invest this money in a good way. i think it is now time for the member states to join this european strategy. it is also time to pool resources with them and look at how we can effectively link economic growth with more and better innovation.
madam president, the horizon 2020 research programme raises a lot of hopes, as we have seen, but also some concerns. let me focus on two concerns. the first concerns israel's participation in this programme - which i am not opposed to at all - which has caused controversy because, on the one hand, israel enjoys a privileged status as the only non-european state to participate in this programme, with a budget of several hundred million euros, even as the policy of colonisation and occupation continues in palestine. but also, on the other hand, because of israel's initial refusal to endorse the european union directives prohibiting the financing and provision of loans and grants, scholarships or prizes to institutions beyond the 1967 lines. fortunately, in the last few days israel has finally agreed, for the first time, to recognise the european policy which prohibits the transfer of funds to israeli companies or institutions in the settlements, and to make proposals to the negotiators. it is crucial, commissioners, that the agreement includes a clause stating that the settlements in the west bank, east jerusalem and the golan heights are not part of the state of israel. i am particularly concerned about east jerusalem. this clause is a red line for many of us and i am writing a letter to mrs ashton today to that effect. my second concern - i will be very brief - is stem cell research. as a former dean of a faculty and director of a very large research centre, i would like to say that ethical values are at the heart of our function and our career as researchers; i have participated in all the european programmes in this field. but stem cell research today is vital - as luís paulo alves said - for the treatment of genetic diseases. if it is to be framed by ethical values, it cannot be impeded by any religious dogmatism. it is in the name of religion that some members of parliament want to block this type of research and for me, as a researcher, this is unacceptable.
president. - mr president, i am sorry to hear that you have not been able to attend the debate on the report. i think what we really need to do today as policymakers is make sure that we create the right ecosystem for entrepreneurship. we see today that too often there are still too many obstacles to the development of genuine entrepreneurship. first of all, i think there are things that every business faces, whether it's our small businesses, but also our larger businesses: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to take measures to ensure that the social partners are not over-regulated, but also to ensure that the member states are able to implement structural reforms in their labour markets in order to create a more competitive environment. secondly, there is of course the activation of dormant capital. we must look at how we as the european union can remove barriers to ensure that the dormant capital that is currently sitting on the sidelines can be activated and that it can flow back to smes and mediumsized enterprises through private equity, venture capital and also loans from traditional banks. in general, i think we should also work on a change of mentality. today we see that too few people dare to take risks. we too, as policy makers, are too often focused on eliminating risk rather than encouraging risk taking. we must also work to enable the private sector to take the risks necessary to keep pace with economic growth.

in writing. in voting for this report, i expressed my strong support for the three pillars proposed in this 2020 framework programme for research and innovation. in concrete terms, it is about supporting and responding to the societal challenges ahead, whether they are related to health, energy, transport, climate action or security, to boosting scientific excellence as well as our industrial leadership, particularly in biotechnology and space technologies. as we know, small and mediumsized enterprises (smes) are the economic lungs of the european union. the report will provide almost eur 70.2 billion directly to support these three key objectives, including through the allocation of concrete financial support. this programme will thus help to combat the current economic crisis, stimulate research and innovation and encourage scientific and industrial excellence. i welcome the adoption of this report, which is a major positive signal of europe's support for our recovery.
in writing. i welcome this report which allocates €70.2 billion to the framework programme for research and innovation. the programme changes will allow for better support for smes, science and for the allocation of funds for research into non-fossil energy. to face the future in an increasingly interdependent and interconnected world, we must join forces and invest in research and innovation. this programme will help the eu to become more competitive. i fully support the investments allocated to smes, which represent at least 11% of the budget. europe has a vital role to play in equalising the opportunities for entrepreneurs throughout europe. we must help those countries which have difficulty in accessing technology and knowledge. it is more than necessary to create a 'productive solidarity'.
in writing. the recovery of the european union and its competitiveness in the world is evident through research and innovation. that is why the vote this afternoon on the horizon 2020 programme for the period 2014-2020 is essential and responds to the need to look to the future. compared to the previous research programme, there has been considerable progress: the budget is increasing with an allocation of eur 70 billion; a specific budget is allocated to smes; the emphasis is on public-private partnerships and the rules are simplified; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme and will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. two reserves, though. the first is linked to the unfounded attacks on israel's participation in the horizon 2020 initiative: it ignores the fact that israel is the most active associated non-member state in european research projects and it ignores the transfer of scientific knowledge that benefits european companies, estimated at 600 million euros for the next seven years. the other reservation concerns the status quo on embryonic stem cells and the lack of real commitment by the european union to the freedom of therapeutic research.
in writing. the financial and economic crisis has revealed the weaknesses of the european production model. to ensure that europe emerges strong from this crisis and that the european economy recovers, the europe 2020 strategy focuses on research and innovation as a means of moving towards a knowledge-based economy, guaranteeing more balanced, diverse and sustainable growth. however, the economic model advocated by the europe 2020 strategy, based on high levels of employment, productivity and social cohesion, will only succeed if we ensure the stability of the research and innovation system in terms of economic and human resources. in other words, a decrease in investment in r & d & i logically affects the performance of the scientific and technological system, its capacity to create knowledge, which ultimately negatively affects our competitiveness and social welfare. it is therefore absolutely essential that the funding for community research and innovation policy not only be spared the impact of budget cuts but that it be given additional resources. for this reason, and because the new programme strengthens the innovation component and extends the range of instruments available to it.
in writing. the real needs of the participating industrial players must be addressed. the most decisive measure in this respect is the introduction of an explicit limit of six months for the time limits for the actual granting of grants. time is becoming an increasingly important factor, as horizon 2020 aims to foster innovation. this is particularly true for highly innovative enterprises and smes. a shorter grant award period is also a prerequisite for attracting excellent research partners from all over the world, with internationalisation being another attraction for participating industrial players.
in writing. the eit is neither a programme nor a network: the eit is an institute. while it is true that it carries out its activities within the framework of a programme and that it forms technology and innovation networks with many different partners, this institute has an important role to play, a role which goes beyond the simple management, coordination or animation of its kics. as an institute, it should be given a very special treatment, different from that reserved for the other sections of the horizon 2020 programme. as a tool directly involved in innovation but also a vehicle for teaching, the eit makes education a fully-fledged part of the union's research and innovation policy. the eit occupies a special place in the overall framework of union policy: it is the only instrument that realizes the knowledge triangle. we must support this programme.
in writing. through the activities of the knowledge and innovation communities (kics), the eit promotes closer interaction between universities, research centres and businesses to bridge the gap between research, teaching and entrepreneurship. the aim is to increase europe's capacity for innovation. the pilot project will be implemented in the framework of the european solidarity corps (esc) and the european solidarity corps (esc) and will be implemented in the framework of the european solidarity corps (esc). they involve more than 200 partners. the experience gained so far indicates an increasing number of participants (including from industry), a satisfactory leverage effect, good rationalisation and tangible results (young start-ups, trained students, etc.).
in writing. the union is going through a difficult economic period. the challenges are growing. real answers are to be expected. if europeans want to see real smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as the 2020 strategy suggests, the european union, in partnership with all national authorities, must focus on the competitiveness of enterprises, and more particularly smes. the latter currently generate 67% of private sector jobs in europe and 58% of total turnover in the european union. despite their importance, many constraints persist, directly hindering their proper development. i therefore welcome with great enthusiasm the reports on business competitiveness and the entrepreneurship 2020 action plan, both of which stress the importance of simplifying bureaucracy while providing funds and credits that enable businesses to better meet current challenges.

in writing. statistics are very useful in decision-making. the transparency and independence of statisticians is an essential prerequisite for the reliability of the statistics provided. greater transparency and independence between the european statistical system and the national statistical institutions will significantly reduce the distortion of data, which is dangerous not only for democracy but also for the economies of the member states.
in writing. reliable and accurate european statistics fulfil two key functions as a public good: they are the basis on which policy-makers take their decisions and they act as a barometer of the state of our economy and society, providing assurances to other governments and financial markets. but events in recent years have shaken public and market confidence. a 2008 eurobarometer survey found that 45% of citizens said they did not trust economic statistics, a figure almost identical to the 46% of citizens who said the opposite. this regulation is timely: we need to strengthen public confidence in statistical data. there is a saying that once statistics are politicized, they are quickly devalued. it is therefore essential to remove any political dimension from the compilation of statistics. the report proposes that member states should be prohibited from postponing the publication of periodical data.
in writing. many european citizens are now in a vulnerable situation due to the adverse effects of the economic and financial crisis. poverty, insecurity and unemployment are on the increase. the european union needs to support the social policies of the member states in order to guarantee all its citizens a fair social system that redistributes equitably the wealth created. i therefore very much welcome the programme which aims in particular to promote the voluntary geographical mobility of workers and to promote access to microfinance for young enterprises. the report also strengthens the union's policy in social areas such as the fight against exclusion and poverty, while promoting social protection and inclusion. particular attention was also paid to young people.

in writing. for 20 years, life has been a highly successful instrument for addressing the environmental and climate challenges faced by european citizens. it is a modest but well-targeted and effective instrument, highly appreciated by local, regional and national public administrations, ngos, research institutions and smes. the results achieved by life are also very satisfactory from a budgetary point of view, with a systematically and significantly higher than average rate of implementation. i will conclude by saying that one euro invested today is 100 euros in 2050!
in writing. the action programme for taxation in the european union for the period 2014-2020 (fiscalis 2020) is helping to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. it should be remembered that tax evasion costs the governments of the european union countries about 860 billion euros and tax evasion nearly 150 billion euros. it is therefore our duty as eu representatives to react swiftly and firmly. fiscalis 2020 proposes regular exchanges of information, based on well-defined and transparent rules and operational means of communication between the different actors, which do not increase administrative constraints or burdens. the aim is to strengthen the internal market through effective tax systems and to improve the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and especially active tax avoidance through better cooperation between member states. i am indeed in favour of even more coordinated action by all eu member states to combat tax fraud and tax evasion.
in writing. i support the idea of continuing the successful implementation of the previous fiscalis 2013 programme during the new eu programming period. the fiscalis 2013 programme received a very favourable assessment from all stakeholders (in particular from national tax authorities) during the mid-term review in 2010, and the national authorities have therefore requested that it be continued beyond 2013. this programme brings real european added value and responds to the european parliament's call for closer cooperation and coordination between national tax authorities in the fight against tax evasion, tax fraud and double non-taxation, as well as a reduction in administrative burdens, obstacles to the functioning of the single market and double taxation. in addition, it aims to encourage innovation and technical progress in the tax administrations of the member states and should therefore allow for greater productivity of national administrations.
in writing. the customs union is the very foundation of the european economic construction. however, the new challenges facing the eu mean that we must modernise it in order to ensure that european citizens are effectively protected against the risks posed by international trade in goods. in order to combat fraud more effectively, to safeguard intellectual property and to improve competitiveness, this report stresses the importance of strengthening cooperation with as many actors as possible: the participating countries, their customs authorities, external experts, international organisations, european union authorities such as olaf and third countries. a global approach is, in my view, the best solution.
in writing. following the decision of the conference of presidents of 16 may 2012 confirming the request of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection and the committee on economic and monetary affairs to split these two programmes, the commission has amended its view to take account of the position of parliament and the council. on 29 august 2012, it adopted an amended proposal on customs 2020 and fiscalis 2020. the commission's customs 2020 proposal is based on article 33 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), which calls for the european union to act in the field of customs cooperation and the union's customs union. in accordance with the proposal for a new multiannual financial framework as amended on 6 july 2012, this regulation on the customs 2020 programme contains a budgetary envelope of eur 548 080 000 (in current prices) for the period 2014-2020. i am pleased that the commission has already taken into consideration parliament's request to split the old fiscus proposal into a customs and a fiscalis programme.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i would like to thank the members for their contributions to this debate. i am sensitive to the criticism of colleagues who advocate respect for the sovereignty of the member states and the economical and efficient use of taxpayers' money. these concerns are my concerns. i would not like my name to be mentioned in the report on the justice programme if it does not explicitly refer to the effective and correct application of the principle of subsidiarity. the explanatory memorandum also expressly states that the legal traditions of the member states are respected. this programme is about promoting cooperation between member states and not about creating yet more european unity. in order to ensure that taxpayers' money is spent properly, the use of available resources is evaluated on the basis of a list of clear indicators. the european parliament should also assume its responsibility in this respect and should therefore review the commission's annual monitoring report as well as the interim evaluation report, which should be available by june 2018. the commission shall be assisted by the european parliament and the council. the public list of projects receiving grants and the brief summary of their activities should increase transparency. in any event, provision is made for the detection and investigation of irregularities or possible irregularities in the expenditure of funds, the recovery of sums wrongly paid and the imposition of administrative and financial penalties in accordance with the financial regulation.

in writing. the process of globalisation has implications for the sovereignty of states, political regimes, law and, therefore, justice. it is therefore important to set up framework programmes to facilitate collaboration and cooperation between member states. the new justice programme aims to promote judicial cooperation and training and to guarantee access to justice for all. improving knowledge of european law is a key issue if we want better application of decisions which are legislated. this will strengthen the rights of european citizens.
in writing. the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides for the creation of an area of freedom, security and justice allowing the free movement of persons. to this end, the union should adopt measures to develop judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters and to encourage and support action by member states in the field of crime prevention. in pursuing the establishment of a european area of justice, respect for fundamental rights and common principles such as non-discrimination, equality between women and men, effective access to justice for all, the rule of law and the existence of an effective independent judiciary should be ensured.
in writing. the rights, equality and citizenship programme 2014-2020 aims to meet the objectives of the stockholm programme by streamlining its funding instruments. to this end, the report proposes the merger of three former programmes, namely the fundamental rights and citizenship programme, daphne ii and the anti-discrimination and diversity and gender equality sections of the employment and social solidarity programme (progress). the aim of this report is to promote the rights of european citizenship and to support certain fundamental principles such as the principle of non-discrimination, equality between men and women, the protection of personal data and the rights of children and consumers. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which aims to simplify the financing instruments, to consolidate data and to make procedures more efficient.
in writing. i strongly support the rights and citizenship programme for the period 2014-2020. at present, there is still too much discrimination on grounds of sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation in europe. this programme is fighting against racism, xenophobia, homophobia and other forms of intolerance. it promotes the rights of disabled people, gender equality, the rights of the child, the exercise of the rights deriving from union citizenship, etc. citizens still face too many obstacles when they want to exercise their rights. this programme will increase awareness of union law and policies, promoting the effective, comprehensive and coherent implementation and application of union instruments and policies in the member states, as well as their monitoring and evaluation. the foundation of our european political system cannot be based on ignorance, especially since all the decisions taken at this level have a direct impact on the well-being of each citizen.
in writing. the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. these values are common to the member states in a society characterised by pluralism, non-discrimination, tolerance, justice, solidarity and equality between women and men. everyone in the union must be able to enjoy the rights conferred on him by the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the treaty on european union. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, has become binding throughout the union, sets out the fundamental rights and freedoms which citizens of the union can rely on. these rights should be promoted and respected. the full enjoyment of those rights, as well as of the rights deriving from international conventions to which the union is a party, should be guaranteed.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 55/2008 provides for autonomous trade preferences ('the pca') for the republic of moldova by removing all tariff duties on industrial products and improving access to the european union market for agricultural products. it provides that the pca are to apply until 31 december 2015. the application of the regulation introducing the pca after 1 january 2013 depends on the successful outcome of certain procedures within the world trade organisation (wto). the european union has initiated these procedures but the date for their completion is not yet known. pending the outcome of the wto procedures, it is therefore important to ensure that trade flows from the republic of moldova can continue without interruption until 31 december 2015. it is also necessary to ensure legal certainty for economic operators to continue to import in accordance with the provisions of the regulation introducing the apas. it is therefore essential to provide that those pcas apply without interruption until their expiry date as set out in council regulation (ec) no 55/2008.
in writing. − the eu stands up for the rights of minorities and disadvantaged groups, but the bottom line is that the emphasis is on strategic trade considerations. by denying the right of self-determination and the rights of the people of western sahara, the eu is becoming more of a cause of the conflict between rabat and the sahrawi people than a solution. in december 2011, the european parliament blocked an earlier version of the fisheries agreement with morocco, precisely because it violated the right to self-determination. this statement followed the line of the un general assembly and security council, the international court of justice and the african union. we should have followed the example of other countries, such as the united states, which have included an exception for western sahara in their agreements with morocco. moreover, there is only one reporting obligation for morocco on the respect of international law and human rights in relation to the sahrawi. anyone who knows anything about morocco's human rights record knows that the country does not have the greatest credibility in this regard. as the winner of the nobel peace prize, which she was awarded exactly one year ago, i would have expected the eu to have a little more backbone.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text because if the required conditions are not met, the agreement will be suspended, which is an important guarantee that justifies my choice. after the european parliament refused last december to approve the one-year extension of the fisheries protocol with morocco, which was due to expire on 27 february 2012, the commission started negotiations for the conclusion of a new protocol, which was submitted for approval. the two sides negotiated with full regard for developments in the european parliament and agreed that the new text should aim to respond to the criticisms and guidance expressed in the fisheries committee report and in the resolution adopted in parallel, which called for ensuring that the agreement is mutually beneficial and based on economic, social and environmental sustainability.
