in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition, so that the european union as a whole can ratify the protocol against the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms which has not yet entered into force. this ratification will, among other things, improve the exchange of information between member states, help to combat arms trafficking, terrorism and organised crime groups and harmonise at european level the licensing and licensing criteria for the export and import of firearms.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report which authorises the council to conclude, on behalf of the european union, an additional protocol to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime. the protocol will be the first comprehensive instrument to combat transnational organised crime and the illicit trade in firearms. it will establish a framework and a set of high-level minimum standards for all states parties and also encourage cooperation among states to prevent, combat and eradicate the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms, their parts, components and ammunition.
in writing. four member states have not yet signed or acceded to the protocol: 18 eu member states have signed the protocol, and 16 member states are contracting parties. the ratification of the protocol by the european union will make the provisions of the protocol legally binding for all member states within the limits of european competence. the protocol aims to prevent, combat and eradicate the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. it advocates the criminalization of the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition and the falsification or erasure of the marking of firearms, as well as the attempted or facilitated commission of such an offence, subject to the different legal traditions of the states parties. it provides for measures to confiscate illicitly manufactured or trafficked weapons and measures to prevent the illicit reactivation of deactivated firearms.
in writing. with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the european union has enlarged its customs union. consequently, it was obliged, under the rules of the world trade organisation, to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights in the lists of acceding countries in order to agree on mutually satisfactory compensation to offset the increased consolidated rights and the resulting material losses. such compensation is necessary if the adoption of the external tariff regime of the union leads to an increase in duties beyond the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto, while 'duly taking into account the reductions in customs duties on the same tariff line made by other constituent entities of the customs union at the time of the establishment of that union'.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's hormones are not used in the production of meat. a disagreement over the european union's ban on hormone-treated beef has long been a point of contention between the union and the united states. however, on 13 may 2009, the two parties signed a memorandum of understanding, paving the way for a final resolution of this "hormone beef dispute". a solution acceptable to both parties was a gradual lifting of the us sanctions on certain products of european agriculture in return for the opening of an autonomous tariff quota with zero duty for high-quality meat from non-hormone-treated bovine animals. the memorandum led to the lifting of sanctions and the increase to 45 000 tonnes of the autonomous tariff quota with zero duty for high-quality beef, on the basis of the most favoured nation principle.

in writing. i voted in favour of this request. the danish authorities argue that the european wind turbine manufacturing sector is severely affected by changes in the structure of international trade, which result in a significant reduction of the union market share. demand for renewable energy, including wind power, will increase significantly, but markets will change. while the wind sector was dominated by europe until 2006 and until recently experienced growth equally shared between europe, asia and the united states, today we are seeing a rise in demand in asia and north america, a development that will be experienced by south america in the future and africa in the longer term. manufacturing and maintenance activities will move to where demand is expressed and to regions with rapid economic growth. due to the high transport costs of the large parts of their wind turbines and also in order to benefit from significantly cheaper labour, european producers are therefore forced to bring their production closer to the most dynamic end-user markets in order to remain competitive and secure their market position. as a result, production started to gradually migrate outside the union.

in writing. deep-sea fishing, which will take up between 400 and 1 500 metres below the sea surface, uses trawls, which are like bottom-dwelling bulldozers, throwing their huge, multi-tonne nets that scratch the ground and pick up whatever they can. the vote is a step we would have liked to have taken bigger, but a step in the right direction for an end to the ploughing of the seas. it is also worth remembering that this fishery, which destroys 4,000-year-old corals in five minutes, represents only 1.7% of european catches. environmental disaster, financial deficit, fuel consumption that exceeds the limits (half a liter of diesel for a kilo of fish caught), fish stocks that do not have time to regenerate: let's be clear, deep-sea fishing is not sustainable!

in writing. - the european parliament voted today on a report calling for better consumer protection in the taking out of loans and mortgages in the real estate market. irresponsible lending played a major role in the current economic crisis, as it led to bubbles and massive debt for millions of consumers in europe. this agreement is a breakthrough in mortgage regulation, thanks to increased transparency of the cost of taking out mortgages. in the future, consumers will receive a standardised information document (esis) that provides the main details of the credit provision in an easily comparable and transparent manner before they sign the contract. costs incurred for loans in another currency should warn of additional costs due to changing exchange rates. in the case of extremely high costs, a rebate or a protection mechanism can also be put in place to protect consumers from hidden costs; but he who desires to make amends before the time appointed, shall not be punished more severely. despite the fact that the new rules do not yet take sufficient account of the risks of irresponsible borrowing, i am voting in favour of this report because it provides greater protection for consumers.
in writing. since the crisis, the need to lend and borrow responsibly has increased. the fsa's mortgage market analysis from july 2010 recognises that around 50% of all mortgage applications in 2007 and 2008 were processed without an income check and that at the peak of the market almost 33% of all residential mortgages in the uk were sold on an interest-only basis, with around three quarters of these loans not specifying a repayment method. achieving the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy for sustainable growth and learning from the crisis, in line with the g20 roadmap, requires a stable, robust, efficient and competitive internal mortgage market. this requires sound lending practices, symmetrical relationships between parties and good consumer information; those conditions are also necessary to promote financial inclusion and ensure a high level of consumer protection. our objective should therefore be to achieve a sustainable internal market in mortgage lending.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on greenhouse gas emission allowances. as we know, the ets, the union's emissions trading system, is an essential tool in the policy of combating greenhouse gas emissions for the european union. but following the economic crisis, we saw that the ets had some dysfunctions, including undervaluing the carbon price, which did not allow the necessary investments in sustainable low-carbon technologies. the report therefore provides short- and medium-term solutions to address its weaknesses and to ensure that this leading instrument can properly fulfil its missions.
in writing. i welcome this report which aims to freeze the auctioning of 900 million allowances in the coming years. due to a growing surplus of emission allowances on the market, the price of co2 emission permits has become so low that companies have little incentive to emit less greenhouse gases. the measures proposed in this report should raise the price of co2 emission allowances to a level that provides sufficient incentives for european industries to pollute less and invest more in low-carbon innovation, which will reduce greenhouse gas emissions and combat climate change. i am glad that the commission can adapt the auction timetable in exceptional circumstances.
in writing. − the cornerstone of european climate policy has been threatened for months by an overabundance of co2 rights. co2 trading should reward sustainable innovation, green energy and industry leaders. unfortunately, this is not the case now, because the cost of a ton of co2 emissions is now about the same as that of a hamburger. this extremely low carbon price does not discourage pollution and does not discourage investment in a green economy. these investments are needed to create jobs and to combat climate change. in addition, companies that have anticipated the ets in time and invested in greening are not rewarded for this and polluting operators can continue with impunity. the adoption today of the groote report on backloading will ensure that the auctioning of 900 million co2 allowances is postponed in order to reduce the surplus of co2 allowances and to buy time to further address the weaknesses of the system. this is a first provisional step to redress the excesses of the emissions trading system and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. the objective of this report is to clarify the legislative provisions relating to the auctioning schedule for allowances set out in directive 2003/87/ec. it seems to me that the commission should be able to adapt the auction schedule adopted in accordance with article 10 (4) of directive 2003/87/ec. however, such measures should only be taken in exceptional circumstances, such as those faced by the etuc at present. in addition, in order not to jeopardise the stability and predictability of the ems, i propose that the decision to adapt the auction timetable be taken only once during the third phase of the ems. in this respect, this short-term measure proposal should not be seen as a remedy for the current imbalances but rather as a means of ensuring the stability of the ems pending the adoption of long-term structural measures.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, having worked on the new budgetary framework and in the committee on employment and social affairs, i had great fears about the future of this globalisation adjustment fund. tomorrow, it's extended and we're going back a long way. the firm negotiations conducted by our rapporteur - whom i commend for her work - and our committee chairman, the fictitious rapporteurs, as well as some of our allies among the negotiators in the council, and with the help of the commission, have ensured the sustainability of the fund, one of the few european supports for workers. the fund has not only been maintained but has also been strengthened to make it more effective, with the reintroduction of the 'crisis' criterion, which makes it possible to meet the reality of our restructuring; with all types of contracts now covered, helping more workers; the co-financing rate was increased to 60%; with young people in disaster areas who may be assisted by the fund; the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. but we're not happy with everything. first, the financial resources for the egf should be significantly increased to meet the needs. secondly, the fund should be able to play a real role in the restructuring process in the future, so as to become an anticipatory tool for monitoring restructuring and helping the process of redeploying workers and thus preventing such redundancies. i am convinced that with this new regulation we are strengthening solidarity between europeans.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, first of all i want to thank all the colleagues – and especially mr swoboda – who are very interested in the democratic choice we have in the liberal group. obviously it is because it is only in the liberal group that there is a democratic choice that everybody is interested in it! besides that i want start my intervention by paying tribute to the citizens of ukraine. i do that because the hundreds of thousands of people in the streets of kiev are in my opinion today the best answer we can give to the rising eurosceptic sentiment in europe today. inside europe, nationalists and populists try to explain to us that it is over with europe, that there is no future for the european union and yet you see, outside our union, in the streets of kiev, people who want to join europe, want to join the european union. my hope is that this pro-european spirit will not only prevail in the streets of kiev next week, but also in next week’s european council. it will be necessary because it is not an ordinary european council. we have in fact three decisive hurdles to overcome in this european council, six months before our european elections. the first is on european defence: it is exactly 60 years ago that the french national assembly made in my opinion a huge mistake, in 1954 if you remember – i was just born one year before, so i do not remember myself – to reject the european defence community. nevertheless we see that, if you carry out a poll in europe, in all the member states of the european union public opinion is in favour of european defence – a majority in favour of european defence, even in the united kingdom. if there is one issue in the uk that they think we have to do together it is about european defence. i know, some were laughing ten years ago when in the aftermath of the iraq war we organised with france and with germany what they called afterwards the chocolate summit. the idea at that time was to build on european defence, based on the st malo agreement between france and great britain. i can only hope that ten years later this idea can blossom again, because certainly in terms of austerity where all the member states have enormous difficulties with their public finances, we do not have the luxury to do the same thing 28 times, and it is far better to cooperate in that matter. the second decisive step we need in this european council is the new economic governance architecture for the eurozone. let me be very blunt about that, commissioner. you have defended here the contractual arrangements, but this parliament does not want this idea of contractual arrangements: the idea that between the commission and a member state we should make a contract in which a specific reform – pension reform or labour market reform – is imposed. this system of contractual arrangements will be the death of europe if you continue with it. it would create resistance in every member state were you to make such a contractual arrangement, because it would be seen as an intrusion from europe in a specific national reform. we have said it already – mr brok, myself, mr gualtieri in the name of the parliament – in the sherpa meetings and you are simply continuing with the idea. the commission should defend another idea, the same idea as parliament, the idea of convergence guidelines. there need to be convergence directives that are applicable to all 28 member states of the union, and to all the 17 member states of the eurozone. naturally, these convergence guidelines will have different consequences in these and other member states with different reforms. please stop this idea of contractual arrangements; it gives the impression that the european union, and specifically the commission, is in fact intervening and imposing a special national reform while it is still member states who are responsible for that. finally, my third point is the banking union. let me first of all say what i have repeated already many times here in the plenary: without this banking union there is no solution to this crisis. we shall see exactly the same as what happened in japan: that is a long period of economic stagnation. we need a real banking union, not merely a banking union, not what i call a loose coordination of national resolution mechanisms. that will not work. we do not need an intergovernmental system, we need a community system. what i have read in the press this morning about the outcome of the ecofin meeting last night is again an intergovernmental system that this parliament hopefully will never accept. secondly, it has to be a system paid for not by taxpayers but by the banks themselves because, if it is again a system like the one we had in the past, it will be the taxpayers again who foot the bill. banks have to pay based on their risk profiles. i hope that in this parliament we can all give full support to the commission proposal that precisely corresponds to this. my conclusion: i hope that at next week’s ecofin meeting and certainly, commissioner, at next week’s european council, the same european spirit can prevail as the european spirit we see today in kiev on maidan square. answer is "blue cardboard". mr audy, i believe that european defence is an imperative because it is an area which the states can no longer finance in its present form. that's the reality. the reality is that european countries spend 42% of us spending on defence, which is a lot, because us military spending is huge. forty two percent! almost half. but we can only do 10% of the operations that the americans can do. this means, if you do a little calculation, that europe is four to five times less effective militarily than the americans. so it's clear we have to continue on the basis of saint-malo. saint-malo was an agreement between france and britain to launch the defense community. what i am proposing, and what we did with mr chirac at this summit ten years ago, is to go further on this point and to put an end to the idiotic idea that we must do the same thing 23 times in the field of european defence.
in writing. there is a lot of political commotion about the fact that on 1 january this year bulgarians and romanians will have free access to the labour market, on an equal footing with all eu citizens. many half-truths and fabrications are told about this. it is worth recalling that free movement within the eu is not unlimited, namely: eu citizens must prove that they are available for the labour market and their application for social assistance may be refused if it is found that they are unlawfully claiming it. some governments, particularly in london, seem to overlook these enforcement instruments and give the impression that the opening up of the labour market is a threat. the same governments are opposing the introduction of effective checks and inspections against the unlawful use of the posting of workers directive in the social affairs council. this is why the recent agreement on the enforcement directive is so important: it is clear that europe can indeed cope with the fraudulent structures of the crooked companies. the agreement is an important step towards fair competition and humane working conditions for posted workers. such concrete decisions will help to convince the citizens that european cooperation is a good thing for all of us.
in writing. the threat of counterfeiting the euro is international in scope. our currency remains a prime target for counterfeiters. it is imperative that member states cooperate with each other in order to deal with this phenomenon. i therefore welcome the report by anthea mcintyre which sets out an action programme on trade, assistance and training for the protection and safeguarding of the euro against counterfeiting. this cooperation should increase the efficiency of operations through the sharing of best practices, common standards and joint specialised training.
in writing. counterfeiting of the euro is a serious criminal offence and its links with organised crime should be taken into account when assessing the economic and social impact of counterfeiting on the lives of citizens. large-scale counterfeiting can harm the european economy and the stability of the currency itself. however, the euro is not counterfeited on a large scale. it is largely protected by its design and by the structures responsible at national and european level for monitoring and combating counterfeiting. the pericles programme has played an important role in this action to date. this long-standing programme has done a valuable service in disseminating best practice in the fight against counterfeiting and has thus contributed to the protection of the financial interests of the union. the commission proposal is still too vague in some respects, however, and this report aims to supplement the text presented by providing details to optimise the use of the funds allocated to the programme. i therefore voted in favour of the text.

in writing. the european parliament has adopted a resolution on the situation in the european union. the european parliament recently noted that europe today has about 880 000 modern slaves. to reduce this alarming figure, the fight for decent living and working conditions for domestic workers, one of the most vulnerable professions, must of course be a priority. the ilo convention guarantees domestic workers the same fundamental rights as other workers and obliges signatory countries to eliminate forced and child labour. it is now up to all the european member states to ratify the ilo convention as soon as possible and to put an end to the unacceptable conditions which we are still facing in europe today.
in writing. i welcome the report on the draft council decision authorising member states to ratify, in the interest of the eu, the 2011 ilo convention on decent work for domestic workers (convention no 189). this convention is intended to improve the situation of these people, to give value to their work and to recognise the importance they have in the national economy. more legislation on this type of work, often informal, would help to combat forced labour, child labour, discrimination, etc. these workers will have the opportunity to learn about working conditions, which are generally ignored because there is often no written contract between the employer and the worker. the convention should, above all, improve the situation of migrant women, who are particularly vulnerable.
in writing. i voted in favour of this convention, which has the main objective of enhancing the value of domestic workers by setting out the following guarantees: recognition of the significant contribution of domestic workers to the world economy; recognition of the fact that domestic work is undervalued and invisible and is mainly carried out by women and girls, many of whom are migrants or belong to disadvantaged communities and are therefore in a highly vulnerable situation; 'domestic worker' means any person who performs domestic work in the context of an employment relationship.

in writing. after the text has been corrected, we have voted as follows: preserving peace, preventing conflict, strengthening international security, assisting people, countries and regions facing natural or man-made disasters, and promoting the sustainable economic, social and environmental development of these countries, with the essential aim of eradicating poverty, are among the principles and primary objectives of the union's external action within the meaning of article 21 of the treaty on european union. crises and conflicts affecting countries around the world and other factors such as challenges and threats related to terrorism, organised crime, climate change and cybersecurity, as well as natural disasters, pose a threat to global stability and security. to solve these problems in an effective and timely manner, specific financial resources and financing instruments are needed to complement humanitarian aid and long-term cooperation instruments.
in writing. a number of important developments have occurred since the launch of the european neighbourhood policy and the creation of the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument. these developments include deepening relations with partners, the establishment of regional initiatives and the establishment of democratic transition processes in the eastern partnership countries and, in particular, in the countries of the southern mediterranean after the events of spring 2011. this led to a new approach to the european neighbourhood policy, which was defined in 2011 following a comprehensive strategic review of the policy. it highlights key objectives promoting cooperation and sustained support for partners committed to building a fairer, more democratic society that respects human rights and freedoms, in accordance with the principles of differentiation ('more for more') and mutual accountability.
in writing. i am of the opinion that a european state which has applied for membership of the union can only become a member when it has been confirmed that it fulfils the criteria for membership laid down at the copenhagen european council in june 1993 and provided that the accession does not exceed the limits of the union's capacity to integrate the new member. these criteria relate to the stability of institutions guaranteeing democracy, the rule of law, respect for human rights and non-discrimination and respect for and protection of minorities and vulnerable groups, the development of the economy which must be sufficient to withstand the pressure of competition in the internal market, and the capacity to assume not only the rights but also the obligations arising from the application of the treaties.
in writing. this draft regulation is one of the elements of the european union's external policy. it is innovative and different from the instruments developed to promote the union's external development. it aims at partnership and cooperation between the union and, in particular, those countries which have succeeded in doing without development aid and become economic partners of interest to the union, such as china, russia, latin america, etc. it aims to promote the union's interests and address key global challenges, in line with the europe 2020 strategy. this instrument has a limited budget of eur 1 131 000 000 for the period 2014-2020. therefore, the objectives, sectors and countries targeted must be carefully determined, and the coordination mechanisms already provided for in this regulation must be adapted to the specific needs of the member states.
in writing. i would like to stress the need for easier access to funding for eidhr beneficiaries. simplifying and speeding up the procedure while reducing the administrative burden would be one way of achieving this objective. in this context, the set of proposals for external action presented by the commission is a step in the right direction, as it contains simplification elements subjecting all the union's external action instruments to the provisions of the general regulation, providing for more flexible procedures for emergency situations, with the possibility of taking ad hoc measures in the form of direct or small grants in cases of human rights violations and to ensure coherence with the financial regulation.
in writing. on 7 december 2011, the european commission presented its proposal for a financing instrument for development cooperation, thus initiating the procedure that will establish a new legal basis for the union's development policies. this proposal introduced several new features. perhaps the most important element is differentiation, i.e. the distinction between the least developed countries and those that have entered the upper middle income countries. equally important is the reduction in the number of thematic programmes from five to two, which makes it possible to lighten the body of the text, while using annexes to specify the priorities of the geographical and thematic programmes. simplification is another objective of the proposal, in line with the general objective of alignment with the policies of the partner countries. country strategy papers will no longer be necessary if the partner country has its own development plan. we share the principles and objectives set out by the commission in its proposal, but we have suggested several amendments, many of which reflect priorities already expressed by parliament with regard to the future development policy of the union and its implementation.
in writing. - in my own region, limburg, we are currently experiencing the disastrous and profound effects that major restructuring at multinational companies can have on workers and their families, with the closure of the ford plant in genk. the blow is not just to the ford plant itself, but to the many local smes in the supply chain. directly and indirectly, almost 10 000 jobs are at stake. the european globalisation adjustment fund is a real opportunity for europe to make a difference in such a situation. because the globalisation fund is not just a compensation fund. the financial support is intended to open up new prospects for the workers concerned and thus for the whole region. this is a well-trained and motivated workforce, which, with appropriate guidance and retraining, can seize new opportunities. it is therefore also positive that the new fund also provides support for young people and encourages entrepreneurship, by supporting employees in the takeover of bankrupt but viable companies. it is a pity that the egf was rather tightly budgeted. the annual budget of eur 150 million must now be used all the more efficiently, with a minimum of red tape, to help the affected workers get back to work as quickly as possible.
in writing. i would like to commend the work of frédéric daerden in this area. the eu must get back on the path to growth with a dynamic job creation programme, otherwise growth could happen without job creation. the egf may help to achieve these objectives by supporting redundant workers who are looking for a job, want to upskill or retrain or want to set up as self-employed in line with the europe 2020 strategy. the evaluation of the fund reported a reintegration rate of 48.1%, and in most cases this rate increased in the medium term. it also indicated that the egf had supported some of the groups of workers who were most difficult to help. in addition, it reported that many beneficiaries had regained their self-confidence and renewed and improved their job search skills, as well as other skills and abilities; similarly, although not all beneficiaries were able to find employment, the fund's assistance improved their employability.
in writing. tax fraud and tax evasion affect all member states of the european union without exception. this is why i welcome this report, which requires member states to collect and share data in the tax area by 2017. this cooperation between states will strengthen the internal market through effective tax systems and improve the fight against tax evasion and tax avoidance.
in writing. this proposal, together with the savings directive and the administrative cooperation directive, which it proposes to amend, means that member states will share as much information with each other as they have committed to do with the united states under the us foreign account tax compliance act (fatca). i support the commission's proposal and believe that it is in line with both the commission's action plan against tax fraud and tax evasion and the position of the european parliament expressed in its own-initiative report on the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens. in times of crisis, when european citizens are faced with rising taxes, there is an urgent need to tackle the problems of tax fraud and tax evasion, which cause an estimated €1 trillion in losses per year, representing an average cost of €2 000 per year for each european citizen.
in writing. the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to replace national notification and authorisation procedures for carriers of radioactive materials by a single registration system. the implementation of the regulation should simplify procedures and reduce administrative burdens, while maintaining a high level of radiation protection. the replacement of these national reporting and authorisation procedures by a single registration system for transport practice will therefore help to simplify procedures, reduce administrative burden, remove barriers to entry, while maintaining the high levels of radiation protection achieved.
in writing. this excellent report underlines the need to put human rights at the heart of the european union's relations with all third countries and to avoid a double standard in its external policy. like the report, i call on the eu foreign affairs council to adopt conclusions on human rights in order to establish a common threshold of minimum requirements in this area. in addition, the union must provide full support to countries in a democratic transition and to their populations in order to assist them in ensuring a more solid transition with concrete guarantees of non-return. however, i remain firm on the question of morocco and western sahara. finally, i would stress the need for the european union to ensure that these same rights are strictly respected within its territory through monitoring mechanisms.

in writing. i had to abstain on this file because the means in place could have been counterproductive. i wanted to express my concern about the situation of sme lending in europe. as the crisis deepens, lending to the real economy continues to decline and become more expensive, not because of the financial situation of the smes concerned, but because of their location within the euro area. this situation must be remedied, because the monetary policy transmission mechanism is de facto broken. another distortion is created by the fact that some banks receiving state aid use this money to buy more sovereign debt while at the same time reducing lending to smes and households.
in writing. the european dairy sector will be profoundly transformed after the expiry of quotas in 2015. for the first time in 31 years, the sector will no longer have milk quotas. this major change is likely to disrupt the market in the dairy sector, particularly in the less-favoured areas and the outermost regions. in these areas, dairy production is often the only source of income and the local community is heavily dependent on the dairy sector. to ensure a stable future for the sector and to avoid the depopulation of rural areas, with the negative economic and environmental consequences that this entails, additional measures are needed at european level. it is vital to continue monitoring the consequences of the abolition of quotas, particularly in the less favoured and outermost regions. the present ini report therefore focuses mainly on these particularly vulnerable regions in order to guarantee farmers a decent livelihood and to ensure the future of rural areas, especially as the cap reform did not address this issue.
in writing. the world will experience more and more natural disasters due to climate change, population growth and countries in conflict. since 1992, 4.4 billion people have been affected by disasters and in 2011 the losses due to these disasters amounted to over 300 billion dollars. it is important to prevent as much as possible in the future in order to reduce losses. i therefore welcome this report which stresses the need for resilience measures in our humanitarian and development aid policies. we need to put in place frameworks that allow for the immediate mobilisation of all available resources, which will allow for more efficient management of the responses provided. it is also important to target the most vulnerable countries and populations. we should be the voice of these populations to enable them to adapt. people are not equal in the face of disasters, we must help the most deprived populations.
in writing. i agree with the rapporteur. the report calls for a strong integration of resilience measures into humanitarian and development programmes in order to significantly advance the resilience approach. it also recognises the challenges posed by climate change and stresses that adaptation to climate change requires consideration of resilience and cpr initiatives.
in writing. i welcome the own-initiative report by angelika werthmann on women with disabilities. women and girls with disabilities represent 16% of the total female population in the union. these women are unfortunately disadvantaged in many areas such as housing, health, public transport, education, employment etc. it is therefore our duty to respond strongly with strategies, legislation and policies to ensure non-discrimination and equal opportunities for all these women and girls with disabilities. it is also important to provide additional support during pregnancy and childcare, especially if they have a mental illness.
in writing. women with disabilities are not only people who are unable to perform specific tasks, they are first and foremost women, human beings. when we talk about them, we must bear in mind that we are talking about citizens and that they cannot be defined by their disability. in fact, they don't want to. every day they face the same challenges and opportunities as other women; they are friends, daughters, mothers, wives and employees. they take on different roles, like all women. we are taking up the challenge of including women with disabilities in society and enabling them to participate on an equal footing. disabled people account for 15% of the european population; one in four europeans has a disabled family member. these figures illustrate the importance of responding to our high expectations and creating a friendly environment for all eu citizens on an equal footing.

in writing. retail trade is of great economic importance, accounting for 11% of gdp at european level and 15% of employment in the union. the european union has placed particular emphasis on retail trade, which is one of the main pillars of the single market. for large retailers, the potential economies of scale in an efficient internal market can be a clear advantage. it is therefore regrettable that many retailers wishing to operate in several or all member states still face unnecessary obstacles, such as different packaging and labelling requirements and differences in administrative practices. the social value of retail is as important as its economic value. the number of opportunities for real-life social interactions is rapidly decreasing, particularly with the ever-increasing importance of the internet in everyday life and the computerization of our societies in general.

i should like to begin by saying, mr president, that it has been clear for over a year now that every year all the public authorities in europe are losing as much as 1 000 billion euros in tax evasion and tax fraud. that is some 2 000 euros per european per year, at a time when in many countries ordinary people are paying the price every day of the crisis into which the failure of the banking system has plunged us. of course, there has been talk for some time that there is some sort of momentum to finally join hands and do something about this. but it can't be just words. between saying and doing, between rhetoric and real action, there is of course a wide gap, the tax gap. we're not gonna close it just by measuring her. the introduction of a measuring instrument is of course a useful thing. but we need to be more ambitious. a few years ago, we introduced the concept of bazooka as a bullet to bail out banks. now, tax evasion and tax avoidance also require a strong approach. the report by mr kleva, which we adopted some time ago, already contained some excellent ideas. we must therefore set binding targets in each member state to reduce the abuse, we must revoke the licences of banks, advisers, lawyers who collaborate in fraudulent structures; they should also be prosecuted. it is also necessary to work towards a serious harmonization of the common tax base for taxes, to define clearly what tax havens are and to prohibit cooperation with them. in short, this must now finally be made a priority. i think the people, the general public, will support you in this.
in writing. one trillion euros are annually withheld from tax revenues. this increases the level of government debt, destroys the possibility of fair competition between honest and fraudulent companies: the fraud of the big ones makes the small ones pay! these frauds shift the tax burden onto workers and low- and middle-income households. in addition, they force the public authorities to make cuts in public services. this is unacceptable. the consequences are even more pronounced in countries where the socioeconomic situation is dire. in greece, for example, large companies have transferred €60 billion out of the country since 1 january 2012 in order to benefit from tax breaks. the total cost of tax fraud is higher than the combined health budgets of the union. stopping tax evasion would wipe out all the deficits in just nine years. we must act! a coherent, concrete and common european taxation strategy and binding measures are essential. finally, we must fight for greater transparency and strict controls to prevent the eu institutions, bodies and agencies from resorting to 'tax havens'!

in writing. in times of economic crisis, when unemployment is high, energy prices are rising, raw materials are becoming scarce and dependence on imports is increasing, sustained economic growth coupled with improved employment is essential to ensure social cohesion. innovation is one of the keys to achieving this and should therefore be encouraged. this is achieved through eco-innovation, a concept combining environmental protection, growth, competitiveness and job creation. green innovations are essential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, to use resources such as water and raw materials more efficiently, to promote greater use of recycled materials and to produce quality products with a lower environmental impact, and to develop more environmentally friendly production processes and services. eco-innovation can take many forms, from a new water filter to clean waste water, to thinner, stronger steel to reduce the consumption of raw materials, to a new business model to sell repair services rather than products.

in writing. the commission, as a result of the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty and the subsequent regulation (eu) no 182/2011 (on implementing powers), had to adapt the rules for decisions on trade policy to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts. the commission has therefore put forward two proposals for alignment, known as omnibus i and omnibus ii, each of which brings together in a single instrument the trade regulations to be updated; omnibus i deals mainly with implementing acts and omnibus ii deals with delegated acts. omnibus ii makes the necessary amendments to the previous texts, which previously referred to the old comitology decision 1999/468/ec. in view of these factors, we approved, without amendment, the council's position at first reading and the joint declaration of parliament, the council and the commission on regulation (eec) no 3030/93 and regulation (ec) no 517/94. it also recommended that parliament take note of the commission's statements on codification and delegated acts. the three declarations will be published together with the final legislative act.

in writing. the european parliament voted on a proposal for a directive establishing a framework for maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal management. i voted against the proposal, not because i am not in favour of integrated coastal management, but on the contrary. i am not at all convinced, however, that we need a european directive for this. in may 2013, the flemish parliament adopted a reasoned subsidy opinion, in which it considered that the commission proposal was contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. flanders is not alone in its concern: parliamentary committees in germany, sweden, the netherlands and poland have also raised a subsidiarity objection. but it is not enough to give the commission a yellow card and ask it to reconsider the proposal. in the same vein, i have tried to amend the commission's proposal in the committee on the environment, but to no avail. the proposal before us today does indeed provide for more flexibility. the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. i hope that during the negotiations between parliament and the council the proposal will still develop in the right direction.
in writing. it is very important to ensure that this framework directive is in line with the principle of subsidiarity and leaves member states a margin of manoeuvre to effectively integrate their particular interests and specificities at national, regional or local level. in particular, the coastline is an area with various characteristics which may warrant different approaches to address its specific characteristics effectively. therefore, a framework directive on maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal zone management should leave member states the flexibility to act effectively within a framework of common objectives. this directive should neither hinder the development of maritime spatial planning programmes nor interfere with formal and informal good practices of integrated coastal zone management. i strongly support a framework of procedures to achieve coherent and coordinated maritime spatial planning in all the member states of the union. i would like to stress in particular the importance of crossborder cooperation between member states and third countries. marine basins, marine waters and ecosystems do not know national boundaries and effective planning and management must therefore be implemented in a cross-border manner.

in writing. i support this resolution as i support the parliament's call for greater transparency and stronger controls to prevent the eu institutions, bodies and agencies, and their intermediaries, from using non-cooperative foreign countries and territories, commonly known as 'tax havens', which are characterised by the absence of taxes or by low taxes, the absence of effective exchange of information with foreign tax authorities and a lack of transparency in legislative, judicial or administrative provisions, or recognised as such by the oecd or the financial action task force.
author. - mr president, i would first like to pay tribute to the two french soldiers who died in the central african republic and tell you how much i regret today that, after more than a year of warning from mrs georgieva and the external action service, it has taken so long to get a resolution - resolution 2127 - at the united nations, which is certainly fundamental for finally getting something in motion to protect the central african republic. we knew and we know that there was a threat of genocide, with all the attendant atrocities. we knew, and yet it took a long time today for something to happen. i've heard things that are unacceptable to my group. i have heard people say, "yes, françafrique is rising again, etc"., about the french action. i would say that i am very measured in relation to military actions and interventions but this time france has only heard what so many people have told us for so long.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, organ harvesting always arouses rumours and fantasies, but it may also evoke a terrible reality. it is our duty, and it is our responsibility as members of parliament, to distinguish carefully between rumours and reality. the trade in organs is now one of the least regulated in the world. the demand is growing and far exceeds the supply, hence grey areas, without regulation, where all practices are possible without being illegal and, on the other hand, criminal practices also exist, combining human trafficking, adoption, kidnapping, etc. in some lands it is common to sell organs and to harvest them from living creatures for religious reasons, for example, because they cannot be harvested from the dead. this is the case in india where poor people sell corneas, kidneys, etc. but such practices are also found in latin america. in some cases, as in austria and belgium, it is legal to harvest organs from the dead, regardless of the cause of death, without consulting anyone. only four countries in africa have legislation on organ harvesting and only two in asia, sri lanka and indonesia. china is not a member of the wto and is therefore in a grey area. for our group, we have two certainties. the first is that china largely uses executed political prisoners for its organs. but i am like mr tannock, we are unable to say whether their execution is related to a need for organs or whether they were executed, and we are against the death penalty. we find no evidence of any particular persecution of falun gong, as evidenced by the detailed report of the new zealand house of representatives, which has extensively investigated this issue and which i put at your disposal. that is why, in our soul and conscience, our group has decided to abstain on this resolution. we have not signed the resolution but we are prepared to work with the council of europe on this matter, which is an extremely sensitive and extremely thorny matter. however, this must be done not in an emergency but in the conscience of parliamentarians.

mr president, in continuing with what i said earlier, i would like to add that china would have many opportunities to be on the emergency agenda. let's not misunderstand what i said earlier. however, whenever human rights are mentioned for some countries, it is for objective facts - today, for central africa, sri lanka - which are supported by crimes, but also supported by international organizations whose job it is to detect where there are human rights problems, whether it is human rights watch, the international federation for human rights, but also amnesty international and many others. we endorse, by holding a debate, this kind of reporting which is supported here - i repeat and regret it - by the presence of what i call a sect - falun gong. their presence in parliament for three days last week, handing out leaflets, is enough to establish an emergency, whereas, as véronique de keyser said, a report, notably from the new zealand assembly, among others, does not support the facts, does not necessarily give them credit. so i have my doubts as to why this urgency has come up in this debate today.
